question_text:
A company owns an asynchronous API that is used to ingest user requests and, based on the request type, dispatch requests to the appropriate microservice for processing. The company is using Amazon API Gateway to deploy the API front end, and an AWS Lambda function that invokes Amazon DynamoDB to store user requests before dispatching them to the processing microservices.
The company provisioned as much DynamoDB throughput as its budget allows, but the company is still experiencing availability issues and is losing user requests.
What should a solutions architect do to address this issue without impacting existing users?
explanation_en:
The amount of throughput in the table has been configured to the maximum budgeted value, but the request is still missing. This requires a buffer mechanism: one function places the request in the SQS queue, the other functions read the queue and write to DynamoDB at a controlled rate. Peaks are smoothed, no data are lost and no changes are detected by existing users.
Option A: The speed limit in API Gateway will discard some requests - that is, it turns data loss into a policy problem and affects users.
Option B: DAX accelerates reading, but does not buffer writing: writing problems still exist.
Option C: The secondary index adds another consumer who writes about throughput, which will only make the situation worse.

options.text: Add throttling on the API Gateway with server-side throttling limits.
Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.
Create a secondary index in DynamoDB for the table with the user requests.
Use the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and Lambda to buffer writes to DynamoDB.

question_text:
A company needs to move data from an Amazon EC2 instance to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must ensure that no API calls and no data are routed through public internet routes. Only the EC2 instance can have access to upload data to the S3 bucket.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
API calls and data are not allowed to be transmitted by public route, and only the example is allowed to be uploaded. The first requirement is met through the VPC terminal node, and the second requirement is met through the storage barrel strategy, which allows only role access to examples (and, if required, only through the terminal node). Key here selects the interface terminal node: it is created in a specific subnet to obtain a private IP address and to protect it through a security group. The difference with the gateway terminal node is that the gateway node works by route from the route list, has neither an IP address nor a security unit, and cannot be accessed from the local network - compared to questions 667, 471.
Option B: Description does not correspond to the mechanism: the gateway terminal node will not be placed in the available area, nor will it support the security group - it is only a route in the VPC route list.
Option C: S3 does not have a private IP address called "private bumpet IP address", which cannot be searched and set as a route through nslookup. Private addresses only appear with interface terminal nodes.
Option D:ip-ranges.json file contains the public IP range for AWS. The route leading to these ranges has no effect on the private conduct of the flow.

options.text: Create an interface VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the subnet where the EC2 instance is located. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.

Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the Availability Zone where the EC2 instance is located. Attach appropriate security groups to the endpoint. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.

Run the nslookup tool from inside the EC2 instance to obtain the private IP address of the S3 bucket’s service API endpoint. Create a route in the VPC route table to provide the EC2 instance with access to the S3 bucket. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.

Use the AWS provided, publicly available ip-ranges.json file to obtain the private IP address of the S3 bucket’s service API endpoint. Create a route in the VPC route table to provide the EC2 instance with access to the S3 bucket. Attach a resource policy to the S3 bucket to only allow the EC2 instance’s IAM role for access.

question_text:
A solutions architect is designing the architecture of a new application being deployed to the AWS Cloud. The application will run on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances and will automatically scale across multiple Availability Zones. The EC2 instances will scale up and down frequently throughout the day. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) will handle the load distribution. The architecture needs to support distributed session data management.
The company is willing to make changes to code if needed.
What should the solutions architect do to ensure that the architecture supports distributed session data management?
explanation_en:
Examples are often added and removed, so they cannot be kept in session status. ElastiCache moves words out of the external memory memory: any instance reads and writes the same data, the response time is in milliseconds and the code changes are allowed under the conditions described.
Option B: Session-relationship will fix the user on a specific instance, which will be lost when removed from the group.
Option C: Systems Manager's session manager is an example shell's administrator access -- it has nothing to do with application user sessions.
Option D: GetsessionToken will generate temporary AWS vouchers -- it does not store Web application sessions.

options.text: Use Amazon ElastiCache to manage and store session data.
Use session affinity (sticky sessions) of the ALB to manage session data.
Use Session Manager from AWS Systems Manager to manage the session.
Use the GetSessionToken API operation in AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to manage the session.

question_text:
A company offers a food delivery service that is growing rapidly. Because of the growth, the company’s order processing system is experiencing scaling problems during peak traffic hours. The current architecture includes the following:
• A group of Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to collect orders from the application
• Another group of EC2 instances that run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to fulfill orders The order collection process occurs quickly, but the order fulfillment process can take longer. Data must not be lost because of a scaling event.
A solutions architect must ensure that the order collection process and the order fulfillment process can both scale properly during peak traffic hours. The solution must optimize utilization of the company’s AWS resources.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
Order collection is fast and compliance is slow – so each stage needs to be decoupled through two queues and each line expanded independently to fit their loads. The appropriate indicator for the queue is the backlog for each instance: the number of messages in the queue divided by the number of consumers, which is maintained by automatic expansion groups. This will reflect the actual workload and will not result in the loss of data during the expansion.
Option A: Maintaining the minimum peak permanently would overpaid and CPU utilization would not reflect the volume of the backlog of orders.
Option B: Creating a new automatic extension group upon receiving a signal is a design that is not feasible and difficult to manage.
Option C: Queue selection is correct, but SQS does not send an extension notice -- you need an indicator based on the number of messages.

options.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to monitor the CPU of each instance in the Auto Scaling groups. Configure each Auto Scaling group’s minimum capacity according to peak workload values.

Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to monitor the CPU of each instance in the Auto Scaling groups. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to invoke an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that creates additional Auto Scaling groups on demand.

Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues: one for order collection and another for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queue. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on notifications that the queues send.

Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues: one for order collection and another for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queue. Create a metric based on a backlog per instance calculation. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on this metric.

question_text:
A company hosts multiple production applications. One of the applications consists of resources from Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, Amazon RDS, Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS), and Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) across multiple AWS Regions. All company resources are tagged with a tag name of “application” and a value that corresponds to each application. A solutions architect must provide the quickest solution for identifying all of the tagged components.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
Resources are marked and dispersed in multiple regions and in different services. The label editor in the AWS resource group can search by label in all regions and resource types at the same time, and generate an on-the-spot list of resources - the fastest way to do this without having to write codes.
Option A: CloudTrail displays API calls instead of the current list of resources with specific labels.
Option B: It is slow and laborious to rotate every service in each region through the command line interface.
Option C: Cloudwatch Logs Insights handles the log rather than the list of resources.

options.text: Use AWS CloudTrail to generate a list of resources with the application tag.
Use the AWS CLI to query each service across all Regions to report the tagged components.
Run a query in Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights to report on the components with the application tag.
Run a query with the AWS Resource Groups Tag Editor to report on the resources globally with the application tag.

question_text:
A company needs to export its database once a day to Amazon S3 for other teams to access. The exported object size varies between 2 GB and 5 GB. The S3 access pattern for the data is variable and changes rapidly. The data must be immediately available and must remain accessible for up to 3 months. The company needs the most cost-effective solution that will not increase retrieval time.
Which S3 storage class should the company use to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The key phrases are "variable and rapidly changing" and "no additional search time". The former meant that the type of visit could not be assumed manually; the latter excluded any option that could not be immediately returned to the object or charged a fee for the search. The smart stratification meets both conditions: objects move automatically between frequent and non-frequent access layers, with no cost of retrieval, and have the same access time at both levels. When the object size is 2-5 GB, it is large enough to make surveillance costs negligible.
Option B: Glacier Instant Retrieval can return to the object immediately, but will charge a clear search fee and require a minimum of 90 days of storage. The data have a life cycle of three months and the frequency of reading is unpredictable — both of which are detrimental to them.
Option C: S3 Standard is not able to optimise: you still have to pay the full cost while no one reads the exported data.
Option D: Standard-IA is designed for infrequent access. In the case of rapid changes in access patterns, the cost of searching and the minimum storage time of 30 days make it more expensive than the smart stratification.

options.text: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval
S3 Standard
S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)

question_text:
A company is developing a new mobile app. The company must implement proper traffic filtering to protect its Application Load Balancer (ALB) against common application-level attacks, such as cross-site scripting or SQL injection. The company has minimal infrastructure and operational staff. The company needs to reduce its share of the responsibility in managing, updating, and securing servers for its AWS environment.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Cross-site script attacks and SQL injections are applied-level attacks, while AWS WAF filters these attacks: attach a Web access control list (Web ACL) to the load balancer, activate the AWS managed rule group (including the Core Rulebook and the SQL database ruleset) and check the traffic before it reaches its application. AWS itself would update the management rules, so that even teams without dedicated administrators would not have to maintain their signatures manually — a requirement that directly met the requirement to reduce their share of responsibility.
Option B: Openly hosting static content in S3 does not relate to a filter attack and does not match the application scenario located behind the load balancer.
Option C: Shield Advanced is used against DDoS attacks, but HTTP requests will not be checked to detect injection attempts.
Option D: The deployment of third-party firewalls on an example is a server that requires patching and maintenance, contrary to requirements.

options.text: Configure AWS WAF rules and associate them with the ALB.
Deploy the application using Amazon S3 with public hosting enabled.
Deploy AWS Shield Advanced and add the ALB as a protected resource.
Create a new ALB that directs traffic to an Amazon EC2 instance running a third-party firewall, which then passes the traffic to the current ALB.

question_text:
A company’s reporting system delivers hundreds of .csv files to an Amazon S3 bucket each day. The company must convert these files to Apache Parquet format and must store the files in a transformed data bucket.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
explanation_en:
Use the minimum development work to convert the format to AWS Gloe. The reptile determines the structure of the CSV file and creates a table in the data directory, while an ETL operation with an built-in conversion function writes the results to the target S3 bucket in Parquet format. There is little need for code writing or for infrastructure management.
Option A: An EMR cluster and a Spark application imply a need for development work and cluster management.
Option C: A Bash script needs to be created from the top to convert to Parquet, and AWS Watch will add an additional environment configuration.
Option D: The Lambda function needs to prepare its own conversion code, and a large file may not be completed within time or memory limits.

options.text: Create an Amazon EMR cluster with Apache Spark installed. Write a Spark application to transform the data. Use EMR File System (EMRFS) to write files to the transformed data bucket.
Create an AWS Glue crawler to discover the data. Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to transform the data. Specify the transformed data bucket in the output step.

Use AWS Batch to create a job definition with Bash syntax to transform the data and output the data to the transformed data bucket. Use the job definition to submit a job. Specify an array job as the job type.

Create an AWS Lambda function to transform the data and output the data to the transformed data bucket. Configure an event notification for the S3 bucket. Specify the Lambda function as the destination for the event notification.

question_text:
A company has 700 TB of backup data stored in network attached storage (NAS) in its data center. This backup data need to be accessible for infrequent regulatory requests and must be retained 7 years. The company has decided to migrate this backup data from its data center to AWS. The migration must be complete within 1 month.
The company has 500 Mbps of dedicated bandwidth on its public internet connection available for data transfer.
What should a solutions architect do to migrate and store the data at the LOWEST cost?
explanation_en:
First check time: 700 TB takes about four months of continuous transmission at 500 Mbps, and the deadline is one month. This excludes the network link, so the data is physically transmitted through Snowball equipment. It is the cheapest to store seven years of requested copies in the S3 Glacier Deep Archive, which is achieved by converting objects to this storage category through life cycle rules.
Option B: A VPN runs on the same Internet connection: cannot meet the deadline within one month.
Option C: A 500 Mbps Direct Connect connection provides the same bandwidth as the existing Internet connection, plus the time required for physical configuration - usually weeks. This cannot be done in one month.
Option D: DataSync is a good tool, but it is limited to the same bandwidth and cannot be uploaded directly to the Glacier storage category: data will first enter S3.

options.text: Order AWS Snowball devices to transfer the data. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
Deploy a VPN connection between the data center and Amazon VPC. Use the AWS CLI to copy the data from on premises to Amazon S3 Glacier.
Provision a 500 Mbps AWS Direct Connect connection and transfer the data to Amazon S3. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data and deploy a DataSync agent on premises. Use the DataSync task to copy files from the on-premises NAS storage to Amazon S3 Glacier.

question_text:
A company has a serverless website with millions of objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uses the S3 bucket as the origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. The company did not set encryption on the S3 bucket before the objects were loaded. A solutions architect needs to enable encryption for all existing objects and for all objects that are added to the S3 bucket in the future.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?
explanation_en:
The task is divided into two parts: new objects and millions of objects that already exist. For new objects, just use the default encryption on the S3 bucket -- then S3 encrypts all the objects that arrive. For an existing object, a batch rewriting is required: S3 Inventory produces a report listing the object and its encryption status, and S3 Watch Operations runs a copy of the report to re-write each encrypted object. All of this is done by management tools — no downloads, no custom codes.
Option A: Downloading and uploading millions of objects through local storage creates a two-way flow, time-consuming and high-risk error — this is precisely what the title calls for to avoid as a "minimum effort".
Option C: Only the default encryption is enabled to affect only new objects, and version control is irrelevant to encryption. Millions of objects that have been uploaded remain unencrypted.
Option D: Currently, there is no console operation to encrypt the selected object in bulk, and manual handling of millions of objects is physically impossible.

options.text: Create a new S3 bucket. Turn on the default encryption settings for the new S3 bucket. Download all existing objects to temporary local storage. Upload the objects to the new S3 bucket.

Turn on the default encryption settings for the S3 bucket. Use the S3 Inventory feature to create a .csv file that lists the unencrypted objects. Run an S3 Batch Operations job that uses the copy command to encrypt those objects.

Create a new encryption key by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Change the settings on the S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). Turn on versioning for the S3 bucket.

Navigate to Amazon S3 in the AWS Management Console. Browse the S3 bucket’s objects. Sort by the encryption field. Select each unencrypted object. Use the Modify button to apply default encryption settings to every unencrypted object in the S3 bucket.

question_text:
A company runs a global web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application stores data in Amazon Aurora. The company needs to create a disaster recovery solution and can tolerate up to 30 minutes of downtime and potential data loss. The solution does not need to handle the load when the primary infrastructure is healthy.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
A maximum acceptable 30-minute shutdown time and partial data loss, and the back-up site does not have to handle loads - this is described as an active-passive failure switch for a ignition or temperature-ready design. Deployment of a minimal infrastructure in the reserve area, data are synchronized through cross-regional Aurora copy (which can be upgraded to the main node), and when the main site fails, Route 53 switch the flow to the back-up site in conjunction with a health check. The design is cheaper than an active-active model and meets the stated RTO and RPO requirements.
Option B: Active-active configuration means that the back-up site always handles part of the flow, and the need is clear that this is not necessary. This would entail unnecessary costs.
Option C: Active-active models that run complete copies are more costly and restore the database from the latest snapshot will result in RPOs that are worse than copies.
Option D: Deployment of the infrastructure from the backup only after a disaster has occurred cannot be completed in 30 minutes, and the setting of a "second main instance of Aurora" in another region describes a global database, not what is required here.

options.text: Deploy the application with the required infrastructure elements in place. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora Replica in a second AWS Region.
Host a scaled-down deployment of the application in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-active failover. Create an Aurora Replica in the second Region.
Replicate the primary infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active- active failover. Create an Aurora database that is restored from the latest snapshot.

Back up data with AWS Backup. Use the backup to create the required infrastructure in a second AWS Region. Use Amazon Route 53 to configure active-passive failover. Create an Aurora second primary instance in the second Region.

question_text:
A company has a web server running on an Amazon EC2 instance in a public subnet with an Elastic IP address. The default security group is assigned to the EC2 instance. The default network ACL has been modified to block all traffic. A solutions architect needs to make the web server accessible from everywhere on port 443.
Which combination of steps will accomplish this task? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
It involves two layers of filtering. The safety group is state-aware, so only one entry rule (A) allowing a port of 443 from any source is required. The Network Access Control List (ACL) is non-state, and therefore two rules are required: the port entry rule for port 443 and the exit rule for temporary port range 32768-65535, as the client's response is sent (E).
Option B: There is no need to configure out-of-station security group rules for access: the response will leave automatically.
Option C: The only stop-in rule in the Network ACL is not sufficient to satisfy the demand: the response is stopped when you leave.
Option D: Allow port 443 outflows to be meaningless: Web server responses are sent from temporary ports, not from port 443.

options.text: Create a security group with a rule to allow TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0.
Create a security group with a rule to allow TCP port 443 to destination 0.0.0.0/0.
Update the network ACL to allow TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0.
Update the network ACL to allow inbound/outbound TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0 and to destination 0.0.0.0/0.
Update the network ACL to allow inbound TCP port 443 from source 0.0.0.0/0 and outbound TCP port 32768- 65535 to destination 0.0.0.0/0.

question_text:
A company’s application is having performance issues. The application is stateful and needs to complete in-memory tasks on Amazon EC2 instances. The company used AWS CloudFormation to deploy infrastructure and used the M5 EC2 instance family. As traffic increased, the application performance degraded. Users are reporting delays when the users attempt to access the application.
Which solution will resolve these issues in the MOST operationally efficient way?
explanation_en:
The application performed the tasks in memory, so the bottleneck was RAM, and the generic M5 series did not match this feature. The example was replaced with R5, which is an example of memory optimization, and the change operation was completed in the CloudFormation template for the deployment of infrastructure. For future capacity planning, Cloudwatch agents have been installed to collect a custom application delay indicator - EC2 does not itself have built-in memory or delay indicators.
Option A: The T3 example has a sudden performance but a limited performance budget: they perform worse under the ongoing memory-intensive load and changes made outside the template lead to configuration drift.
Option B: Manual volume adjustment is not an operational efficiency exercise and the type of example is not suitable for the load.
Option C: The type of instance is selected correctly, but EC2 does not have built-in memory indicators — only agents can provide them.

options.text: Replace the EC2 instances with T3 EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group. Make the changes by using the AWS Management Console.

Modify the CloudFormation templates to run the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Increase the desired capacity and the maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group manually when an increase is necessary.

Modify the CloudFormation templates. Replace the EC2 instances with R5 EC2 instances. Use Amazon CloudWatch built-in EC2 memory metrics to track the application performance for future capacity planning.

Modify the CloudFormation templates. Replace the EC2 instances with R5 EC2 instances. Deploy the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to generate custom application latency metrics for future capacity planning.

question_text:
A solutions architect is designing a new API using Amazon API Gateway that will receive requests from users. The volume of requests is highly variable; several hours can pass without receiving a single request. The data processing will take place asynchronously, but should be completed within a few seconds after a request is made.
Which compute service should the solutions architect have the API invoke to deliver the requirements at the lowest cost?
explanation_en:
Requests are rare and uneven and are processed for only a few seconds. The Lambda function is only charged on the actual time of execution and therefore does not incur costs during idle hours and can be extended instantaneously. This is the cheapest way to provide this mode of traffic.
Option A: An AWS Glue operation is designed for batch processing of data, with significant delay in start-up, and is charged at a minimum duration increment.
Option C: An EKS cluster will continuously charge, including control of flat costs, even if not requested.
Option D: EC2 instances located behind ECS will continue to run and will continue to charge regardless of the amount requested.

options.text: An AWS Glue job
An AWS Lambda function
A containerized service hosted in Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
A containerized service hosted in Amazon ECS with Amazon EC2

question_text:
A company runs an application on a group of Amazon Linux EC2 instances. For compliance reasons, the company must retain all application log files for 7 years. The log files will be analyzed by a reporting tool that must be able to access all the files concurrently.
Which storage solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Logs must be kept for seven years and be available for reporting and reading. S3 The cost per gigabytes is lower than any block or file storage, supports any quantity and reads it, and life-cycle rules allow older logs to move to cheaper storage categories. The example simply uploads the file to the S3 bucket.
Option A: An EBS volume bound to a usable area and an example is more expensive per gigabyte and cannot be available and accessed with the reporting tool.
Option B: EFS does provide simultaneous access, but the cost of storage is significantly higher per gigabyte than S3, which is a determining factor for seven years of archiving.
Option C: Examples stored data disappears when the example is closed: To meet the seven-year reservation requirement, it is simply impossible to use instances stored.

options.text: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
Amazon EC2 instance store
Amazon S3

question_text:
A company has hired an external vendor to perform work in the company’s AWS account. The vendor uses an automated tool that is hosted in an AWS account that the vendor owns. The vendor does not have IAM access to the company’s AWS account.
How should a solutions architect grant this access to the vendor?
explanation_en:
An external supplier does not need a certificate in your account - it only needs to be able to perform the operation in your role. You create a role in an account with the required strategy, which allows the subject from the supplier account to assume that role. The supplier's tool calls AssumeRole and obtains temporary vouchers. On that basis, it is a good practice to use external IDs in the terms of a confidence strategy: it prevents confusion of agency issues when suppliers serve multiple clients.
Option B: An IAM user with a password is a long-term certificate, which is distributed externally to your account - you must cancel them manually.
Option C: Users from different accounts cannot be added to the IAM group: the group is valid only in its own account.
Option D: IAM does not have an "AWS account" identity provider type: it is configured with SAML and OIDC. Cross-account access is achieved through role and trust strategies.

options.text: Create an IAM role in the company’s account to delegate access to the vendor’s IAM role. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the role for the permissions that the vendor requires.

Create an IAM user in the company’s account with a password that meets the password complexity requirements. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.

Create an IAM group in the company’s account. Add the tool’s IAM user from the vendor account to the group. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the group for the permissions that the vendor requires.

Create a new identity provider by choosing “AWS account” as the provider type in the IAM console. Supply the vendor’s AWS account ID and user name. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the new provider for the permissions that the vendor requires.

question_text:
A company has deployed a Java Spring Boot application as a pod that runs on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) in private subnets. The application needs to write data to an Amazon DynamoDB table. A solutions architect must ensure that the application can interact with the DynamoDB table without exposing traffic to the internet.
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to accomplish this goal? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
There are two separate requirements — competence and route. Permission: EKS packagings are assigned a role through IRSA (the role is linked to the service account through the clustered OIDC provider) and the application is then run on a temporary voucher (A). Route: In order to prevent the call to DynamoDB from going to the Internet, a VPC endpoint was created - for DynamoDB, it is a free gateway endpoint (D). Code does not contain keys and there is no NAT gateway in the design.
Option B: IAM users are not "add" to a Pod: that's a long-term voucher, and Pod gets permission by character.
Option C: The Network Access Control List (ACL) allows or rejects traffic, but without an endpoint, the path to DynamoDB will still flow through the Internet or NAT gateway.
Option E: The code contains access keys as a direct reverse mode: the key will eventually appear in mirrors and warehouses and will never be rotated.

options.text: Attach an IAM role that has sufficient privileges to the EKS pod.
Attach an IAM user that has sufficient privileges to the EKS pod.
Allow outbound connectivity to the DynamoDB table through the private subnets’ network ACLs.
Create a VPC endpoint for DynamoDB.
Embed the access keys in the Java Spring Boot code.

question_text:
A company recently migrated its web application to AWS by rehosting the application on Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The company wants to redesign its application architecture to be highly available and fault tolerant. Traffic must reach all running EC2 instances randomly.
Which combination of steps should the company take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
There are two separate requirements. Inter-regional error tolerance: the examples are evenly distributed between two available areas, so that failure in one area does not result in an uneven reduction of capacity — that is, two examples each available area (E). Request a random distribution between all running cases: the multi-value response strategy in Route 53 returns up to eight records with an associated health check, from which the client selects one and an unhealthy address is excluded from the response (C).
Option A: The failure switch is only sent to the backup in the event of a failure of the main resource - this is not a random distribution between all examples.
Option B: Weighted routers to set a proportional distribution of traffic, which requires a random distribution between all health objectives.
Option D: The distribution of the three examples into two plus one is uneven: if the area with two examples fails, only one third of the capacity is left.

options.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy.
Create an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy.
Create an Amazon Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy.
Launch three EC2 instances: two instances in one Availability Zone and one instance in another Availability Zone.
Launch four EC2 instances: two instances in one Availability Zone and two instances in another Availability Zone.

question_text:
A media company collects and analyzes user activity data on premises. The company wants to migrate this capability to AWS. The user activity data store will continue to grow and will be petabytes in size. The company needs to build a highly available data ingestion solution that facilitates on-demand analytics of existing data and new data with SQL.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
High availability, increasing data volume and demand for demand-driven SQL queries need to be achieved at minimal operational cost. Kinesis Data Firehose can ingest data without the need to manage the fraction and transmit the data directly to the Redshift cluster, thereby supporting SQL queries immediately, including historical data.
Option A: Data stored in S3 drums does not in themselves provide SQL queries: you still need a directory and a query engine, and Kinesis data streams need a fractional management.
Option C: The customised processing function that is triggered by the arrival of a file means that a code and maintenance need to be prepared and that the design does not contain a query engine at all.
Option D: Self-defined intake services deployed on the example plus a relational RDS database are difficult to expand to the petabytes level and require complete operations management.

options.text: Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Send activity data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the stream to deliver the data to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
Place activity data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure Amazon S3 to run an AWS Lambda function on the data as the data arrives in the S3 bucket.
Create an ingestion service on Amazon EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Configure the service to forward data to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ database.

question_text:
A company collects data from thousands of remote devices by using a RESTful web services application that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance receives the raw data, transforms the raw data, and stores all the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The number of remote devices will increase into the millions soon. The company needs a highly scalable solution that minimizes operational overhead.
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
Millions of equipment, raw data streams, and minimal operational requirements mean that data intake must be server-free and flexible to expand. The API Gateway receiver HTTP request, which places the records in the Kinesis Data Stream, Firehose buffers these records and writes them into S3, without the participation of the server (E). The conversions previously performed by the example are now handled by the hosting ETL tool AWS Glue, which works directly on the data (A) available in S3. There are no examples in the design at all.
Option B: Route 53 distributes the request to the example, but the example does not disappear: the operational burden remains.
Option C: It is the manual extension that adds more examples, and that's what the title is about to avoid.
Option D: SQS queued and processed on the example can smooth peaks, but still requires a full set of machines to run, and Kinesis is better suited to handle data flows.

options.text: Use AWS Glue to process the raw data in Amazon S3.
Use Amazon Route 53 to route traffic to different EC2 instances.
Add more EC2 instances to accommodate the increasing amount of incoming data.
Send the raw data to Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Use EC2 instances to process the data.
Use Amazon API Gateway to send the raw data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to use the data stream as a source to deliver the data to Amazon S3.

question_text:
A company needs to retain its AWS CloudTrail logs for 3 years. The company is enforcing CloudTrail across a set of AWS accounts by using AWS Organizations from the parent account. The CloudTrail target S3 bucket is configured with S3 Versioning enabled. An S3 Lifecycle policy is in place to delete current objects after 3 years.
After the fourth year of use of the S3 bucket, the S3 bucket metrics show that the number of objects has continued to rise. However, the number of new CloudTrail logs that are delivered to the S3 bucket has remained consistent.
Which solution will delete objects that are older than 3 years in the MOST cost-effective manner?
explanation_en:
The symptoms are described very accurately: there are no new logs, but the number of objects continues to grow - which means that expired versions are accumulating. In the version S3 bucket, life cycle rules with expired operations only remove the current version and turn it into a delete mark, while the earlier version is still kept and charged on an ongoing basis. The solution is to add to the rule the Noncurrent VersionEximation (and also to clear the expired deleted tags). This is a configuration change rather than a code operation, so it is also the most economical option.
Option A: CloudTrail log stream does not set itself to specify how long the object will remain in the S3 bucket: the object life cycle is managed by S3.
Option C: The function of an item object and version means that a code is required and that the cost of the function calling and the cost of the LIST and DELETE requests is required. The life cycle rules allow the same operation to be performed free of charge.
Option D: The object ' s ownership affects the object ' s access rights, rather than deciding how many versions to retain or what the cost is.

options.text: Configure the organization’s centralized CloudTrail trail to expire objects after 3 years.
Configure the S3 Lifecycle policy to delete previous versions as well as current versions.
Create an AWS Lambda function to enumerate and delete objects from Amazon S3 that are older than 3 years.
Configure the parent account as the owner of all objects that are delivered to the S3 bucket.

question_text:
A company has an API that receives real-time data from a fleet of monitoring devices. The API stores this data in an Amazon RDS DB instance for later analysis. The amount of data that the monitoring devices send to the API fluctuates. During periods of heavy traffic, the API often returns timeout errors.
After an inspection of the logs, the company determines that the database is not capable of processing the volume of write traffic that comes from the API. A solutions architect must minimize the number of connections to the database and must ensure that data is not lost during periods of heavy traffic.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Two requirements: to reduce the number of connections to the database and not to lose data in the event of a surge in traffic. A SQS queue can receive records and keep them immediately, while a Lambda function reads queues in batches and writes data into databases with limited co-activity - hence the small number of connections, and the surge in traffic only results in longer queues.
Option A: More memory will not increase the number of connections allowed, nor will it prevent data loss in the event of a surge in traffic.
Option B: In the Multi-AZ configuration, the backup example does not accept writing: it is not possible to write the data into "all examples of activity".
Option D: SNS immediately delivers the message without buffering: data will be lost if the subscriber is unavailable.

options.text: Increase the size of the DB instance to an instance type that has more available memory.
Modify the DB instance to be a Multi-AZ DB instance. Configure the application to write to all active RDS DB instances.
Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SQS invokes to write data from the queue to the database.
Modify the API to write incoming data to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Use an AWS Lambda function that Amazon SNS invokes to write data from the topic to the database.

question_text:
A company manages its own Amazon EC2 instances that run MySQL databases. The company is manually managing replication and scaling as demand increases or decreases. The company needs a new solution that simplifies the process of adding or removing compute capacity to or from its database tier as needed. The solution also must offer improved performance, scaling, and durability with minimal effort from operations.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
The company is currently processing manually the copying and extension of MySQL on the example. Aurora Servers for Aurora MySQL completely eliminates the need for engines to be compatible with MySQL, so applications need not be changed, capacity adjusted automatically, storage expands itself and data is stored in six copies of the three available areas.
Option B: The PostgreSQL option needs to switch engines and rewrite queries, while the company currently uses MySQL.
Option C: Consolidation of the database into a larger case is a manual vertical extension — that's what they want to get out of.
Option D: Relationship database cannot be expanded through the EC2 Autoextend group: new examples will not be able to share the same data.

options.text: Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora MySQL.
Migrate the databases to Amazon Aurora Serverless for Aurora PostgreSQL.
Combine the databases into one larger MySQL database. Run the larger database on larger EC2 instances.
Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group for the database tier. Migrate the existing databases to the new environment.

question_text:
A company is concerned that two NAT instances in use will no longer be able to support the traffic needed for the company’s application. A solutions architect wants to implement a solution that is highly available, fault tolerant, and automatically scalable.
What should the solutions architect recommend?
explanation_en:
High availability, tolerance and automatic expansion are all necessary. The NAT gateway is a hosting service that can be automatically extended to dozens of kibbits and maintained by AWS. The deployment of a gateway in each of the available areas ensures independence between the available areas if one of them fails.
Option A: Two gateways in the same area of availability means that failure in the area of availability will result in all subnets losing Internet access.
Option B: The example of NAT using an automatic extension group behind the load balancer is a self-builder: the default route cannot point to the load balancer.
Option D: Spot example can be retrieved at any time and it is not feasible to flow through the load balancer route.

options.text: Remove the two NAT instances and replace them with two NAT gateways in the same Availability Zone.
Use Auto Scaling groups with Network Load Balancers for the NAT instances in different Availability Zones.
Remove the two NAT instances and replace them with two NAT gateways in different Availability Zones.
Replace the two NAT instances with Spot Instances in different Availability Zones and deploy a Network Load Balancer.

question_text:
An application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance that has an Elastic IP address in VPC A. The application requires access to a database in VPC B. Both VPCs are in the same AWS account.
Which solution will provide the required access MOST securely?
explanation_en:
Both networks belong to the same account and are within AWS and should therefore be connected privately. VPC reciprocal connections create a direct route between the two networks on the internal infrastructure of AWS: traffic does not flow to the Internet, databases do not have a public network address and access is further restricted through the security team.
Option A: Allowing through a public network IP address means that traffic will pass through the Internet and that the rule itself is easily circumvented if the address changes.
Option C: Open public access to databases is a gross violation of basic security practice: it exposes the entire Internet.
Option D: Deployment of an agent in a separate case would introduce a failure point, cost and maintenance requirements, while a normal peer-to-peer connection is sufficient.

options.text: Create a DB instance security group that allows all traffic from the public IP address of the application server in VPC A.
Configure a VPC peering connection between VPC A and VPC B.
Make the DB instance publicly accessible. Assign a public IP address to the DB instance.
Launch an EC2 instance with an Elastic IP address into VPC B. Proxy all requests through the new EC2 instance.

question_text: A company runs demonstration environments for its customers on Amazon EC2 instances. Each environment is isolated in its own VPC. The company’s operations team needs to be notified when RDP or SSH access to an environment has been established.
explanation_en:
A signal needs to be created at a moment when someone connects to the environment through RDP or SSH. The standard way to view connections per se is VPC flow logs: they record reception connections with target ports 3389 and 22, which are sent to Cloudwatch Logs, where the indicator filter converts these logs to indicators, while the alarm sends a notification. All content is based on the hosting component and works in the same manner in all segregated VPCs.
Option A: Claudwatch Application Insights monitors the health status and indicators of the application, rather than the fact that SSH or RDP are logged in.
Option B: A role with the AmazonSSMManaged InstanceCore policy allows you to manage examples through the system manager, but using it alone does not inform anyone of anything.
Option D: EC2 instance change event report instances started, stopped and terminated. User connectivity is not one of those events.

options.text: Configure Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights to create AWS Systems Manager OpsItems when RDP or SSH access is detected.
Configure the EC2 instances with an IAM instance profile that has an IAM role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy attached.
Publish VPC flow logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create required metric filters. Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric alarm with a notification action for when the alarm is in the ALARM state.

Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to listen for events of type EC2 Instance State-change Notification. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target. Subscribe the operations team to the topic.

question_text:
A solutions architect has created a new AWS account and must secure AWS account root user access.
Which combination of actions will accomplish this? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
The root user account cannot be limited by the IAM policy - it always has full access to the account. The key to protecting root accounts is therefore to make access more difficult: a strong and unique password (A) and multifactor authentication (B), preferably with a hardware or virtual device independent of the main device. In addition, AWS recommends never create access keys for root accounts and that daily operations should be done through the IAM role.
Option C: Root accounts should not have access keys from the outset - so there is no content that needs to be stored. An encrypted S3 bucket does not change the fact that the disclosure of such keys means that there is complete control over the account.
Option D: Root accounts are not subject to the IAM policy: add them to groups with no role and no restrictions.
Option E: Unable to attach an interconnective policy to the root user. Its operation can only be limited by the SCP strategy of AWS Organizations to manage accounts, even if it is not fully effective.

options.text: Ensure the root user uses a strong password.
Enable multi-factor authentication to the root user.
Store root user access keys in an encrypted Amazon S3 bucket.
Add the root user to a group containing administrative permissions.
Apply the required permissions to the root user with an inline policy document.

question_text:
A company is building a new web-based customer relationship management application. The application will use several Amazon EC2 instances that are backed by Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application will also use an Amazon Aurora database. All data for the application must be encrypted at rest and in transit.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The question is which service is responsible for what. The static encryption of data in AWS is the responsibility of KMS: the storage of EBS volumes and Aurora clusters is open using the specified KMS keys. The encryption of the data to the user during the transmission is performed by TLS certificates on the load balancer, which are issued and managed by ACM and are free of charge and automatically renewed. It's this combination -- KMS is responsible for data on disk, ACM is responsible for traffic -- which is described by the right options.
Option A: The function of the service is interchangeable: KMS does not issue TLS certificates for the load balancer, and ACM does not encrypt EBS volumes or database storage.
Option B: There is no global "encrypted for all the contents of the account" switch, and daily operations using root accounts violate basic security guidelines.
Option D: BitLocker is a Windows mechanism that you maintain on your own, not a hosting volume encryption. And you cannot attach KMS keys to the load balancer to replace the ACM certificate.

options.text: Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) certificates on the ALB to encrypt data in transit. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest.

Use the AWS root account to log in to the AWS Management Console. Upload the company’s encryption certificates. While in the root account, select the option to turn on encryption for all data at rest and in transit for the account.
Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to encrypt the EBS volumes and Aurora database storage at rest. Attach an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate to the ALB to encrypt data in transit.
Use BitLocker to encrypt all data at rest. Import the company’s TLS certificate keys to AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) Attach the KMS keys to the ALB to encrypt data in transit.

question_text:
A company is moving its on-premises Oracle database to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The database has several applications that write to the same tables. The applications need to be migrated one by one with a month in between each migration. Management has expressed concerns that the database has a high number of reads and writes. The data must be kept in sync across both databases throughout the migration.
What should a solutions architect recommend?
explanation_en:
Migration from Oracle to Aurora PostgreSQL is engine change, so AWS Schema Conversion Tool converts mode and storage code. DMS runs a full load-on-data capture task for all tables: it moves data first and then applies changes continuously, so the database is synchronized throughout the months of the phased application of the migration. Given the high frequency of reading and writing operations, memory optimized copy examples — DMS keeps its change cache in memory.
Option A: DataSync moves a file instead of database content and only uses a CCDC task without initial loading will leave the target database empty.
Option B: Same error, misreading DataSync as a tool for initial database migration.
Option D: The calculation of an optimised example is not appropriate for a CDC with a high change frequency, and the selection of the largest table alone would cause the remaining tables to lose sync.

options.text: Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.

Use AWS DataSync for the initial migration. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.

Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a memory optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select all tables.

Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool with AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) using a compute optimized replication instance. Create a full load plus change data capture (CDC) replication task and a table mapping to select the largest tables.

question_text:
A company has a three-tier application for image sharing. The application uses an Amazon EC2 instance for the front-end layer, another EC2 instance for the application layer, and a third EC2 instance for a MySQL database. A solutions architect must design a scalable and highly available solution that requires the least amount of change to the application.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
Extension and high availability are necessary, and minimal modifications to the application are required. Elastic Beanstalk directly uses existing codes and deploys them into environments equipped with load balancers and multiple available areas, and the database moves to the Multi-AZ configuration of the RDS, while user images migrate to S3, thereby reducing the load of the case.
Option A: Migration to Lambda and DynamoDB means that the application needs to be rewrited, which is inconsistent with the requirement to avoid changes.
Option B: Read a copy does not provide an automatic failure switch and storing the image in a relationship database is inefficient.
Option C: A larger example of a database does not meet the requirement of availability or solve the problem of image storage.

options.text: Use Amazon S3 to host the front-end layer. Use AWS Lambda functions for the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use Amazon S3 to store and serve users’ images.

Use load-balanced Multi-AZ AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments for the front-end layer and the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon RDS DB instance with multiple read replicas to serve users’ images.

Use Amazon S3 to host the front-end layer. Use a fleet of EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group for the application layer. Move the database to a memory optimized instance type to store and serve users’ images.

Use load-balanced Multi-AZ AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments for the front-end layer and the application layer. Move the database to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. Use Amazon S3 to store and serve users’ images.

question_text:
An application running on an Amazon EC2 instance in VPC-A needs to access files in another EC2 instance in VPC-
B. Both VPCs are in separate AWS accounts. The network administrator needs to design a solution to configure secure access to EC2 instance in VPC-B from VPC-A. The connectivity should not have a single point of failure or bandwidth concerns.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The network between the different accounts requires private connections, and there can be no single point failure or bandwidth limitations. The VPC peer-to-peer connection meets all of these needs: it is a hosting function for the AWS network itself, without intermediate equipment that may fail, and without bandwidth restrictions normally present in tunnels.
Option B: Gateway peer points provide access to services such as S3 and DynamoDB, rather than access to examples from other accounts VPC.
Option C: Virtual private gateway is the access point to connect your local site through VPN or DirectConect - it is not used to connect two VPCs.
Option D: The private virtual interface is DirectConnect, created for the data centre connection, not for the connection between the two VPCs.

options.text: Set up a VPC peering connection between VPC-A and VPC-B.
Set up VPC gateway endpoints for the EC2 instance running in VPC-B.
Attach a virtual private gateway to VPC-B and set up routing from VPC-A.
Create a private virtual interface (VIF) for the EC2 instance running in VPC-B and add appropriate routes from VPC-A.

question_text:
A company wants to experiment with individual AWS accounts for its engineer team. The company wants to be notified as soon as the Amazon EC2 instance usage for a given month exceeds a specific threshold for each account.
What should a solutions architect do to meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
When EC2 usage exceeds the threshold in a month, notification is required and is achieved at the lowest possible cost. AWS Budgets is designed for this purpose: a budget with a monthly cycle, filtering to EC2 services, setting alarm thresholds and sending notifications to the SNS theme. The first two budgets in the account are free of charge, the excess is measured on a daily basis and divided into units of beauty. Cost Explorer and CUR are analytical tools - they do not send notifications when the threshold is exceeded.
Option A: Cost Explorer can generate reports, but cannot send a notification when the threshold is exceeded - this is the use of Budgets.
Option B: Same error: Cost Explorer is not a notification mechanism.
Option D: CUR, Athena and a time query can be achieved, but multiple services are involved, custom queries are required, and fees for scanning are required, and only the budget can be used.

options.text: Use Cost Explorer to create a daily report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances. Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.

Use Cost Explorer to create a monthly report of costs by service. Filter the report by EC2 instances. Configure Cost Explorer to send an Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) notification when a threshold is exceeded.

Use AWS Budgets to create a cost budget for each account. Set the period to monthly. Set the scope to EC2 instances. Set an alert threshold for the budget. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.

Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create a report with hourly granularity. Integrate the report data with Amazon Athena. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an Athena query. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to receive a notification when a threshold is exceeded.

question_text:
A solutions architect needs to design a new microservice for a company’s application. Clients must be able to call an HTTPS endpoint to reach the microservice. The microservice also must use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to authenticate calls. The solutions architect will write the logic for this microservice by using a single AWS Lambda function that is written in Go 1.x.
Which solution will deploy the function in the MOST operationally efficient way?
explanation_en:
Original answer: A; source correction answer: B.
LambdaFunction URL provides an HTTPS endpoint for a single function and supports AWS_IAM validation; this topic does not require conditions for the API Gateway extra functionality, so B is much less than the original answer A.
A single HTTPS terminal for a single function requires IAM authentication. This is exactly what the Lambda function URL of AWS_IAM authentication type (B) provides: no additional service is required and the terminal point is created with the function.
Option A: IAM authentication on API Gateway is technically feasible, but it introduces a service that has to be configured, formatted and paid for. The demand does not involve route, API key or flow restriction - so this is an unnecessary level.
Option C: Lambda@Edge requires a CloudFront distribution and the authentication logic must be written manually - this is the most cumbersome task of all options.
Option D: CloudFront Operations failed in both respects: they are the lightweight JavaScript function, which edits the head without network access and does not support the AWS_IAM authentication type.

options.text: Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Configure the method to use the Lambda function. Enable IAM authentication on the API.
Create a Lambda function URL for the function. Specify AWS_IAM as the authentication type.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy the function to [email protected] Integrate IAM authentication logic into the [email protected] function.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Deploy the function to CloudFront Functions. Specify AWS_IAM as the authentication type.

question_text:
A company previously migrated its data warehouse solution to AWS. The company also has an AWS Direct Connect connection. Corporate office users query the data warehouse using a visualization tool. The average size of a query returned by the data warehouse is 50 MB and each webpage sent by the visualization tool is approximately 500 KB. Result sets returned by the data warehouse are not cached.
Which solution provides the LOWEST data transfer egress cost for the company?
explanation_en:
Costs only apply to traffic leaving AWS. If the visualization tool operates in the same area as the data repository, the 50 MB query results do not leave AWS at all - only 500 KB web pages will come out, reducing the amount of data by a hundred times. In addition, this outflow is through DirectConnect route, with a rate of less per gigabytes than the Internet rate.
Option A: Local tools will pull the full 50 MB result of each query from AWS and fold the most expensive Internet rate on this basis. This is the worst option.
Option B: is correctly located and leaves a smaller station, but the cost of Internet traffic is higher than that of traffic through DirectConnect.
Option C: Connect costs less than the Internet, but the full search results are still flowing - the amount of data is 100 times the number of web pages.

options.text: Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over the internet.
Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse. Access it over the internet.
Host the visualization tool on premises and query the data warehouse directly over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same AWS Region.
Host the visualization tool in the same AWS Region as the data warehouse and access it over a Direct Connect connection at a location in the same Region.

question_text:
An online learning company is migrating to the AWS Cloud. The company maintains its student records in a PostgreSQL database. The company needs a solution in which its data is available and online across multiple AWS Regions at all times.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The data must remain on-line, remain available in multiple regions and operate at minimal cost. Creates a single operation to read a copy of the RDS in another area, receives changes on an ongoing basis, can be consulted and can be upgraded to a stand-alone database if needed.
Option A: PortgreSQL clusters, managed on a case-by-case basis, are the largest maintenance programmes.
Option B: Multi-AZ operations take place only within a single region: data will not be available in other regions.
Option D: Copying snapshots to another region does not provide online access: the database still needs to be restored first from these snapshots.

options.text: Migrate the PostgreSQL database to a PostgreSQL cluster on Amazon EC2 instances.
Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with the Multi-AZ feature turned on.
Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Create a read replica in another Region.
Migrate the PostgreSQL database to an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Set up DB snapshots to be copied to another Region.

question_text:
A company hosts its web application on AWS using seven Amazon EC2 instances. The company requires that the IP addresses of all healthy EC2 instances be returned in response to DNS queries.
Which policy should be used to meet this requirement?
explanation_en:
The request is to return the address of all health cases to the DNS response. This is the function of the multivalue answer router: Route 53 returns up to eight records, each linked to its own health check, and unhealthy cases are excluded from the response.
Option A: A simple route strategy returns directly to the record and does not support a health check.
Option B: The delayed router will select a region with the lowest delay instead of returning the full list.
Option D: A geographically based route-oriented strategy selects the response according to the client ' s location and does not return to the list of all health addresses.

options.text: Simple routing policy
Latency routing policy
Multivalue routing policy
Geolocation routing policy

question_text:
A medical research lab produces data that is related to a new study. The lab wants to make the data available with minimum latency to clinics across the country for their on-premises, file-based applications. The data files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket that has read-only permissions for each clinic.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The clinic needs document-based access to data stored in S3 and a minimal local delay. A file gateway has been deployed as a virtual machine in each clinic: it presents a familiar NFS or SMB sharing to local applications, supported by S3 S3 buckets, and will cache frequently read files locally. Applications do not need to be changed and delays are controlled by local caches.
Option B: DataSync is a tool for one-time or periodic transfers, rather than continuous file access. Copying the entire data set to each clinic is a waste of resources and does not provide a single data source.
Option C: A scroll gateway provides a roll through iSCSI, while the clinic application works on a file basis.
Option D: An EFS file system cannot be mounted on any local server via the Internet: this requires a private connection to the VPC, and delays in this case will be determined by a network link rather than by local cache control.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic
Migrate the files to each clinic’s on-premises applications by using AWS DataSync for processing.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway as a virtual machine (VM) on premises at each clinic.
Attach an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to each clinic’s on-premises servers.

question_text:
A company is using a content management system that runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The EC2 instance contains both the web server and the database software. The company must make its website platform highly available and must enable the website to scale to meet user demand.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Levels need to be separated, with fault tolerance across available areas and expanded capabilities. The database is migrated to Aurora and a copy is configured in another available area to create the AMI, Web layer from the existing example to an automatic stretching group that crosses the two available areas and is behind the application load balancer. The failure of a serviceable area does not result in the disruption of applications or databases.
Option A: All machines and load balancers are located in a single serviceable area: failure of a serviceable area disrupts the entire site, and manual start-up examples do not provide extended capability.
Option B: The copy and the second machine remain in the same serviceable area - there is no tolerance for its failure.
Option D: The separate database example contains a copy in S3 with a single point failure and recovery time, while the hosting database solves the problem.

options.text: Move the database to Amazon RDS, and enable automatic backups. Manually launch another EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone. Configure an Application Load Balancer in the Availability Zone, and set the two instances as targets.

Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora instance with a read replica in the same Availability Zone as the existing EC2 instance. Manually launch another EC2 instance in the same Availability Zone. Configure an Application Load Balancer, and set the two EC2 instances as targets.

Move the database to Amazon Aurora with a read replica in another Availability Zone. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the EC2 instance. Configure an Application Load Balancer in two Availability Zones. Attach an Auto Scaling group that uses the AMI across two Availability Zones.

Move the database to a separate EC2 instance, and schedule backups to Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the original EC2 instance. Configure an Application Load Balancer in two Availability Zones. Attach an Auto Scaling group that uses the AMI across two Availability Zones.

question_text:
A company is launching an application on AWS. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to direct traffic to at least two Amazon EC2 instances in a single target group. The instances are in an Auto Scaling group for each environment. The company requires a development environment and a production environment. The production environment will have periods of high traffic.
Which solution will configure the development environment MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Reference answer: A; dispute option: D.
Reducing the target of the development environment to one does not guarantee that Auto Scaling group will stop the second example, so A does not necessarily save money; simply reduces ASG maximum and does not explicitly modify desired/minimm capacity, nor does D guarantee cost reduction. Lack of current capacity and abbreviation constraints and retention of source A for information purposes only.
The cost of developing the environment is determined by the number of cases actually in operation, not by how the load balancer distributes the request. Option A has been interpreted as `maintaining one example instead of two in the development environment' — halving expenditure. This is a truly controversial issue: the literally `reconfiguration of target groups' does not change the expected capacity of the automatic expansion group, which will restart the second example. Some communities therefore choose D. The argument against D is that the maximum value is only the upper limit, and that if the expected capacity of the development environment is 2 and never expanded, the reduction of the maximum value is useless.

This was repeated because the forms were resubmitted after the time elapsed. The accelerator continuously inspects the target ' s health, diverts each player ' s path to the nearest healthy area and completes the traffic switch in a few seconds, not affected by the DNS cache.
Option B: CloudFront optimizes content caches, while game traffic is dynamic; it does not provide for health check-ups or rapid cross-regional failure switching.
Option C: S3 S3 buckets cannot be used as a source for game applications: there is no logic and there is no session status.
Options D: DynamoDB and DAX relate to data storage and are not related to the route of traffic to healthy areas.

question_text:
A company has one million users that use its mobile app. The company must analyze the data usage in near-real time. The company also must encrypt the data in near-real time and must store the data in a centralized location in Apache Parquet format for further processing.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
Data stream ingestion, encryption, writing in Parquet format and analysis in near real time are necessary and require minimal operating costs. Kinesis Data Firehose itself has all these operations: it encrypts data, converts records to Parquet format and writes the data directly to S3, without having to manage the fractions, while Kinesis Data Analytics uses SQL queries to run flow analysis.
Option A: Kinesis Data Streams does not write data into S3 per se, needs to manage the fraction and needs an intermediate function to complicate the design.
Option B: EMR clusters must be created and paid for, and the flow itself is still unable to deliver the data directly to S3.
Option C: Firehouse was correct, but using EMR cluster analysis means that management nodes are needed, not hosting services.

options.text: Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application to analyze the data. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to send the data to the Kinesis Data Analytics application.
Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to store the data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to analyze the data. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to send the data to the EMR cluster.

question_text:
A gaming company has a web application that displays scores. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application stores data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Users are starting to experience long delays and interruptions that are caused by database read performance. The company wants to improve the user experience while minimizing changes to the application’s architecture.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Reference answer: B; dispute option: A.
Examtopics t1 q268 - RDS Proxy solves the problems of connective pools rather than reading performance; some communities prefer ElastiCache
It is clear that database reading performance is inadequate, ElastiCache can cache double-read and lower RDS read load; RDS Proxy is mainly linked to the database and cannot independently cache query results or add case reading through. Source answer B should be amended to A; the Cache Scheme still needs to apply the Cache.
Source answer B's original resolution (in conflict with verification results, not accepted):
The limitation in the process is `minimizing changes to the application architecture'. RDS Proxy is located transparently between the application and the database: only the connection string needs to be modified, and no code changes are required. It eliminates the main cause of `long delays and interruptions' during the surge - i.e. depletion and re-establishment of MySQL connections. The point at issue was that Proxy did not increase readability, whereas the title referred to `database readability', which led some communities to choose ElastiCache. Examination experience rules: complaints about connection and interruptions point to RDS Proxy; complaints about extensive double reading and allowing changes to codes point to caches or to reading copies.
Old Source Option A: A strong alternative: Cache does reduce reading pressure. Cache itself, however, cannot work independently - Cache side logic has to be added to the application: read the cache and, if you fail, then access the database, which must lapse when writing. This is a change at the application level, and the title requires that such changes be avoided.
Source old option C: Migration to Lambda changes the computational layer, but the database itself is the performance bottleneck. The issue of reading remains exactly the same, and structural changes are the most significant of all options.
Source old option D: Migration to DynamoDB means that data models and all queries need to be redesigned. This is the largest structural change for the need to minimize changes.

options.text: Use Amazon ElastiCache in front of the database.
Use RDS Proxy between the application and the database.
Migrate the application from EC2 instances to AWS Lambda.
Migrate the database from Amazon RDS for MySQL to Amazon DynamoDB.

question_text:
