The performance degradation is attributed to an increase in the number of read-only SQL queries triggered by business analysts. A solutions architect needs to solve the problem with minimal changes to the existing web application.
What should the solutions architect recommend?
explanation_en:
The downgrading was due to a read-only query initiated by the analyst. A reading copy removes these queries from the main example: applications continue to run on the main example, analysts are connected to the copy and code changes are minimal.
Option A: DynamoDB needs to rewrite the query and is not suitable for immediate analysis.
Option B: ElastiCache is a memory cache; it is not possible to run any SQL analysis query above.
Option D: Redshift requires a separate loading pipeline and a cluster of ongoing operations: changes and costs have increased significantly.

question_text:
A company is using a centralized AWS account to store log data in various Amazon S3 buckets. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the data is encrypted at rest before the data is uploaded to the S3 buckets. The data also must be encrypted in transit.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
The particulars of differentiation are a word: the data must be encrypted before being uploaded. Any server-end encryption (SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, SSE-C) is performed after S3 has received the object, which means that data remain in explicit form during transmission of any intermediate component between the application and S3. This requirement is met only if the client encrypts: the application itself encrypts the object, and only the secret text arrives at S3. Encryption during the transfer is provided by TLS, S3 default supports TLS and can be enforced by the aws:SecureTransport condition in the storage barrel policy.
Option B: Server-end encryption is executed by the service after the service receives the object. By definition, the requirement of 'encrypted before upload' has not been met.
Option C: The storage barrel policy only compels the client to request SSE-S3 - the same server-end encryption, which is only set as enforcement. The timing of the encryption event has not changed.
Option D: Encryption of the default S3 bucket using KMS keys is still a server-end solution: objects are encrypted after they are received.

options.text: Use client-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
Use server-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
Create bucket policies that require the use of server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE- S3) for S3 uploads.

question_text:

The peak capacity is the ‘same every night and the batch jobs always start at 1 AM. The solutions architect needs to find a cost-effective solution that will allow for the desired EC2 capacity to be reached quickly and allow the Auto Scaling group to scale down after the batch jobs are complete.
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The peak is known in advance: the operation begins at 1 a.m. and the required capacity is the same every night. The planned expansion increases the number of cases required before the operation begins, so that the one-hour waiting period disappears and the group automatically downsizes through its normal strategy after the operation is completed.
Option A: The minimum volume of permanent increase means that the cost of idle cases continues to be paid throughout the day.
Option B: Maximum capacity is capped and has no impact on the speed of expansion.
Option D: A larger step will accelerate the rate of growth, but the expansion will only begin after the load has arrived and is detected.

options.text: Increase the minimum capacity for the Auto Scaling group.

question_text:
A company serves a dynamic website from a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website needs to support multiple languages to serve customers around the world. The website’s architecture is running in the us-west-1 Region and is exhibiting high request latency for users that are located in other parts of the world.
The website needs to serve requests quickly and efficiently regardless of a user’s location. However, the company does not want to recreate the existing architecture across multiple Regions.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The architecture cannot be replicated, and what needs to be accelerated is the existing entry points. Use the load balancer as the source of the CloudFront, even for dynamic content, to reduce delays: TLS terminates at the nearest edge and requests transfer to the area via the AWS backbone network. Once the Accept-Language head is contained in the Cache Behaviour Settings, the language version is provided correctly - and a separate cache copy is maintained for each language.
Option A: The website is dynamic, and its full migration to the S3 drum means that the application needs to be rewritten — this is not required in the demand.
Option C: API Gateway Cache is an additional layer of structure added to the load balancer to provide neither a global edge network nor a delayed advantage for users on other continents.
Option D: The deployment of custom cache servers in each region is an infrastructure that needs to be deployed and maintained — this is the multi-area setup that the company does not want to achieve.

options.text: Replace the existing architecture with a website that is served from an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as the origin. Set the cache behavior settings to cache based on the Accept-Language request header.

question_text:
A rapidly growing ecommerce company is running its workloads in a single AWS Region. A solutions architect must create a disaster recovery (DR) strategy that includes a different AWS Region. The company wants its database to be up to date in the DR Region with the least possible latency. The remaining infrastructure in the DR Region needs to run at reduced capacity and must be able to scale up if necessary.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LOWEST recovery time objective (RTO)?
explanation_en:
The requirement is that the database for the second region be kept as up-to-date as possible and that the recovery time be minimized in cases where infrastructure in the region is operating at reduced capacity but is already available. While the global Aurora database replicates data in storage, usually delayed at the subsecond level, the heating deployment means that all components in the second area are already operating at a reduced scale and need only be expanded. This is much faster than building an environment from scratch.
Option A: A pilot deployment means that a closed or very low-calculated layer must be deployed at the time of the disaster, leading to longer recovery than heating.
Option C: Multi-AZ is configured to operate within a single area and no copy of data from another region is provided at all.
Option D: Same error: Multi-AZ is not a cross-regional solution, regardless of the alternative mode chosen.

Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a pilot light deployment.
Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a warm standby deployment.

question_text:
A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to implement a disaster recovery (DR) solution for the application. The DR solution needs to have a recovery time objective (RTO) of less than 4 hours. The DR solution also needs to use the fewest possible AWS resources during normal operations.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?
explanation_en:
A RTO of less than four hours allows disaster recovery stations to be offline rather than operational and the use of resources must be minimized during normal operations. Mirrors were copied to a secondary area and the entire infrastructure was described in the AWS CloudFormation template: in the event of a disaster, stacks were deployed through a single operation, using standard mechanisms rather than custom scripts to maintain them.
Option A: Custom functions and deployed scripts are codes that need to be prepared, tested and maintained.
Option C: The example of continuity in the second area is a direct violation of the requirement to minimize the use of resources.
Option D: The second available area cannot withstand regional-level failure and means that the machine is running continuously.

options.text: Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to a secondary AWS Region. Automate infrastructure deployment in the secondary Region by using AWS Lambda and custom scripts.
Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to a secondary AWS Region. Automate infrastructure deployment in the secondary Region by using AWS CloudFormation.

question_text:
A company runs an internal browser-based application. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The Auto Scaling group scales up to 20 instances during work hours, but scales down to 2 instances overnight. Staff are complaining that the application is very slow when the day begins, although it runs well by mid-morning.
How should the scaling be changed to address the staff complaints and keep costs to a minimum?
explanation_en:
The morning delay occurred because the group would react only after the load had already appeared. A target tracking strategy with a lower CPU utilization threshold would start increasing capacity earlier, while a shorter cooling cycle would allow examples to be added more frequently. Cost increases only during the period of actual load increases.
Option A: Setting the required capacity to 20 in advance means that peak configuration costs must be paid even if not yet required.
Option B: Step-up is equally feasible, but it increases the number of cases in fixed numbers and maintains target levels as accurately as target tracking.
Option D: Encoding the minimum hard value to 20 examples will prevent the group from ever shrinking and make the programme the most expensive.

options.text: Implement a scheduled action that sets the desired capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.
Implement a step scaling action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
Implement a target tracking action triggered at a lower CPU threshold, and decrease the cooldown period.
Implement a scheduled action that sets the minimum and maximum capacity to 20 shortly before the office opens.

question_text:
A company has a multi-tier application deployed on several Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. An Amazon RDS for Oracle instance is the application’ s data layer that uses Oracle-specific PL/SQL functions. Traffic to the application has been steadily increasing. This is causing the EC2 instances to become overloaded and the RDS instance to run out of storage. The Auto Scaling group does not have any scaling metrics and defines the minimum healthy instance count only. The company predicts that traffic will continue to increase at a steady but unpredictable rate before leveling off.
What should a solutions architect do to ensure the system can automatically scale for the increased traffic?
(Choose two.)
explanation_en:
There are two separate issues, each of which is resolved independently. The database storage space is inadequate and is addressed by the use of automatic storage extensions in the RDS instance, so that the volume increases automatically when the storage space is filled and does not result in a stoppage (A). The example is overloaded and the auto-extend group is not configured at all, so an expansion strategy based on average CPU utilization is designed to enable the example group to expand as the flow increases (D).
Option B: Migration to Aurora requires to abandon the specific Oracle PL/SQL functions that are being used, and the scene makes it clear that these functions are being used.
Option C: Low storage space alarms will only inform the problem itself and will not add any storage space.
Option E: Free memory is not the default indicator for Cloudwatch — which needs to be collected by proxy — and as the primary indicator for the load on the Web layer, it is less efficient than CPU.

question_text:
A company provides an online service for posting video content and transcoding it for use by any mobile platform.
The application architecture uses Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard to collect and store the videos so that multiple Amazon EC2 Linux instances can access the video content for processing. As the popularity of the service has grown over time, the storage costs have become too expensive.
Which storage solution is MOST cost-effective?
explanation_en:
Video files are objects that are only written once and read during processing, so it would be expensive to store them in file systems like EFS. Store source files and results in S3 and copy only the files in processing to an EBS volume attached to the example during the transcode, thus eliminating the continuing cost of storage of persistent files, and S3 costs only a small fraction of EFS per gui byte.
Option A: The file gateway is a hybrid gateway for accessing S3 from the local network. It is pointless to place it between cloud examples and S3 buckets — it is just an extra layer of expenses and costs.
Option B: Volume gateway solves the same blending problem of a roll, which is also not suitable for this scene.
Option C: Storage remains in the EFS, so the main cost drivers remain unchanged, and moving the results to EBS only increases additional costs.

options.text: Use AWS Storage Gateway for files to store and process the video content.
Use AWS Storage Gateway for volumes to store and process the video content.

question_text:
A company wants to create an application to store employee data in a hierarchical structured relationship. The company needs a minimum-latency response to high-traffic queries for the employee data and must protect any sensitive data. The company also needs to receive monthly email messages if any financial information is present in the employee data.
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
Two independent demands. Storage of employee data with a hierarchical structure and keeping minimum delay at high load point to DynamoDB(B): the partitioning and sorting keys naturally map to the hierarchical structure, delay at the level of several bits of milliseconds and export to S3 per month for audit. Test financial information and send monthly circulars pointing to Amazon Macie (E): it disaggregates sensitive data in S3 and will be posted to EventBridge and then notified to the subscriber to the SNS theme.
Option A: Redshift is an analytical repository constructed for complex queries on large data sets, rather than a source for high-flow, low-delayed point queries.
Option C: Sending an event to the Lambda function means that the e-mail sending and subscription logic must be built from the top. SNS theme does this without code.
Option D: Athena and QuickSight provide an analysis and dashboard, but they cannot meet the need for fast-track application queries or for financial data testing.

Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the employee data in hierarchies. Export the data to Amazon S3 every month.

question_text:

explanation_en:
AWS Backup covers all requirements and is achieved only through one plan: a monthly plan, a life-cycle strategy, after six months to move back-up to cold storage and to maintain a seven-year retention period. No scripts, no manual operations.
Option B: The DynamoDB backup cannot be moved to S3 S3 buckets and managed using life-cycle rules - they are internal objects of the service.
Option C: Two custom plan scripts are the maximum possible development and maintenance costs, and an off-the-shelf hosting service exists.
Option D: A backup command as required does not accept the parameters used for transition to cold storage or to delete the plan - these are defined by the AWS Backup plan.

question_text:

question_text:

Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
A RPO less than a second means almost zero data loss, which can only be provided by synchronized copying. The RDS Multi-AZ will synchronise each service into a backup example of another available area, so that the submitted service will not be lost when the failure switch occurs.
Option B: The RDS database example does not have automatic case extension and a single available area cannot withstand the region ' s failure.
Option C: Read a copy of the copy by step - The delay is measured in seconds and does not guarantee the required recovery point.

question_text:
A company runs a web application that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnet of a VPC. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across the public subnets directs web traffic to the EC2 instances.
The company wants to implement new security measures to restrict inbound traffic from the ALB to the EC2 instances while preventing access from any other source inside or outside the private subnet of the EC2 instances.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The requirement is to allow traffic only from the load balancer and not from any other source. This was achieved by citing the security team: the entry rules for the example only allowed traffic from the security group ALB. No other source, inside or outside the subnet, can be connected.
Option A: The inability to create a path from the Internet to a private address of the example, even if created, exposes the example to worldwide access.
Option C: Move the example to a public subnet with flexible IP addresses, on the contrary - it places the example on the Internet.
Option D: Allow the load balancer to receive any TCP traffic at any port, without limiting access to the example itself, but rather undermining the security posture.

question_text:
A research company runs experiments that are powered by a simulation application and a visualization application.
The simulation application runs on Linux and outputs intermediate data to an NFS share every 5 minutes. The visualization application is a Windows desktop application that displays the simulation output and requires an SMB file system.
The company maintains two synchronized file systems. This strategy is causing data duplication and inefficient resource usage. The company needs to migrate the applications to AWS without making code changes to either application.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The underlying reason is two different protocols: Linux Simulation is written on NFS, Windows is visualized on SMB and the company is forced to maintain two synchronized copies. Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP is the only service that can provide the same data through both NFS and SMB in the AWS file service. A duplicate copy disappears when the application moves to an EC2 instance without a code change.
Option A: Lambda is not suitable for a long run simulation or Windows desktop application, moving to S3 means that two applications need to be rewrited, which contradicts the requirements.
Option B: FSx File Gateway is a mixed gateway to access FSx from the local network, rather than to provide shared storage and two protocol access to the AWS internal workload.
Option C: SQS only delivers messages, it does not provide file resources - applications must be rewritten to fit the queue.

options.text: Migrate both applications to AWS Lambda. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to exchange data between the applications.
Migrate both applications to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon FSx File Gateway for storage.

question_text:
As part of budget planning, management wants a report of AWS billed items listed by user. The data will be used to create department budgets. A solutions architect needs to determine the most efficient way to obtain this report information.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
What is required is a cost-distribution of sectoral budgets by consumers, and it needs to be completed quickly. Cost Explorer helps you to construct reports that are grouped by cost allocation labels (e.g. by owner or sector), grouped by associated account, grouped by service, viewed in chart form, and exported as CSV files. This is the most direct path - no export, no SQL, no storage.

Option C: The billing from the billing control dashboard shows the total by service, but lacks the necessary information to group by owner and lacks a flexible filter function.
Option D: AWS Budgets sends an alarm when the threshold is exceeded, which is not a tool for constructing the cost structure report.

options.text: Run a query with Amazon Athena to generate the report.
Create a report in Cost Explorer and download the report.

question_text:
A company hosts its static website by using Amazon S3. The company wants to add a contact form to its webpage.
The contact form will have dynamic server-side components for users to input their name, email address, phone number, and user message. The company anticipates that there will be fewer than 100 site visits each month.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
There is no point in paying for an ongoing server when less than 100 visits are made per month. The form is processed by calling API Gateway and the backend is covered by a Lambda function, which sends mail through Amazon SES. Such a combination would cost zero in idle hours and would remain within a free-of-charge range at 100 requests per month.
Option A: ECS tasks are charged for running on a continuous basis, even if the flow is almost zero.
Option C: Lightsail is an example of a fixed monthly fee, while WorkMail is charged by the number of mailboxes.
Option D: Ongoing examples with LAMP inn need to be maintained - the most expensive and labour-intensive option.

options.text: Host a dynamic contact form page in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to connect to any third-party email provider.

question_text:
A company has a static website that is hosted on Amazon CloudFront in front of Amazon S3. The static website uses a database backend. The company notices that the website does not reflect updates that have been made in the website’s Git repository. The company checks the continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipeline between the Git repository and Amazon S3. The company verifies that the webhooks are configured properly and that the CI/CD pipeline is sending messages that indicate successful deployments.
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that displays the updates on the website.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Successfully deployed and documents in the S3 buckets have been updated, but users still see the old version — which means that Cloud Front is providing content from the cache. The object is kept at the edge until its TTL expires, so each deployment requires an invalid operation, which is best integrated into the same delivery conduit.
Option A: The load balancer distributes the flow to the instance, but the site is static and exists in the S3 buckets - not related to outdated caches.
Option B: The cache before the database can speed up the search, but it is not providing outdated documents — the content distribution network.
Option D: Certificate authentication involves TLS and is not related to the freshness of the content.

options.text: Add an Application Load Balancer.

question_text:
A company wants to migrate a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers: an application tier, a business tier, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server. The company wants to use specific features of SQL Server such as native backups and Data Quality Services. The company also needs to share files for processing between the tiers.
How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The scene indicated that the hosting service did not provide certain SQL Server functions: back-up of primary engines and data quality services. The database must therefore be deployed in the EC2 instance. In the Windows environment, the shared file exchange between levels is provided by Amazon FSx for Windows File Server - a SMB sharing that supports Windows ACL and can be accessed at all three levels.
Option A: FSx File Gateway is used to access FSx filesystems from local networks, but all levels are already inside AWS - this will only introduce an unnecessary middle layer.
Option C: RDS for SQL Server does not support either the original backup method used by the company or data quality services - which is directly contrary to demand.
Option D: RDS has the same problem; furthermore, EBS volumes are not multiple examples of file resources that can be shared.

options.text: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.
Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.

question_text:

explanation_en:
A group of Linux servers sharing file access without applying changes is Amazon EFS. The file system is mounted on all Web servers in all available areas through the NFS, and applications can still use normal paths and files, and storage can expand automatically.
Option A: S3 is the object stored, accessed through API. To use it, the application had to be rewrited, which contradicted the requirements.
Option B: CloudFront is located in front of S3 to speed up the distribution of static content, but it is still unable to provide a shared file system for the server.
Option D: An EBS volume can only be mounted in a single available area, on which a normal file system is not designed for simultaneous writing by multiple servers.

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 Standard bucket with access to the web servers.

question_text:
A company has an AWS Lambda function that needs read access to an Amazon S3 bucket that is located in the same AWS account.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure manner?
explanation_en:
The correct way to grant any AWS permission to calculate resources is to use the role. The Lambda function takes an executing role and assigns an additional IAM policy to the s3: GetObject and s3:ListBucket privileges of a specific S3 bucket, with a specific prefix if required. The evidence involved is temporary: they are sent by STS, they are automatically refreshed and they will never be stored anywhere. The key phrase in the title is 'the safest way' - between a role being directed only at a single drum and a role being directed at all drums, the former being chosen because even in a single account, the principle of minimal authority applies.
Option A: A drum policy describes who can access the resource, but the function still requires its own identity and privileges. In individual accounts, this is usually handled by role rather than by open S3 buckets.
Option C: Access key embedded function code is a long-standing secret stored in the warehouse and deployment package and cannot be rotated automatically. This is the worst option.
Option D: Using the role is the right approach, but the permission is granted to each of the S3 buckets in the account. This is a violation of the principle of minimum competence, and the title requires the safest option.

options.text: Apply an S3 bucket policy that grants read access to the S3 bucket.
Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.
Embed an access key and a secret key in the Lambda function’s code to grant the required IAM permissions for read access to the S3 bucket.
Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to all S3 buckets in the account.

question_text:
A media company uses Amazon CloudFront for its publicly available streaming video content. The company wants to secure the video content that is hosted in Amazon S3 by controlling who has access. Some of the company’s users are using a custom HTTP client that does not support cookies. Some of the company’s users are unable to change the hardcoded URLs that they are using for access.
Which services or methods will meet these requirements with the LEAST impact to the users? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
This scenario hides two separate user restrictions, each of which has its own CloudFront solution. The client that does not support Cookie cannot use signature Cookie - for this type of user, signature URL is appropriate because the signature is directly in the link. URLs that are coded and unalterable cannot be switched to the signature URL - For such users, signature is more appropriate because the address remains unchanged and the signature is passed through the cookie header. Therefore, both mechanisms should be included in the answer: each has a minimum impact on serving a particular user group.
Option C: AWS AppSync is a hosting GraphQL API service. It has nothing to do with limiting access to the content of CloudFront.
Option D: JWT is not by itself an authorization mechanism for CloudFront - authentication of such tokens requires the preparation of the Lambda@Edge function. It's development work, not `minimal impact'.
Option E: Securitys Manager is used to store application keys. It does not manage access to video files.

question_text:
A company is preparing a new data platform that will ingest real-time streaming data from multiple sources. The company needs to transform the data before writing the data to Amazon S3. The company needs the ability to use SQL to query the transformed data.
Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
Three types of data are required: ingestion, conversion before writing, and ability to use SQL query results. Both possible combinations end with S3 and Athena. First: Kinesis Data Streams, Kinesis Data Analytics converts in real time, Firehose delivers the results to S3 (A). Second: Amazon MSK consumption data stream, AWS Glue executes conversion and writes data into S3 (B).

Option D: Data in S3 cannot be searched through the Amazon RDS query editor - the tool works on the database itself.
Option E: The same question as the RDS query editor, the tool cannot access objects in S3.

question_text:
A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached its end of life. The company wants to use AWS as part of a new backup solution and wants to maintain local access to all the data while it is backed up on AWS. The company wants to ensure that the data backed up on AWS is automatically and securely transferred.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
The key requirement is to maintain local access to all data, not just partial data. This is precisely what the storage gateway achieves in the memory scroll mode: the entire data set is kept on a local disk, while the snapshot is traveled and encrypted to S3. Backup has become automatic and access delays remain local.
Option A: Snowball is a one-time transmission device - it does not have a permanent S3 terminal to mount and does not provide automatic, continuous upload.
Option B: Snowball Edge is also designed for one-off transfers, not a durable backup solution.
Option C: Cache scroll mode keeps only part of the data locally, but requires local access to the entire volume.

options.text: Use AWS Snowball to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Configure on-premises systems to mount the Snowball S3 endpoint to provide local access to the data.
Use AWS Snowball Edge to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Use the Snowball Edge file interface to provide on-premises systems with local access to the data.

question_text:
An application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket. Traffic must not traverse the internet.
How should a solutions architect configure access to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
One requirement is that traffic should not go through the Internet. For S3, the gateway VPC terminal node needs to be used - adding the path to the VPC path table pointing to the service prefix, the traffic will be kept in the AWS network and the terminal node will not be expensive per se. In addition, S3 buckets can be restricted by the aws:sourceVpce condition so that they can only accept requests through the terminal node. The same techniques are described in question 91, 480 and 710.
Option A: A Route 53 private trust area is responsible for the definition of the name inside the VPC, without prejudice to the route to S3.
Option C: A NAT gateway is the path to the Internet - it is a direct violation of that requirement and will charge for the traffic processed.
Option D: A Site-to-Site VPN connects VPC to an external network instead of connecting to S3 services - no such construction exists.

options.text: Create a private hosted zone by using Amazon Route 53.

question_text:
An ecommerce company stores terabytes of customer data in the AWS Cloud. The data contains personally identifiable information (PII). The company wants to use the data in three applications. Only one of the applications needs to process the PII. The PII must be removed before the other two applications process the data.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
This is the same data, but different applications require different data views. S3 Subject Lambda can attach the function to the point of access: to convert objects in real time when the data returns, so that two applications get a version of the removed personal data, while a third application gets the original data. No additional copy of the data will appear, and all logics will be included in a single function.
Option A: A custom agent layer is an application that needs to be developed, extended and maintained.
Option C: Three data from too-bytes means three times the cost of storage and the continuing need for synchronization.
Option D: The same idea, but in DynamoDB, storage of toobytes is more expensive and data access needs to be redesigned.

options.text: Store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create a proxy application layer to intercept and process the data that each application requests.

question_text:
A development team has launched a new application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances inside a development VPC. A solutions architect needs to create a new VPC in the same account. The new VPC will be peered with the development VPC. The VPC CIDR block for the development VPC is 192.168.0.0/24. The solutions architect needs to create a CIDR block for the new VPC. The CIDR block must be valid for a VPC peering connection to the development VPC.
What is the SMALLEST CIDR block that meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
Two binding conditions apply. The address range of the equivalent VPC cannot overlap, so that 192.168.0.0/24 and any content within it are invalid. And the minimum permissible VPC address block is 28, so the /32 mask is invalid under any circumstances. Of the given options, only 10.0.0/24 remains.
Option A: A /32 mask specifies a single address - VPC cannot be created with this block; the minimum requirement is /28.
Option B: This section fully matches the block of the existing network, and an overlap of address ranges makes a reciprocal connection impossible.
Option C: Again is a 32 % mask, which is not valid for VPC and the address is also in the vicinity of the network.

question_text:
A company deploys an application on five Amazon EC2 instances. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributes traffic to the instances by using a target group. The average CPU usage on each of the instances is below 10% most of the time, with occasional surges to 65%.
A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to automate the scalability of the application. The solution must optimize the cost of the architecture and must ensure that the application has enough CPU resources when surges occur.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Examples already exist and load balancers and target groups are configured — what is required is automatic expansion without excessive payment. Created an automatic extension group, using the same load balancer and the same target group, and setting a target tracking strategy based on average CPU utilization: the capacity can increase to 65 percentage points in times of surge in traffic, and will fall back to a minimum during periods of calm.
Option A: A custom function that terminates an instance upon receiving a signal cannot achieve an extension and circumvents the standard extension mechanism.
Option C: Groups that do not set an expansion strategy maintain only a fixed number of examples and do not respond to surges in traffic.
Option D: Manual changes in the number of instances upon receipt of mail are not automated - automation is the function required.

question_text:
A company is running a critical business application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group and access an Amazon RDS DB instance.
The design did not pass an operational review because the EC2 instances and the DB instance are all located in a single Availability Zone. A solutions architect must update the design to use a second Availability Zone.
Which solution will make the application highly available?
explanation_en:
A subnet of AWS has always belonged to exactly one available area, so there is no subnet that crosses multiple available areas. The correct approach is to have a sub-network of one of the available areas, with the automatic extension group distributing the examples in two available areas, and the database being configured for deployment as a multi-usable area, with simultaneous copying and automatic failover.
Option A: The subnet is configured correctly, but the database is still located in a single available area — the `connection to each network' does not provide fault tolerance.
Option B: The subnet cannot cross two available areas and the database is once again a single point failure.
Option D: The same error across the subnet, although the database configuration is correct.

Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.

question_text:
A research laboratory needs to process approximately 8 TB of data. The laboratory requires sub-millisecond latencies and a minimum throughput of 6 GBps for the storage subsystem. Hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux will distribute and process the data.
Which solution will meet the performance requirements?
explanation_en:
Hard indicators have been specified: submarisecond delay and at least 6 GBps throughput, while hundreds of Linux examples are running. The performance configuration is fully compatible with Amazon FSx for Lustre, which is based on the persistence of SSD storage - it is the only option that can achieve these indicators. Source data are stored in S3 and linked to the file system through the import/export function, which facilitates both loading of data and preservation of results.

Option C: Persistence storage based on HDD disks cannot achieve submarisecond delay: mechanical hard drives are in essence slow.
Option D: Close the layer solves a problem, but the performance of ONTAP is still not up to the required target.

Create an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system. Set each volume’s tiering policy to NONE. Import the raw data into the file system. Mount the file system on the EC2 instances.

question_text:
A company needs to migrate a legacy application from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud because of hardware capacity constraints. The application runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. The application’s database storage continues to grow over time.

explanation_en:
The application continues to operate around the clock and database storage continues to grow over time. For a stable and constant load, the least costly option — up to three-quarters of the required price discount — is the case. Aurora also automatically expands its storage space, so that no manual intervention is required to cope with the increased storage demand, and Aurora retains examples that also reduce the cost of the data layer.

Option B: RDS examples, if required, are charged at full cost, even if they are constant and predictable.
Option D: Here the opposite is true: the discount is applicable to the database, but the largest level — the application — is still fully charged.

question_text:
A university research laboratory needs to migrate 30 TB of data from an on-premises Windows file server to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. The laboratory has a 1 Gbps network link that many other departments in the university share.
The laboratory wants to implement a data migration service that will maximize the performance of the data transfer. However, the laboratory needs to be able to control the amount of bandwidth that the service uses to minimize the impact on other departments. The data migration must take place within the next 5 days.
Which AWS solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
It takes about three days to reach the full load by a 30-byte link, so it is possible to reach the five-day window as long as the link is not fully occupied by other flows. The main requirement is to control bandwidth use, which is provided by AWS DataSync: a task can set bandwidth limits, transmit data through parallel streams, include completeness verification, and write directly to FSx for Windows File Server.
Option A: Snowcone can store only a few bytes - 30 TB requires more than one device and transport time will take up the deadline.
Option B: FSx File Gateway provides continuous access to the file system from the local network, but it is not a one-time migration tool with bandwidth control.
Option D: AWS Transport Family provides SFTP, FTPS and FTP services through S3 and EFS - it does not support bandwidth-restricted mass movements, nor does it write directly to FSx.

Amazon FSx File Gateway
AWS DataSync
AWS Transfer Family

question_text:
A company wants to create a mobile app that allows users to stream slow-motion video clips on their mobile devices. Currently, the app captures video clips and uploads the video clips in raw format into an Amazon S3 bucket. The app retrieves these video clips directly from the S3 bucket. However, the videos are large in their raw format.
Users are experiencing issues with buffering and playback on mobile devices. The company wants to implement solutions to maximize the performance and scalability of the app while minimizing operational overhead.
Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
There are two separate issues, each of which is resolved independently. The document is too large in its original form — it needs to be coded into formats and code rates suitable for mobile devices, and the managed Amazon Elastic Transcoder is designed for that purpose (C). The problem of delays and buffers for users around the globe was resolved through the margin cache, which meant the deployment of a Cloud Front distribution (A) in front of the drums.
Option B: Copying a file into a S3 bucket in other regions increases storage costs and requires a separate route logic, while CDN caches achieve the same result at a lower cost.
Option D: The use of customized case-based clusters for content distribution in local regions is an infrastructure that needs to be maintained, rather than a ready-made content distribution network.
Option E: Converting on self-managed examples means managing case clusters and queues rather than using managed transcode services.

options.text: Deploy Amazon CloudFront for content delivery and caching.

question_text:
A company is launching a new application deployed on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster and is using the Fargate launch type for ECS tasks. The company is monitoring CPU and memory usage because it is expecting high traffic to the application upon its launch. However, the company wants to reduce costs when utilization decreases.

These tasks are running on Fargate, so there are no examples that need to be expanded. The number of service assignments is controlled by AWS Application Auto Scaling: the target tracking strategy maintains a set CPU or memory utilization level, increases tasks at load peaks, removes tasks at load valleys - automatically reduces costs.

Option B: A custom function that adjusts the size of the service to a signal requires the preparation and maintenance of codes, while the built-in policy achieves the same function.
Option C: Again, expand the EC2 instance, which does not exist in this architecture.

options.text: Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to scale at certain periods based on previous traffic patterns.

question_text:

Between the two regions, large-scale two-way data cyclical transmissions between NFS file systems are typical examples of AWS DataSync missions. question_text:
A company is designing a shared storage solution for a gaming application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access data. The solution must be fully managed.
Which AWS solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
The request is simple and very clear: support SMB access and provide a fully hosted solution. This is Amazon FSx for Windows File Server -- a file system with original SMB, Windows ACL support and Active Directory integration, all managed by AWS. During the examination: SMB map to FSx for Windows, NFS map to EFS, object access through API map to S3, and the self-hosted file server running on EC2 violated the `full hosting' requirement.

Option D:S3 is an object storage that does not support SMB. A drum can only be mounted through a third-party tool and does not have the full syntax of the document.

options.text: Create an AWS DataSync task that shares the data as a mountable file system. Mount the file system to the application server.
Create an Amazon EC2 Windows instance. Install and configure a Windows file share role on the instance. Connect the application server to the file share.
Create an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Attach the file system to the origin server. Connect the application server to the file system.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Assign an IAM role to the application to grant access to the S3 bucket. Mount the S3 bucket to the application server.

question_text:
A company wants to run an in-memory database for a latency-sensitive application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes more than 100,000 transactions each minute and requires high network throughput. A solutions architect needs to provide a cost-effective network design that minimizes data transfer charges.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
The goal is to maximize network throughput, minimize delays and minimize data transmission costs. All of this comes from the placement of examples in a single available area within a cluster placement group: these machines will eventually be located in the same network segment and there will be no cost associated with the flow of private addresses within the same available area.
Option B: Different available areas mean data transfer costs and higher delays across the available areas, and the partition strategy is designed to distribute examples between aircraft shelves to achieve tolerance.
Option C: Re-integral distribution will introduce traffic across available areas, and network-based expansion will not meet the delay requirement.
Option D: The same cross-available area cost issue, and the stairwell extension is not related to network performance.

options.text: Launch all EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with cluster strategy when launching EC2 instances.
Launch all EC2 instances in different Availability Zones within the same AWS Region. Specify a placement group with partition strategy when launching EC2 instances.
Deploy an Auto Scaling group to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones based on a network utilization target.
Deploy an Auto Scaling group with a step scaling policy to launch EC2 instances in different Availability Zones.

question_text:
A company that primarily runs its application servers on premises has decided to migrate to AWS. The company wants to minimize its need to scale its Internet Small Computer Systems Interface (iSCSI) storage on premises.
The company wants only its recently accessed data to remain stored locally.
Which AWS solution should the company use to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Two words determine the answer. iSCSI means block access, so it is necessary to use Volume Gateway: S3 File Gateway to provide file access via NFS and SMB, Tape Gateway simulation tape library. "Reserve only recently visited data stored locally" points to volume mode: in a cache, the main data set is stored on AWS, while the local side keeps the cache of hotspots, so there is no need to expand local capacity. The repository is the opposite - the complete copy is kept locally and only the express notes are uploaded to AWS.
Option A: S3 File Gateway provides file access through NFS and SMB. It's not suitable for applications working through iSCSI.
Option B: Tape Gateway is the virtual tape library for backup. It is not stored for the daily running of applications.
Option C: Storage volumes keep complete copies of data locally, so the demand for local capacity remains unchanged. It is not possible to meet the requirement of minimizing local storage extension.

options.text: Amazon S3 File Gateway
AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway stored volumes
AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached volumes

question_text:
A company has multiple AWS accounts that use consolidated billing. The company runs several active high performance Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances for 90 days. The company’s finance team has access to AWS Trusted Advisor in the consolidated billing account and all other AWS accounts.
The finance team needs to use the appropriate AWS account to access the Trusted Advisor check recommendations for RDS. The finance team must review the appropriate Trusted Advisor check to reduce RDS costs.
Which combination of steps should the finance team take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
Original answer: BD; source correction answer: BC.
The examples are described as active, so running the "free database example" on these examples will not have any results from the inspection (D) - it looks for unconnected databases. A 90-day running example of cost reduction is precisely the function of "Amazon RDS preset example optimization" to check (C), while a preset example is recommended for aggregation in payment account (B)
Payer account for consolidation of bills can view Reserved Information Optimization; the example is running on-going and still using On-Demand, and should be checked for RDS Service Implementation, not Idle DB Standards. Source modified BD to BC, supported by official inspection instructions.
The example continues to run for 90 days, and therefore the cost savings arise from the conversion to a pre-encumbrance, which is precisely what the trusted consultant "Amazon RDS pre-encumbers" marked (C). You need to see (B) in the summary billing account: the recommendation to leave examples is to be calculated on an organization-wide basis, not in each individual account.
Option A: Recommendations from case-by-case operating accounts must be collected on an account-by-account basis, and the purchase of pre-encumbrance examples in this way will not allow for joint use across the organization.
Option D: "Examples of an empty database" check will search for unconnected databases in the last few days. The title made it clear that the examples were active and therefore the inspection would not mark them. This is an error in the source practice answer key.
Option E: Redshift prefix check applies to different services and is not related to RDS.

options.text: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the account where the RDS instances are running.
Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations from the consolidated billing account to see all RDS instance checks at the same time.
Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.
Review the Trusted Advisor check for Amazon Redshift Reserved Node Optimization.

question_text:
A solutions architect needs to optimize storage costs. The solutions architect must identify any Amazon S3 buckets that are no longer being accessed or are rarely accessed.
Which solution will accomplish this goal with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
S3 Storage Lens is an built-in storage analyser dashboard that shows the size and number of objects in all S3 buckets and also shows the frequency of access when advanced activity indicators are enabled. No configuration or manual analysis is required.
Option B: Standard S3 console displays the contents of the S3 buckets, but does not display aggregated access statistics.
Option C: The storage barrel size indicator reflects storage capacity rather than frequency of access and requires a separate analysis.
Option D: Enable object-level event logs in CloudTrail will significantly increase the volume of the logs and require the preparation of self-inquiries - with significant operating costs.

options.text: Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 Storage Lens dashboard for advanced activity metrics.
Analyze bucket access patterns by using the S3 dashboard in the AWS Management Console.
Turn on the Amazon CloudWatch BucketSizeBytes metric for buckets. Analyze bucket access patterns by using the metrics data with Amazon Athena.
Turn on AWS CloudTrail for S3 object monitoring. Analyze bucket access patterns by using CloudTrail logs that are integrated with Amazon CloudWatch Logs.

question_text:
A company sells datasets to customers who do research in artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML). The datasets are large, formatted files that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The company hosts a web application that the customers use to purchase access to a given dataset. The web application is deployed on multiple Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. After a purchase is made, customers receive an S3 signed URL that allows access to the files.
The customers are distributed across North America and Europe. The company wants to reduce the cost that is associated with data transfers and wants to maintain or improve performance.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The costs are derived from data transmission from S3 to clients in North America and Europe. The placement of Cloud Front in front of the S3 buckets reduces costs (ClaudFront's data transmission rate is below S3 direct transmission rate), while bringing the file closer to the user. Access controls are transferred to the URL for Cloud Front signature - the S3 signature URL is no longer applicable once the request has been circulated.
Option A: The speed of transmission will speed up the uploading of data to the S3 buckets, which is an additional cost: costs will increase, not decrease.
Option C: Cross-regional reproduction using a second drum doubles the storage costs for these large data sets and charges an additional cost for reproduction.
Option D: through the company ' s own application proxy data, increase the case load, maintain the same flow of outstations and increase the development workload.

options.text: Configure S3 Transfer Acceleration on the existing S3 bucket. Direct customer requests to the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.
Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the existing S3 bucket as the origin. Direct customer requests to the CloudFront URL. Switch to CloudFront signed URLs for access control.

Set up a second S3 bucket in the eu-central-1 Region with S3 Cross-Region Replication between the buckets. Direct customer requests to the closest Region. Continue to use S3 signed URLs for access control.

Modify the web application to enable streaming of the datasets to end users. Configure the web application to read the data from the existing S3 bucket. Implement access control directly in the application.

question_text:
A company is using AWS to design a web application that will process insurance quotes. Users will request quotes from the application. Quotes must be separated by quote type, must be responded to within 24 hours, and must not get lost. The solution must maximize operational efficiency and must minimize maintenance.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
Requests must be separated by type and must not be lost, and must be processed within 24 hours with minimal operating expenses. A SNS theme filters every message by type of attribute to its corresponding SQS queue, and each group of backend servers reads only its own queue. A maximum of 14 days ' notice is kept in line, so no information will be lost.
Option A: Multiple Kinesis streams need to manage fractions and create custom codes over KCL - operating costs are higher.
Option B: A SNS theme with a subscription function does not store messages: if processing fails, the request will be lost.
Option D: Firehose and an OpenSearch cluster form an analytical conduit rather than a task queue; it is highly impractical to process them by searching for messages in the index.

options.text: Create multiple Amazon Kinesis data streams based on the quote type. Configure the web application to send messages to the proper data stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to use the Kinesis Client Library (KCL) to pool messages from its own data stream.

Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for each quote type. Subscribe the Lambda function to its associated SNS topic. Configure the application to publish requests for quotes to the appropriate SNS topic.

Create a single Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues to the SNS topic. Configure SNS message filtering to publish messages to the proper SQS queue based on the quote type. Configure each backend application server to use its own SQS queue.

Create multiple Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams based on the quote type to deliver data streams to an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster. Configure the application to send messages to the proper delivery stream. Configure each backend group of application servers to search for the messages from OpenSearch Service and process them accordingly.

question_text:
A company has an application that runs on several Amazon EC2 instances. Each EC2 instance has multiple Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) data volumes attached to it. The application’s EC2 instance configuration and data need to be backed up nightly. The application also needs to be recoverable in a different AWS Region.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?
explanation_en:
The case configuration and the data on each additional volume need to be backed up and recovery must be done in different regions. AWS Backup can see EC2 instances as a single resource: backup includes case mirrors and all additional volumes. A backup plan with daily plans and cross-regional reproduction rules has been configured.
Option A: Customized snapshot functions mean the code, plan and error you need to maintain, and it is still unable to keep the case configuration.
Option C: If only a volume is added to the plan, the example configuration will not be backed up: you cannot restore the whole instance.
Option D: Copying to a different available area does not prevent faults at the regional level, and a custom function again means additional operating expenses.

options.text: Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application’s EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Region.
Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EC2 instances as resources.
Create a backup plan by using AWS Backup to perform nightly backups. Copy the backups to another Region. Add the application’s EBS volumes as resources.
Write an AWS Lambda function that schedules nightly snapshots of the application's EBS volumes and copies the snapshots to a different Availability Zone.

question_text:
A company is building a mobile app on AWS. The company wants to expand its reach to millions of users. The company needs to build a platform so that authorized users can watch the company’s content on their mobile devices.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Millions of mobile users, plus only authorized user access requirements, point to the use of CloudFront and signature URLs. After verifying user privileges, the application generates a signature URL with a limited validity period (optional attachment to IP address), content from the nearest edge node, and S3 bucket access control is restricted to direct access. Extension becomes the responsibility of the CDN, not your duty.
Option A: A public drum means open access to all, which contradicts the requirement of "authorized users". The KMS key itself does not "stream" anything -- that's the encryption key management service function.
Option B: Creating IPsec VPN for mobile applications running on millions of devices is not feasible at the technical and organizational levels and cannot solve the problem of video distribution.
Option D: Client VPN is designed to connect employees to the enterprise network, not to distribute content publicly to millions of viewers. Its cost and complexity are grossly incompatible with the mandate.

options.text: Publish content to a public Amazon S3 bucket. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to stream content.
Set up IPsec VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.
Use Amazon CloudFront. Provide signed URLs to stream content.
Set up AWS Client VPN between the mobile app and the AWS environment to stream content.

question_text:
A company has an on-premises MySQL database used by the global sales team with infrequent access patterns.
The sales team requires the database to have minimal downtime. A database administrator wants to migrate this database to AWS without selecting a particular instance type in anticipation of more users in the future.
Which service should a solutions architect recommend?
explanation_en:
The key phrase is "not to select a particular type of example". This is precisely the function provided by Aurora Servers for MySQL: the capacity is defined in the ACU range and is automatically extended to include new users upon arrival. The lower frequency of access makes it less expensive during free time, while MySQL compatibility remains the same.
Option A: A standard Aurora cluster requires the selection of an example category - which is in direct contradiction with the requirements.
Option C: Redshift Spectrum Reads data from S3 for analysis, not a transactional MySQL database.
Option D: RDS for MySQL also needs to select an example category and to expand manually when the load increases.

options.text: Amazon Aurora MySQL
Amazon Aurora Serverless for MySQL
Amazon Redshift Spectrum
Amazon RDS for MySQL

question_text:
A company experienced a breach that affected several applications in its on-premises data center. The attacker took advantage of vulnerabilities in the custom applications that were running on the servers. The company is now migrating its applications to run on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to implement a solution that actively scans for vulnerabilities on the EC2 instances and sends a report that details the findings.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The request is for a proactive scan of the cases and a report of the results of the scan — that is, Amazon Inspector. It carries out continuous scanning through SSM angent, matching installed software packages with CVE databases, assessing the network accessibility of each loophole and generating results of priority rankings, which can be exported and distributed. The difference to remember is that Inspector found a loophole, GuardDuty found signs of invasion, Macie found sensitive data, and Shield defended the DDoS attack.
Option A: AWS Shield protects against usable attacks and does not conduct any scanning at all.
Option B: Macie finds sensitive data in S3 instead of finding loopholes in the instance software.
Option C: GuardDuty detects suspicious activity and intrusion signs, but it does not generate a list of bug packages.

options.text: Deploy AWS Shield to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Create an AWS Lambda function to log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
Deploy Amazon Macie and AWS Lambda functions to scan the EC2 instances for vulnerabilities. Log any findings to AWS CloudTrail.
Turn on Amazon GuardDuty. Deploy the GuardDuty agents to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.
Turn on Amazon Inspector. Deploy the Amazon Inspector agent to the EC2 instances. Configure an AWS Lambda function to automate the generation and distribution of reports that detail the findings.

question_text:
A company uses an Amazon EC2 instance to run a script to poll for and process messages in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The company wants to reduce operational costs while maintaining its ability to process a growing number of messages that are added to the queue.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The script only rotated the queue and processed the message, but the example was continuously billed. The Lambda function, which uses SQS as the source of events, only runs when the message arrives, automatically expands as the number of messages increases, and is charged only on the basis of the time of execution.
Option A: Larger examples will speed up processing, but costs will increase rather than decrease.
Option B: The planned closure will result in messages not being processed within that time period and will require additional automated support.
Option D: Run Compand can run scripts as needed, but examples still exist and need to be billed.

options.text: Increase the size of the EC2 instance to process messages faster.
Use Amazon EventBridge to turn off the EC2 instance when the instance is underutilized.
Migrate the script on the EC2 instance to an AWS Lambda function with the appropriate runtime.
Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run the script on demand.

question_text:
A company uses a legacy application to produce data in CSV format. The legacy application stores the output data in Amazon S3. The company is deploying a new commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) application that can perform complex SQL queries to analyze data that is stored in Amazon Redshift and Amazon S3 only. However, the COTS application cannot process the .csv files that the legacy application produces.
The company cannot update the legacy application to produce data in another format. The company needs to implement a solution so that the COTS application can use the data that the legacy application produces.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The application can only work with Redshift and S3, but the data arrives in CSV format. A planned AWS Glue operation reads, converts and loads these files into Redshift - an ETL tool of the type, without a custom code or cluster management.
Option B: A custom script running on an EC2 instance means that it needs to be developed and maintained, and.sql files are not suitable for the application in any case.
Option C: DynamoDB is not within the data source supported by the application: cannot run a SQL query on it.
Option D: Creating an EMR cluster every week means additional delay and nodal management, while costs are higher.

options.text: Create an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job that runs on a schedule. Configure the ETL job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in Amazon Redshift.
Develop a Python script that runs on Amazon EC2 instances to convert the .csv files to .sql files. Invoke the Python script on a cron schedule to store the output files in Amazon S3.

Create an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB table. Use an S3 event to invoke the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in the DynamoDB table.

Use Amazon EventBridge to launch an Amazon EMR cluster on a weekly schedule. Configure the EMR cluster to perform an extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to process the .csv files and store the processed data in an Amazon Redshift table.

question_text:
A company recently migrated its entire IT environment to the AWS Cloud. The company discovers that users are provisioning oversized Amazon EC2 instances and modifying security group rules without using the appropriate change control process. A solutions architect must devise a strategy to track and audit these inventory and configuration changes.
Which actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
There are two stand-alone needs, which are met by two stand-alone services. AWS CloudTrail records who called which API and when - for example, who initiated a mega-example or modified the Security Group Rules (A). AWS Config tracks the history of resource allocation and allows you to define compliance rules to mark violations - for example, the type of prohibited example or overly liberal rule (D).
Option B: Data life-cycle strategy to manage snapshots and mirrors, rather than change audits.
Option C: Trusted Advisor provides general advice on account configuration, but it does not record a change in history or enforce compliance rules.
Option E: CloudFormation can deploy infrastructure, but it is not a tool for auditing or rolling back any changes.

options.text: Enable AWS CloudTrail and use it for auditing.
Use data lifecycle policies for the Amazon EC2 instances.
Enable AWS Trusted Advisor and reference the security dashboard.
Enable AWS Config and create rules for auditing and compliance purposes.
Restore previous resource configurations with an AWS CloudFormation template.

question_text:
A company has hundreds of Amazon EC2 Linux-based instances in the AWS Cloud. Systems administrators have used shared SSH keys to manage the instances. After a recent audit, the company’s security team is mandating the removal of all shared keys. A solutions architect must design a solution that provides secure access to the EC2 instances.
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of administrative overhead?
explanation_en:
Shared SSH keys need to be removed while maintaining access rights. Session Manager achieves this by not having to use a single key and not having to open the port: the proxy on the example will initiate an out-link to the service, the permission will be given through the IAM policy description, the operation will be assigned to a specific user, the session will be recorded in Cloudwatch Logs or S3. The example only requires a role with AmazonSSMManaged InstanceCore. Management costs are minimal: no jumper, no key distribution, no address list.
Option B: STS sends temporary AWS certificates instead of SSH keys. There is no such mechanism.
Option C: Use a shared key jumper does not solve the problem: shared key still exists, but in fewer numbers.
Option D: Comnito is a self-study system built around the key in combination with a custom key generation function - this is exactly what the company wants to eliminate.

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to the EC2 instances.
Use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to generate one-time SSH keys on demand.
Allow shared SSH access to a set of bastion instances. Configure all other instances to allow only SSH access from the bastion instances.
Use an Amazon Cognito custom authorizer to authenticate users. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate a temporary SSH key.

question_text:
A company is using a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances to ingest data from on-premises data sources. The data is in JSON format and ingestion rates can be as high as 1 MB/s. When an EC2 instance is rebooted, the data in-flight is lost. The company’s data science team wants to query ingested data in near-real time.
Which solution provides near-real-time data querying that is scalable with minimal data loss?
explanation_en:
The problem is that the instant data of the case restart is lost because the data only exists in the memory and disk of the case. Kinesis Data Teams receives records and stores them in streams, not related to consumer status, so restarting does not result in any data being lost, and Kinesis Data Analytics allows you to search data near real time.
Option B: Firehose cache data is transmitted to Redshift with tens of seconds or more delay: this is no longer near real time and the cache itself may be lost if the source fails.
Option C: Store the ingestion data in case storage will keep the original problem: all data will disappear when the example is restarted.
Option D: EBS Volumes and Redis Channels constitute a self-building programme, without assurance of delivery and without easy access to ingestion methods.

options.text: Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Use Kinesis Data Analytics to query the data.
Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon Redshift as the destination. Use Amazon Redshift to query the data.
Store ingested data in an EC2 instance store. Publish data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose with Amazon S3 as the destination. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
Store ingested data in an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Publish data to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Subscribe to the Redis channel to query the data.

question_text: What should a solutions architect do to ensure that all objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket are encrypted?
explanation_en:
You need to make sure that unencrypted objects don't go into the drums at all, rather than repair the problem after the fact. This is achieved by a storage barrel strategy that explicitly refuses to perform s3:PutObject operations if the request lacks x-amz-server-side-encryption headers (or its value does not meet the requirements - for example, is not an aws:kms). This refusal triggers before writing: the client will receive an AccessDenied error and must retransmit a request containing encryption. Remember the difference: the default encryption encrypts all data that arrives, while the rejection policy explicitly requires the client to request encryption in visible form.
Option A: Access control list for x-amz-acl header-set objects. It has nothing to do with encryption.
Option B: The same question: the pprivate value limits who can see the object, but the object may still be written unencrypted.
Option C:aws: SecureTransport condition requires TLS, which is the encryption during the transfer. Data will reach through secure connections, but it may still be written on disks in unencrypted form — an issue that concerns static encryption.

options.text: Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set.
Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an s3:x-amz-acl header set to private.
Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an aws:SecureTransport header set to true.
Update the bucket policy to deny if the PutObject does not have an x-amz-server-side-encryption header set.

question_text:
A solutions architect is designing a multi-tier application for a company. The application's users upload images from a mobile device. The application generates a thumbnail of each image and returns a message to the user to confirm that the image was uploaded successfully.
The thumbnail generation can take up to 60 seconds, but the company wants to provide a faster response time to its users to notify them that the original image was received. The solutions architect must design the application to asynchronously dispatch requests to the different application tiers.
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Users need to respond immediately, and the generation of thumbnails may take up to one minute. The SQS queue addresses this problem: applications release news about new pictures and immediately confirm uploading, while processors generate thumbnails at their own pace to ensure that tasks are not lost.
Option A: A function that generates both thumbnails and informs the user leaves 60 seconds of waiting time on the response path.
Option B: Step Forces coordinates the steps, but the user notification is tied to the generation and the design is more complex.
Option D: SNS does not store messages: if the subscriber fails, the thumbnail generation task will be lost.

options.text: Write a custom AWS Lambda function to generate the thumbnail and alert the user. Use the image upload process as an event source to invoke the Lambda function.
Create an AWS Step Functions workflow. Configure Step Functions to handle the orchestration between the application tiers and alert the user when thumbnail generation is complete.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) message queue. As images are uploaded, place a message on the SQS queue for thumbnail generation. Alert the user through an application message that the image was received.

Create Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification topics and subscriptions. Use one subscription with the application to generate the thumbnail after the image upload is complete. Use a second subscription to message the user's mobile app by way of a push notification after thumbnail generation is complete.

question_text:
A company’s facility has badge readers at every entrance throughout the building. When badges are scanned, the readers send a message over HTTPS to indicate who attempted to access that particular entrance.
