question_text:
A company stores raw collected data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data is used for several types of analytics on behalf of the company's customers. The type of analytics requested determines the access pattern on the S3 objects.
The company cannot predict or control the access pattern. The company wants to reduce its S3 costs.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The key phrase is "unforeseeable or controlled access patterns": access patterns are set by the client according to the type of analysis that he or she orders. Any situation requiring speculation as to the age of the subject or payment of search costs would be disadvantageous here. The intelligent layer moves its own objects between different levels based on actual access and is free of search charges, so unexpected requests for analysis do not result in a sudden increase in bills.
Option A: The copy will copy the object to another S3 bucket instead of changing the storage category of the existing object. Under this setting, you need to pay for two copies, not save costs.
Option B: The transition to Standard Archive (Standard-IA) by age is premised on the fact that objects are no longer read after N days. It was requested that this be made clear that this was unpredictable and that every visit to an archive would be charged.
Option D: S3 dashboard is a report - it does not move objects; moving objects is still a task for life cycle rules. In addition, manual analysis of access patterns repeats work already done automatically by the intelligent stratification.

options.text: Use S3 replication to transition infrequently accessed objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA)
Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard- IA)
Use S3 Lifecycle rules to transition objects from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering
Use S3 Inventory to identify and transition objects that have not been accessed from S3 Standard to S3 Intelligent-Tiering

question_text:
A company has applications hosted on Amazon EC2 instances with IPv6 addresses. The applications must initiate communications with other external applications using the internet. However the company’s security policy states that any external service cannot initiate a connection to the EC2 instances.
What should a solutions architect recommend to resolve this issue?
explanation_en:
These addresses are IPv6, which requires an outward connection and is prohibited from being internal. This is precisely the purpose of the stand-alone Internet gateway: it allows traffic to be initiated from within and to respond through the state of the connection, but does not allow any connection to be opened from outside.
Option A: A NAT gateway only applies to IPv4; it does not apply to IPv6.
Option B: A conventional Internet gateway is two-way: external services can initiate connections to examples.
Option C: A virtual private gateway is a connection point for VPN and Direct Contact - it has nothing to do with Internet access.

options.text: Create a NAT gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
Create an internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
Create a virtual private gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table
Create an egress-only internet gateway and make it the destination of the subnet's route table

question_text:
A company is creating an application that runs on containers in a VPC. The application stores and accesses data in an Amazon S3 bucket. During the development phase, the application will store and access 1 TB of data in Amazon S3 each day. The company wants to minimize costs and wants to prevent traffic from traversing the internet whenever possible.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
There are two requirements: to keep traffic outside the public Internet and to avoid unnecessary costs associated with 1 TB per day. The VPC terminal of the S3 gateway will add a route to the VPC's path chart, so traffic will be transmitted through the AWS internal network — crucially, the terminal node is free of charge per se, regardless of the amount of data it contains. The interface terminal is also private, but charges are charged for each available area per hour as well as for each processing byte: the flow of 1 TB per day will incur significant costs. Remember the difference: the gateway terminal is only available for S3 and DynamoDB and is completely free of charge, and all other services must be accessed through the interface terminal.
Option A: Storage classes change storage costs rather than flow paths. The requirement to keep data outside the Internet cannot be met.
Option B: The S3 Transfer Acceleration function is the opposite: it links traffic routes to the global peripheral network with additional fees. This is not only more expensive but also less private.
Option D: The interface terminal does address privacy requirements, but it is charged per hour of available area and per gigabyte, and therefore costs more than a free gateway terminal per day in traffic with 1 TB. In addition, interface terminal nodes are created in the subnet and are associated with the security group, not "connected to the route sheet" — this connection is the way the gateway terminal nodes work.

options.text: Enable S3 Intelligent-Tiering for the S3 bucket
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for the S3 bucket
Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Associate this endpoint with all route tables in the VPC
Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. Associate this endpoint with all route tables in the VPC

question_text:
A company has a mobile chat application with a data store based in Amazon DynamoDB. Users would like new messages to be read with as little latency as possible. A solutions architect needs to design an optimal solution that requires minimal application changes.
Which method should the solutions architect select?
explanation_en:
The demand is for minimal reading delays for new messages and for as few changes as possible for applications. DAX is the built-in memory cache of DynamoDB, with a data response time at the microsecond level; it is compatible with the same API, so the change relates only to the end-point address that is replaced by the end-point address of the DAX cluster.
Option B: DynamoDB does not read a copy: Read the extension through capacity, global tables or DAX.
Option C: Double the reading capacity unit to eliminate the restricted flow, but the response time is still at msi - no delay to improve.
Option D: Redis Cache can provide a low delay, but it needs to achieve its own Cache Loading and Validation logic in the code, which means that a major application change is required.

options.text: Configure Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for the new messages table. Update the code to use the DAX endpoint.
Add DynamoDB read replicas to handle the increased read load. Update the application to point to the read endpoint for the read replicas.
Double the number of read capacity units for the new messages table in DynamoDB. Continue to use the existing DynamoDB endpoint.
Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache to the application stack. Update the application to point to the Redis cache endpoint instead of DynamoDB.

question_text: A company hosts a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website serves static content. Website traffic is increasing, and the company is concerned about a potential increase in cost.
explanation_en:
The website provides static content and traffic is growing, resulting in the cost of data transmission regions and of handling instances of duplicate requests. CloudFront solves these two problems: the file is cached at the edge, so repeated requests will never reach the load balancer or instance, and the cost of transmitting data externally via CloudFront is lower than the cost of transmitting data directly from EC2. It also reduces delays in remote user access.
Option B: ElastiCache is a cache used for application data (sessions, query results) rather than providing files to clients. The load balancer cannot provide content from ElastiCache.
Option C: AWS WAF filtering requests without caches - it does not have this function.
Option D: The deployment of a second load balancer in another area means that the entire infrastructure needs to be replicated and that it does not reduce the cost of providing static content.

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache state files at edge locations
Create an Amazon ElastiCache cluster. Connect the ALB to the ElastiCache cluster to serve cached files
Create an AWS WAF web ACL and associate it with the ALB. Add a rule to the web ACL to cache static files
Create a second ALB in an alternative AWS Region. Route user traffic to the closest Region to minimize data transfer costs

question_text:
A company has multiple VPCs across AWS Regions to support and run workloads that are isolated from workloads in other Regions. Because of a recent application launch requirement, the company’s VPCs must communicate with all other VPCs across all Regions.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of administrative effort?
explanation_en:
There are multiple VPCs across regions, and all VPCs need to be connected to each other and must minimize their costs. Transit Gateway serves as the central router in the region: each VPC is connected by a single connection and the number of connections increases linearly. Between regions, the gateway is interconnected through the transmission gateway peer-to-peering. The minimum number of objects to be configured is managed by the route chart of the gateway.
Option A: The network structure of a reciprocal connection is growing twice: for n networks, you need n multiplied by (n minus I) divided by two links, and each route sheet will eventually contain an entry for each partner. This is difficult to manage and reciprocal connections do not support transmission routes.
Option B: Direct Connect gateway is used to connect local data centres to VPC - it does not provide connectivity between VPCs.
Option D: PrivateLink publishes a single service by an endpoint and provides one-way access instead of full network connectivity between all VPCs.

options.text: Use VPC peering to manage VPC communication in a single Region. Use VPC peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
Use AWS Direct Connect gateways across all Regions to connect VPCs across regions and manage VPC communications.
Use AWS Transit Gateway to manage VPC communication in a single Region and Transit Gateway peering across Regions to manage VPC communications.
Use AWS PrivateLink across all Regions to connect VPCs across Regions and manage VPC communications

question_text:
A company is designing a containerized application that will use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).
The application needs to access a shared file system that is highly durable and can recover data to another AWS Region with a recovery point objective (RPO) of 8 hours. The file system needs to provide a mount target m each Availability Zone within a Region.
A solutions architect wants to use AWS Backup to manage the replication to another Region.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
There are three requirements: each available area must have a file system that mounts the target, is highly persistent, and is copied to another area by AWS Backup, RPO is 8 hours. Amazon EFS meets all requirements by using standard storage categories: data are stored between multiple available areas, each region creates a mounted target, and AWS Backup can copy an EFS backup to another region according to the plan.
Option A: FSx for Windows File Server uses the SMB protocol to deploy only one active endpoint in a multi-usable area instead of having a mounted target in each area.
Option B: FSx for NetApp ONTAP also has only one active endpoint for access in multi-usable area deployment, instead of having a stand-alone mounted target for each available area.
Option D: FSx for OpenZFS is deployed in a single available area and therefore cannot meet the availability requirements.

options.text: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server with a Multi-AZ deployment
Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP with a Multi-AZ deployment
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with the Standard storage class
Amazon FSx for OpenZFS

question_text:
A company is expecting rapid growth in the near future. A solutions architect needs to configure existing users and grant permissions to new users on AWS. The solutions architect has decided to create IAM groups. The solutions architect will add the new users to IAM groups based on department.
Which additional action is the MOST secure way to grant permissions to the new users?
explanation_en:
The authority in IAM is granted by strategy, and the group exists to allow a strategy to be added to the entire sector once and for all. Once the new employee joins the group, the corresponding rights set is automatically obtained, and the change of strategy is immediately effective for all. Roles do not apply to this scenario: roles cannot be added to the group — roles are assumed by the subject through AssumeRole, not through membership in the group. The principle of minimal authority is derived from the content of the strategy itself: it only contains the operations required for the required resources.
Option A: SCPs is an organizational-level tool to limit the maximum privileges available in the account. They themselves do not grant any privileges, so the new users will still not have any.
Option B: Roles cannot be added to the IAM group: Roles are assumed by the subject through AssumeRole, not through membership in the group.
Option D: The permission boundary sets a ceiling on the authority that a user or character can be granted, but it does not in itself grant any authority. In the absence of a strategy, there would be virtually no authority.

options.text: Apply service control policies (SCPs) to manage access permissions
Create IAM roles that have least privilege permission. Attach the roles to the IAM groups
Create an IAM policy that grants least privilege permission. Attach the policy to the IAM groups
Create IAM roles. Associate the roles with a permissions boundary that defines the maximum permissions

question_text:
A law firm needs to share information with the public. The information includes hundreds of files that must be publicly readable. Modifications or deletions of the files by anyone before a designated future date are prohibited.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure way?
explanation_en:
Two requirements are in the opposite direction: the document must be publicly readable, but not subject to modification until a date has been set. Open access is derived from the storage barrel policy, which grants the s3: GetObject permission to anonymous requests (usually used in conjunction with static web hosting), while non-variability is derived from the S3 object lock, which sets a target date for its retention period and is built on the version control. A key detail excludes half the option: access to anonymous readers is controlled by the storage barrel strategy, not by IAM: the public has no AWS account to grant any privileges.
Option A: IAM permissions apply only to AWS subjects, and `public' is not one of them: documents are either never accessible or become accessible through completely different mechanisms. And there is no protection against modification at all.
Option C: A function that is restored from the backup after the object has been modified is a reaction after the event. The requirement is that the modification should not have occurred in the first place.
Option D: The object is locked on the S3 bucket level (and a version control is required) - you cannot select a `folder ' and only protect the folder. Besides, it's once again making an IAM error about anonymous readers.

options.text: Upload all files to an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for static website hosting. Grant read-only IAM permissions to any AWS principals that access the S3 bucket until the designated date.

Create a new Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Use S3 Object Lock with a retention period in accordance with the designated date. Configure the S3 bucket for static website hosting. Set an S3 bucket policy to allow read-only access to the objects.

Create a new Amazon S3 bucket with S3 Versioning enabled. Configure an event trigger to run an AWS Lambda function in case of object modification or deletion. Configure the Lambda function to replace the objects with the original versions from a private S3 bucket.

Upload all files to an Amazon S3 bucket that is configured for static website hosting. Select the folder that contains the files. Use S3 Object Lock with a retention period in accordance with the designated date. Grant read-only IAM permissions to any AWS principals that access the S3 bucket.

question_text:
A company is making a prototype of the infrastructure for its new website by manually provisioning the necessary infrastructure. This infrastructure includes an Auto Scaling group, an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon RDS database. After the configuration has been thoroughly validated, the company wants the capability to immediately deploy the infrastructure for development and production use in two Availability Zones in an automated fashion.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
A prototype built manually needs to be re deployable. AWS ClaudFormation describes the entire infrastructure in the form of a template: Auto-extend groups, load balancers and databases are created in one operation and consistent development and production environments are deployed using the same template using different parameters.
Option A: Systems Manager manages existing resources and does not describe infrastructure in the form of infrastructure, i.e. code.
Option C: AWSConfig records configuration and check compliance, but it does not create anything.
Option D: Elastic Beanstalk uses its own platform template to deploy applications and cannot copy any existing infrastructure.

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager to replicate and provision the prototype infrastructure in two Availability Zones
Define the infrastructure as a template by using the prototype infrastructure as a guide. Deploy the infrastructure with AWS CloudFormation.
Use AWS Config to record the inventory of resources that are used in the prototype infrastructure. Use AWS Config to deploy the prototype infrastructure into two Availability Zones.
Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk and configure it to use an automated reference to the prototype infrastructure to automatically deploy new environments in two Availability Zones.

question_text:
A business application is hosted on Amazon EC2 and uses Amazon S3 for encrypted object storage. The chief information security officer has directed that no application traffic between the two services should traverse the public internet.
Which capability should the solutions architect use to meet the compliance requirements?
explanation_en:
This requires that traffic between EC2 and S3 should not go through the public Internet. Only the VPC terminal node can change the path - for S3, it is usually a free gateway node, which adds to the route list a path pointing to the prefix for service in the AWS network. Encryption, subnet type and gateways to local networks have no impact on this path. Access is usually further limited by the ows:sourceVpce condition in the storage barrel strategy.
Option A: KMS Encryption Object, but does not change the path of the package: the encrypted data will still pass the S3 public terminal node.
Option C: Where there is no terminal node for an example located in a private subnet, access to S3 through the NAT gateway - that is, via the Internet. Private subnets themselves cannot meet this requirement.
Option D: Virtual private gateway is the connection point of the VPC to the local network via VPN or DirectConect. It has nothing to do with the request to S3.

options.text: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS)
VPC endpoint
Private subnet
Virtual private gateway

question_text:
A company hosts a three-tier web application in the AWS Cloud. A Multi-AZAmazon RDS for MySQL server forms the database layer Amazon ElastiCache forms the cache layer. The company wants a caching strategy that adds or updates data in the cache when a customer adds an item to the database. The data in the cache must always match the data in the database.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Requires a written statement: data must enter the cache immediately upon writing and the cache must always be consistent with the database. This is the policy of writing penetrating — the application updates the database and caches at the same time as each writing, and therefore does not have obsolete values.
Option A: Lazy loads the data into the cache only when the reading is missing, so the cache lags behind the database between writing and first reading.
Option C: TTL limits the duration of the difference, but it does not eliminate the difference or update the cache when the data is added.
Option D: AWS AppConfig Distribution Application Configuration Parameter is not a data cache policy.

options.text: Implement the lazy loading caching strategy
Implement the write-through caching strategy
Implement the adding TTL caching strategy
Implement the AWS AppConfig caching strategy

question_text:
A company wants to migrate 100 GB of historical data from an on-premises location to an Amazon S3 bucket. The company has a 100 megabits per second (Mbps) internet connection on premises. The company needs to encrypt the data in transit to the S3 bucket. The company will store new data directly in Amazon S3.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
Reference answer: B; dispute option: A.
100 GB via 100 Mbps links, only plain aws s3 sync via TLS, without any component deployment, which takes approximately 2.5 hours; DataSync needs to deploy and maintain an agent, but at the cost of exchange data integrity verification and automatic re-try failure transmission - "Minimal operating costs"
100 GB is available online via the 100 Mbps link; AWS CLI aws s3 sync defaults on HTTPS/TLS and does not require the deployment of DataSync anent. The drying will be at the least operational instead of continuous synchronization or complex validation, as old B becomes A; the actual network time is still dependent on the bandwidth available.
Source answer B's original resolution (in conflict with verification results, not accepted):
This question has been marked as controversial: both reasonable options meet the requirements, and everything depends on how you understand the "minimum operating cost". Mathematical calculations show that the link is fast enough: 100 GBs are connected to 100 Mbps for approximately 2.5 hours, so no offline transmission is required. Encryption during transmission is from TLS, which is provided in both ways. Amended key option is AWS DataSync: The agent divides the transmission into parallel streams, retests failed data blocks and validates data integrity on its own. The reason for selecting aws s3 sync is that it is a single order and does not require the deployment of any component, while DataSync implies the deployment and operation of an agent to perform a one-time task. Practically practical principles are: selection of DataSync for duplicate or large-scale transmissions that need to be verified; selection of CLI for a single copy of several dozen to several hundred GB data.
Source old option A: A powerful choice: the aws s3 sync command runs via HTTPS, uploads the partitions and does not require the deployment of any components. The weakness is the lack of data integrity checks and automatic retesting functionality embedded in DataSync.
Source old option C: AWS Snowball is an offline transfer method for the transmission of 100 GB data that could have been transmitted through the network within hours. The process of ordering, waiting, copying and sending back equipment is a disproportionate effort.
Source old option D:IPsec VPN adds an additional layer of encryption to the secure TLS connection (S3) that requires setting up and maintaining a tunnel. This is an additional component, with no real gain.

options.text: Use the s3 sync command in the AWS CLI to move the data directly to an S3 bucket
Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data from the on-premises location to an S3 bucket
Use AWS Snowball to move the data to an S3 bucket
Set up an IPsec VPN from the on-premises location to AWS. Use the s3 cp command in the AWS CLI to move the data directly to an S3 bucket

question_text:
A company containerized a Windows job that runs on .NET 6 Framework under a Windows container. The company wants to run this job in the AWS Cloud. The job runs every 10 minutes. The job’s runtime varies between 1 minute and 3 minutes.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The operation was short and operated every 10 minutes and was packed in Windows containers. Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate supports Windows packagings, which allow you to create a planned task: starting the container, running it for one to three minutes, then terminating it, so you pay only for running time, without managing the server.
Option A: AWS Lambda cannot run Windows packagings: mirrors based on Linux are only supported.
Option B: AWS Watch does not support Windows containers on the Fargate resource, so the operation will not be able to run.
Option D: Windows task plan programs are running inside the operating system, and in the Fargate start-up type, there is no bottom machine available to run it.

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function based on the container image of the job. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the function every 10 minutes.
Use AWS Batch to create a job that uses AWS Fargate resources. Configure the job scheduling to run every 10 minutes.
Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate to run the job. Create a scheduled task based on the container image of the job to run every 10 minutes.

Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate to run the job. Create a standalone task based on the container image of the job. Use Windows task scheduler to run the job every 10 minutes.

question_text:
A company wants to move from many standalone AWS accounts to a consolidated, multi-account architecture. The company plans to create many new AWS accounts for different business units. The company needs to authenticate access to these AWS accounts by using a centralized corporate directory service.
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
It is a two-step mission. First step, migrate to a multi-account architecture: create an organization in AWS Organizations and activate all functionality to enable SCP and centralized management to be available and then create a new account (A) in it. The second step is to provide single-point login through the existing catalogue of enterprises: to use AWS IAM Infrastructure Center as a source of identity and to allocate privileges to the account (E). Users use their business certificates to log in and obtain a temporary role in the respective accounts.
Option B: Amazon Cognito is designed for application end-users, not for employees. IAM Identity Center does not accept Cognito as a source of corporate identity.
Option C: SCP is used to control limits, not authentication, and the order "Add the IAM effectiveness Center to AWS Directory Service" is reversed: the directory is connected to Identity Center as its identity source, not the other way around.
Option D: There is no authentication mechanism for the organization itself: The login is configured in IAM Infrastructure Center, while the Organizations are responsible for the account structure and policy.

options.text: Create a new organization in AWS Organizations with all features turned on. Create the new AWS accounts in the organization.
Set up an Amazon Cognito identity pool. Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to accept Amazon Cognito authentication.
Configure a service control policy (SCP) to manage the AWS accounts. Add AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to AWS Directory Service.
Create a new organization in AWS Organizations. Configure the organization's authentication mechanism to use AWS Directory Service directly.
Set up AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) in the organization. Configure IAM Identity Center, and integrate it with the company's corporate directory service.

question_text:
A company is looking for a solution that can store video archives in AWS from old news footage. The company needs to minimize costs and will rarely need to restore these files. When the files are needed, they must be available in a maximum of five minutes.
What is the MOST cost-effective solution?
explanation_en:
Two factors determine the solution to this problem: access is very rare and cannot be retrieved for more than five minutes. The live access category (IA) meets the time requirement, but is too costly for data that have been idle for a long time, while the S3 Glacier Deep Archive does not meet the five-minute window requirement. Therefore, only S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval will be available for urgent search: while urgent search can return archived data within 1-5 minutes, standard search takes 3-5 hours. You will only pay for the urgent search when data are actually needed, while storage costs for the rest of the time will be charged at the filing rate.
Option B: Standard search from S3 Glacier takes 3-5 hours, which is contrary to the "up to five minutes" requirement.
Option C: S3 Standard-IA can return the object immediately, but its storage cost is about three times that of S3 Glacier. Given the minimal cost and the rare nature of the recovery, it would be unreasonable to pay a premium for a quick visit that could take place only once a year.
Option D: S3 One Zone-IA is cheaper than S3 Standard-IA, but its storage costs are still higher than S3 Glacier, and only a copy is kept in a single area available - a questionable trade-off for news video archiving.

options.text: Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Glacier and use Expedited retrievals.
Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Glacier and use Standard retrievals.
Store the video archives in Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).
Store the video archives in Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA).

question_text:
A company is building a three-tier application on AWS. The presentation tier will serve a static website The logic tier is a containerized application. This application will store data in a relational database. The company wants to simplify deployment and to reduce operational costs.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The requirement is simple: simple deployment and low operating costs. S3 Host static content without servers; run ECS examples on Fargate to host logical layer packagings without managing any nodes; and a hosted RDS cluster to store data. Each level is chosen to ensure that there is no infrastructure that needs to be maintained.
Option B: CloudFront does not itself store content -- it needs a source -- running ECS on an EC2 instance would reintroduce node management problems.
Option C: Amazon EKS needs to manage the Kubernetes cluster and has a higher cost than ECS for the same load - adding complexity, but no benefit.
Option D: Hosting static content on preset cases is the most costly and labour-intensive of these options.

options.text: Use Amazon S3 to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
Use Amazon CloudFront to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
Use Amazon S3 to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.
Use Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances to host static content. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 for compute power. Use a managed Amazon RDS cluster for the database.

question_text:
A company seeks a storage solution for its application. The solution must be highly available and scalable. The solution also must function as a file system be mountable by multiple Linux instances in AWS and on premises through native protocols, and have no minimum size requirements. The company has set up a Site-to-Site VPN for access from its on-premises network to its VPC.
Which storage solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
Collection needs: A file system that can be mounted from AWS and local networks (through the configured VPN) using primary tools, with no minimum size requirements and extended and highly usable. This is precisely what Amazon EFS has achieved with its mounted target in multiple available areas: each mount target serves the client in its available area, while the local Linux server uses the NFS to mount the file system through the tunnel.
Option A: Amazon FSx family for SMB, Lustre, ONTAP or OpenZFS construction, which, as described, does not meet the original mounted requirements from Linux instance and does not have a minimum size.
Option B: Amazon EBS Multi-Attach only allows the attachment of volumes to multiple examples within a single area of availability and requires a cluster perception file system, which cannot be accessed at all from the local network.
Option D: A single mounted target means that the client in the other available area must pass through the target route, making the target area a single point failure. Access points manage privileges, but they are not a substitute for mounted targets.

options.text: Amazon FSx Multi-AZ deployments
Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach volumes
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with multiple mount targets
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) with a single mount target and multiple access points

question_text:
A 4-year-old media company is using the AWS Organizations all features feature set to organize its AWS accounts.
According to the company's finance team, the billing information on the member accounts must not be accessible to anyone, including the root user of the member accounts.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
This is a strict requirement: billing information must be unaccessible to any person in a member ' s account, including its root user. The IAM strategy has nothing to do here — they have no influence on the root users of the accounts. The only mechanism that can limit the user base of a member ' s account is to attach a service control policy (SCP) to the root of the organization or to the related organizational unit (OU): the policy sets a maximum limit for each subject in the account. SCP will reject operations such as aws-portal:* (or account: GetAccountInformation and related billing operations).
Option A: The AWS managed billing strategy grants access, but requires the opposite — access needs to be blocked. The strategy also has no impact on the root users of member accounts.
Option B: Identity-based strategies do not apply to root users: only SCPs from organizations can limit root users.
Option D: Switching to a unified billing functional set would deprive the organization of SCP and other governance tools, making the situation worse than solving the problem.

options.text: Add all finance team users to an IAM group. Attach an AWS managed policy named Billing to the group.
Attach an identity-based policy to deny access to the billing information to all users, including the root user.
Create a service control policy (SCP) to deny access to the billing information. Attach the SCP to the root organizational unit (OU).
Convert from the Organizations all features feature set to the Organizations consolidated billing feature set.

question_text:
An ecommerce company runs an application in the AWS Cloud that is integrated with an on-premises warehouse solution. The company uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send order messages to an on-premises HTTPS endpoint so the warehouse application can process the orders. The local data center team has detected that some of the order messages were not received.
A solutions architect needs to retain messages that are not delivered and analyze the messages for up to 14 days.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
explanation_en:
Undelivered SNS messages will be routed to the Dead List - and the goal will always be attached to the subscriber SQS queue. SQS can be set for a maximum of 14 days to analyze the message after. There's no need to write any code -- it's just a subscription settings.
Option A: SNS Death Queue can only target SQS Queue; Kinesis data stream does not support use in this role.
Option B: Queue placed in front of the theme does not help: Messages are lost between SNS and local endpoints located downstream of the theme.
Option D: DynamoDB tables are also not the target of the SNS Dead Letter queue.

options.text: Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream target with a retention period of 14 days.
Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue with a retention period of 14 days between the application and Amazon SNS.
Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) target with a retention period of 14 days.
Configure an Amazon SNS dead letter queue that has an Amazon DynamoDB target with a TTL attribute set for a retention period of 14 days.

question_text:
A gaming company uses Amazon DynamoDB to store user information such as geographic location, player data, and leaderboards. The company needs to configure continuous backups to an Amazon S3 bucket with a minimal amount of coding. The backups must not affect availability of the application and must not affect the read capacity units (RCUs) that are defined for the table.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
DynamoDB has a built-in table exported to the S3 function, which is based on a continuous backup operation and therefore needs to be restored at the opening point at time. Export operations read data from backup rather than from real-time tables, so they do not consume reading capacity units and do not affect the availability of applications. There is no need to write any code.
Option A: An Amazon EMR cluster running a Hive operation directly reads the table itself, consumes the reading capacity unit and requires additional infrastructure to manage it.
Option C: Use stream plus a Lambda function means that a custom processing code needs to be prepared and maintained, and the internal export enables the same function to be performed through a single setting.
Option D: Regular export through the Lambda function means that both codes and tables are required, and this is not a continuous backup, but a regular snapshot.

options.text: Use an Amazon EMR cluster. Create an Apache Hive job to back up the data to Amazon S3.
Export the data directly from DynamoDB to Amazon S3 with continuous backups. Turn on point-in-time recovery for the table.
Configure Amazon DynamoDB Streams. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume the stream and export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Create an AWS Lambda function to export the data from the database tables to Amazon S3 on a regular basis. Turn on point-in-time recovery for the table.

question_text:
A solutions architect is designing an asynchronous application to process credit card data validation requests for a bank. The application must be secure and be able to process each request at least once.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Three requirements: stept processing, "at least one" delivery, and minimum costs with appropriate protection. "At least once" is the assurance provided by the standard SQS queue, which is cheaper than the FIFO queue and is not limited by the volume of the FIFO pass; the FIFO is required when strict sequencing and precision of a treatment is essential, and this is not the case in this scenario. The encryption of card data using the company ' s own KMS key is reasonable. Finally, kms: Decrypt privileges are given to the executive role of the function - the role, not the function itself, as the subject of IAM.
Option B: A FIFO queue is more expensive than the standard queue and is not needed in this scenario: demand is at least one delivery, not a strict order. The SQS management key is also not capable of allowing the company to control the key, which is usually necessary for the payment of data.
Option C: Encryption is the right choice, but FIFO once again introduces unnecessary assurance and additional costs compared to standard queues.
Option D: Queue type and encryption is correct, but the description of permissions is incorrect: permission to use KMS key (kms:Decrypt) is given to Lambda to perform the role, not the function itself.

options.text: Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source. Use AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.

Use AWS Lambda event source mapping. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source. Use SQS managed encryption keys (SSE-SQS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.

Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the event source. Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Add the kms:Decrypt permission for the Lambda execution role.

Use the AWS Lambda event source mapping. Set Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queues as the event source. Use AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for encryption. Add the encryption key invocation permission for the Lambda function.

question_text:
A company has multiple AWS accounts for development work. Some staff consistently use oversized Amazon EC2 instances, which causes the company to exceed the yearly budget for the development accounts. The company wants to centrally restrict the creation of AWS resources in these accounts.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
explanation_en:
This restriction needs to be centralized in multiple accounts and does not require development work. This requires using SCP: Development accounts are grouped into a separate OU with a policy to ban the ec2: RunInstances operation, which is judged on the basis of the type of instance that is not in the allowed list (ec2: InstanceType condition). Refuses to operate for all subjects in the account, including root users, and cannot be bypassed by local strategies. There is no code or product catalogue to maintain.
Option A: Systems Manager templates describe a process but do not prohibit any operation: an employee can still bypass the template to start an example directly.
Option C: Respond through a function after the example has been created, meaning that a code needs to be prepared and a fee is paid for the time that a large instance runs before it is discovered. There is no preventive deterrent mechanism.
Option D: Service Catalog provides a convenient directory to approve the configuration, but it requires pre-prepared products and cannot prevent the creation of cases directly unless the permission is restricted separately.

options.text: Develop AWS Systems Manager templates that use an approved EC2 creation process. Use the approved Systems Manager templates to provision EC2 instances.
Use AWS Organizations to organize the accounts into organizational units (OUs). Define and attach a service control policy (SCP) to control the usage of EC2 instance types.
Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function when an EC2 instance is created. Stop disallowed EC2 instance types.
Set up AWS Service Catalog products for the staff to create the allowed EC2 instance types. Ensure that staff can deploy EC2 instances only by using the Service Catalog products.

question_text:
A company wants to use artificial intelligence (AI) to determine the quality of its customer service calls. The company currently manages calls in four different languages, including English. The company will offer new languages in the future. The company does not have the resources to regularly maintain machine learning (ML) models.
The company needs to create written sentiment analysis reports from the customer service call recordings. The customer service call recording text must be translated into English.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)
explanation_en:
The pipeline consists of three hosting services, each of which is responsible for one step. Amazon Transcribe converts the telephone recording to text (D) in any supporting language. Amazon Translate translated the text into English (E). Amazon Comprehend carries out emotional analysis and produces the required content for the report (F). There is no need to maintain a self-defined machine learning model at any stage.
Option A: Comprehend analyzes text - it neither translates nor converts audio into text.
Option B: Amazon Lex builds dialogue robots instead of emotional analysis.
Option C: Amazon Polly works in the opposite direction - it converts the text to a voice.

options.text: Use Amazon Comprehend to translate the audio recordings into English.
Use Amazon Lex to create the written sentiment analysis reports.
Use Amazon Polly to convert the audio recordings into text.
Use Amazon Transcribe to convert the audio recordings in any language into text.
Use Amazon Translate to translate text in any language to English.
Use Amazon Comprehend to create the sentiment analysis reports.

question_text:
A company is conducting an internal audit. The company wants to ensure that the data in an Amazon S3 bucket that is associated with the company’s AWS Lake Formation data lake does not contain sensitive customer or employee data. The company wants to discover personally identifiable information (PII) or financial information, including passport numbers and credit card numbers.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The mission is to search for personal and financial data on the S3 object: passport number, card number. This is precisely what Amazon Macie designed to do with the managed data identifier: it runs a discovery operation, scans objects (including samples, so you do not have to pay for scanning all the contents) and returns the discovery that contains the type and location of the data. There is no need to write a custom rule or regular expression.
Option A: Audit Manager collects evidence that matches the frame, but does not analyse the object content.
Option B: S3 Information lists objects and their metadata. It did not know what was inside the document.
Option D: S3 Select runs a query on the content of a single object with a known structure. It is not a tool to search for sensitive data in S3 buckets.

options.text: Configure AWS Audit Manager on the account. Select the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standards (PCI DSS) for auditing.
Configure Amazon S3 Inventory on the S3 bucket Configure Amazon Athena to query the inventory.
Configure Amazon Macie to run a data discovery job that uses managed identifiers for the required data types.
Use Amazon S3 Select to run a report across the S3 bucket.

question_text:
A company uses on-premises servers to host its applications. The company is running out of storage capacity. The applications use both block storage and NFS storage. The company needs a high-performing solution that supports local caching without re-architecting its existing applications.
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
The application uses two different types of storage and cannot be rewrited. The replacement must therefore be based on protocol matching: the file gateway replaces the NFS storage, the data is provided through S3 and local caches (B), while the volume gateway replacement block is stored, the volume is provided through iSCSI and the active data is stored locally (D). Both gateways meet local cache requirements under the topic.
Option A: S3 cannot be mounted as a file system using primary tools, and third-party solutions provide neither cache nor file system syntax.
Option C: Snowball Edge is intended for data transfer and temporary on-site calculations, rather than permanent extended storage.
Option E: The EFS file system can only be mounted through a private connection from the local network and does not provide local caches: the delay is determined by the link, and it is simply not a substitute for block storage.

options.text: Mount Amazon S3 as a file system to the on-premises servers.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway to replace NFS storage.
Deploy AWS Snowball Edge to provision NFS mounts to on-premises servers.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway to replace the block storage.

question_text:
A company has a service that reads and writes large amounts of data from an Amazon S3 bucket in the same AWS Region. The service is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances within the private subnet of a VPC. The service communicates with Amazon S3 over a NAT gateway in the public subnet. However, the company wants a solution that will reduce the data output costs.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The cost here is not for storage - data transferred from one gigabyte to S3 or from S3 must pass through the NAT gateway: not only is the hourly cost of the gateway charged, but the amount of data transmitted is also charged. A gateway VPC terminal node completely eliminates NAT on this path - adding a route to the S3 prefix in the chart of the private subnet, traffic is transmitted through the AWS network and no cost is incurred by the terminal node itself or by the data passing through it. This is the only option that would actually reduce costs rather than simply transfer costs. Related issues: 42, 91, 612.
Option A: The NAT example replaces the hosting service with one of your own machines: you need to pay for the example and its traffic, you need to be responsible for its fault tolerance and be limited to the amount of throughput at a single node.
Option B: This configuration is impossible: NAT must be located in a public subnet, and the route chart that needs to be modified belongs to the private subnet. The configuration described in this option cannot be achieved.
Option D: The second NAT gateway will double the hourly cost and will not reduce the amount of gigabyte data passed.

options.text: Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the public subnet. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 traffic.

Provision a dedicated EC2 NAT instance in the private subnet. Configure the route table for the public subnet to use the elastic network interface of this instance as the destination for all S3 traffic.
Provision a VPC gateway endpoint. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use the gateway endpoint as the route for all S3 traffic.
Provision a second NAT gateway. Configure the route table for the private subnet to use this NAT gateway as the destination for all S3 traffic.

question_text:
A company uses Amazon S3 to store high-resolution pictures in an S3 bucket. To minimize application changes, the company stores the pictures as the latest version of an S3 object. The company needs to retain only the two most recent versions of the pictures.
The company wants to reduce costs. The company has identified the S3 bucket as a large expense.
Which solution will reduce the S3 costs with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The drum has been enabled to use version control, while the old (non-current) version of the picture is the reason for the higher cost. The S3 Life Cycle Rules happen to have two settings needed to solve this problem: NoncurrentVersionExpiration deletes non-current versions, while NewerNoncurrentVersions specifies the number of most recent versions to be retained. Set it to 2 so you can automatically clean it up without writing any code. Application access to the current version of the object is exactly the same as before.
Option B: A Lambda function solves this problem by creating, scheduling, processing errors and ubiquitous lists. The life-cycle rule achieves the same function by configuration.
Option C: S3 Batch Operations is a one-time task driven by the S3 dashboard report. You need to run it over and over again, and life cycle rules can run automatically on a continuous basis.
Option D: Discontinuation of version control does not remove an old version that has accumulated - the billing remains unchanged. Moreover, the requirement to retain the two most recent versions could not be met, as no new versions would be created.

options.text: Use S3 Lifecycle to delete expired object versions and retain the two most recent versions.
Use an AWS Lambda function to check for older versions and delete all but the two most recent versions.
Use S3 Batch Operations to delete noncurrent object versions and retain only the two most recent versions.
Deactivate versioning on the S3 bucket and retain the two most recent versions.

question_text:
A company needs to minimize the cost of its 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection. The company's average connection utilization is less than 10%. A solutions architect must recommend a solution that will reduce the cost without compromising security.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The connection has a usage rate of less than one tenth of its capacity and therefore needs to be reduced at port speed. Specialized connections can only be ordered at the speed of 1 Gbps, 10 Gbps or 100 Gbps, while the lower speed of 50 Mbps to 500 Mbps exists only as a hosting connection and is configured by AWS Direct Contact partners. Ordering a 200 Mbps hosting connection in an existing account reduces port costs without compromising the privacy or security of the path.
Option A: A second connection to the same 1 Gbps doubles the cost of the port; sharing the connection with another account does not reduce the cost of the company.
Option B: Console does not allow to order a 200 Mbps dedicated connection - only 1 Gbps and above can be ordered.
Option C: Gg connection costs through partners are approximately the same as today. Savings are due to lower port speed, not changes in connection ordering.

options.text: Set up a new 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.
Set up a new 200 Mbps Direct Connect connection in the AWS Management Console.
Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 1 Gbps connection. Share the connection with another AWS account.
Contact an AWS Direct Connect Partner to order a 200 Mbps hosted connection for an existing AWS account.

question_text:
A company has multiple Windows file servers on premises. The company wants to migrate and consolidate its files into an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. File permissions must be preserved to ensure that access rights do not change.
Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
Windows file permissions must be preserved, so the migration tool needs to understand access control lists (ACLs) - AWS DataSync: it carries access control lists and ownership with the file and can write directly to FSx for Windows File Server filesystems. The agent can be deployed as a virtual machine (A) in the data centre, or, if the network links are weak, can operate directly on the AWS Snowcone device connected to the local network (D). Both paths can achieve the same results.
Option B: Copying data to S3 first loses Windows access control lists: the file becomes an object and ACLs will never be transmitted to FSx.
Option C: Importing a disk into S3 will transform the data into objects and lose access in the same way, while the physical transport disk cannot control the integrity of the data.
Option E: Copying data to Snowball device with CLI and copying to S3 will make the file an object and lose ACLs. Snowball is useful here only as a platform for running agents, not as a transit point for S3.

options.text: Deploy AWS DataSync agents on premises. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
Copy the shares on each file server into Amazon S3 buckets by using the AWS CLI. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.
Remove the drives from each file server. Ship the drives to AWS for import into Amazon S3. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.

Order an AWS Snowcone device. Connect the device to the on-premises network. Launch AWS DataSync agents on the device. Schedule DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.

Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Connect the device to the on-premises network. Copy data to the device by using the AWS CLI. Ship the device back to AWS for import into Amazon S3. Schedule AWS DataSync tasks to transfer the data to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.

question_text:
A company wants to ingest customer payment data into the company's data lake in Amazon S3. The company receives payment data every minute on average. The company wants to analyze the payment data in real time.
Then the company wants to ingest the data into the data lake.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
explanation_en:
Data arrive once a minute on average and require real-time analysis before being stored in the data lake. Kinesis Data Firehose is a fully hosted transmission service: it buffers, converts and writes to S3 itself, and expands without you managing the fractions. Real-time analysis based on this data stream is done by Kinesis Data Analytics through a regular SQL query. So far, no operation — and that is the expression of maximum operational efficiency — is required.
Option A: Data Teams needs to manage the fractions, while the analysis in the Lambda function needs a custom code.
Option B: AWS Glue is a batch processing ETL service; it is not designed for ingestion of continuous data streams.
Option D: API Gateway and function means that manual construction of data intake and manual construction analysis is required, instead of using two hosting services specifically designed for specific purposes.

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.
Use AWS Glue to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest data. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to analyze the data in real time.
Use Amazon API Gateway to ingest data. Use AWS Lambda to analyze the data in real time.

question_text:
A company runs a website that uses a content management system (CMS) on Amazon EC2. The CMS runs on a single EC2 instance and uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance for the data tier. Website images are stored on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that is mounted inside the EC2 instance.
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to improve the performance and resilience of the website? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
There are two weaknesses: individual examples, and mirrors stored on local rolls. Move the mirror to Amazon EFS and mount it on each instance, meaning that each example can see the complete set of files (C). The site itself is an automatic extension group with at least two examples, built through AMI and supported by the Application Load Balancer, which deploys a cache of mirrors in front of the edge to significantly increase the speed of content delivery (E).
Option A: There is no standard method to mount S3 drums as a file system on the instance; the application must be rewritten to work through API.
Option B: Providing file services through the NFS from the main example turns it into a single-point failure — error tolerance changes rather than better.
Option D: Error tolerance increases, but Global Accerator optimizes the flow path and does not slow down static content. For a web site that provides mirrors, the real gain comes from the cache of Cloud Front.

options.text: Move the website images into an Amazon S3 bucket that is mounted on every EC2 instance
Share the website images by using an NFS share from the primary EC2 instance. Mount this share on the other EC2 instances.
Move the website images onto an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that is mounted on every EC2 instance.

question_text:
A company runs an infrastructure monitoring service. The company is building a new feature that will enable the service to monitor data in customer AWS accounts. The new feature will call AWS APIs in customer accounts to describe Amazon EC2 instances and read Amazon CloudWatch metrics.
What should the company do to obtain access to customer accounts in the MOST secure way?
explanation_en:
This is the classic model for third-party service access to customer accounts: the client creates itself a role with minimal access (here is the read-only EC2 and Cloudwatch access) and designates the provider's account in a trust strategy. The service calls AssumeRole and operates with a temporary voucher. You will never store another person's key, and the client can withdraw access by deleting the character at any time. An important addition from practical application: the use of external IDs in confidence-building strategies to guard against confusing proxy attacks.
Option B: Self-issuing temporary certificates does not solve the fundamental problem: to issue these certificates, you still need to have privileges in the client ' s account, which in turn means that you need a trusted role.
Option C: Storage of IAM user keys for thousands of customers in their own storage is the worst option: long-term valid keys, responsibility for safe custody, and trouble with manual revocation.
Option D: Cognito is designed for application end users rather than for cross-account access to AWS API. The password in the key storage remains a valid key for long periods of time.

options.text: Ensure that the customers create an IAM role in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions and a trust policy to the company’s account.
Create a serverless API that implements a token vending machine to provide temporary AWS credentials for a role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions.
Ensure that the customers create an IAM user in their account with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions. Encrypt and store customer access and secret keys in a secrets management system.

Ensure that the customers create an Amazon Cognito user in their account to use an IAM role with read-only EC2 and CloudWatch permissions. Encrypt and store the Amazon Cognito user and password in a secrets management system.

question_text:
A company needs to connect several VPCs in the us-east-1 Region that span hundreds of AWS accounts. The company's networking team has its own AWS account to manage the cloud network.
What is the MOST operationally efficient solution to connect the VPCs?
explanation_en:
Hundreds of accounts and a lot of VPCs in individual regions are the scenes that Transit Gateway was designed to solve. It is deployed in the accounts of the network team, shared through AWS RAM with other accounts, and each VPC connects through only one connection. Route management remains centralized by network teams — the most efficient option from an operational point of view.
Option A: Hundreds of VPCs have set up a full network of peer-to-peer connections that mean tens of thousands of connections and edits each route chart. This is unmanageable in practice.
Option B: Connecting the internal network through the Internet means losing privacy, having to pay for the transmission of data from the outstation and causing delays.
Option D: Transit VPC, built on its own VPN gateway, is the old pattern replaced by Transit Gateway: it requires independent equipment, is limited to the tunnel bandwidth and must be maintained manually.

options.text: Set up VPC peering connections between each VPC. Update each associated subnet’s route table
Configure a NAT gateway and an internet gateway in each VPC to connect each VPC through the internet
Create an AWS Transit Gateway in the networking team’s AWS account. Configure static routes from each VPC.
Deploy VPN gateways in each VPC. Create a transit VPC in the networking team’s AWS account to connect to each VPC.

question_text:
A company has Amazon EC2 instances that run nightly batch jobs to process data. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group that uses On-Demand billing. If a job fails on one instance, another instance will reprocess the job. The batch jobs run between 12:00 AM and 06:00 AM local time every day.
Which solution will provide EC2 instances to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
These operations operate six hours a day and tolerate interruptions: if the example is lost, another will reprocess the operation. This use is the typical application scene that captures the example — saves up to 90 per cent of the cost, and the application's own re-test logic already absorbs volume changes resulting from the recovery of the case.
Option A: A Savings Plan has a return under a full-time load; running only six hours a day will lead to underutilization of the commitment.
Option B: Keep a constant billing of examples, but only one quarter of the time a day.
Option D: A larger case-by-case will only further increase the billing: the billing model itself has not changed.

options.text: Purchase a 1-year Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 that covers the instance family of the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
Purchase a 1-year Reserved Instance for the specific instance type and operating system of the instances in the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Set the instances to Spot Instances. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.
