question_text:
A social media company is building a feature for its website. The feature will give users the ability to upload photos. The company expects significant increases in demand during large events and must ensure that the website can handle the upload traffic from users.
Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST scalability?
explanation_en:
The bottleneck is the application of the document to the server. The pre-signed URL completely eliminates this bottleneck: the application server generates only one signature link and the browser uploads the file directly to S3. The server is not involved in data transmission, so the surge during a major event is limited to S3's own scalability, which is virtually unlimited.
Option A: The files are applied to servers that are the bottlenecks in the surge and require you to expand the server cluster and its bandwidth.
Option B: The file gateway is a hybrid gateway for local data centres; it has nothing to do with the upload of the user browser.
Option D: The EFS file system is mounted on an example inside the VPC; it cannot be uploaded directly from the browser.

options.text: Upload files from the user's browser to the application servers. Transfer the files to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file gateway.
Generate Amazon S3 presigned URLs in the application. Upload files directly from the user's browser into an S3 bucket.
Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Upload files directly from the user's browser to the file system.

question_text:
A company has a web application for travel ticketing. The application is based on a database that runs in a single data center in North America. The company wants to expand the application to serve a global user base. The company needs to deploy the application to multiple AWS Regions. Average latency must be less than 1 second on updates to the reservation database.
The company wants to have separate deployments of its web platform across multiple Regions. However, the company must maintain a single primary reservation database that is globally consistent.
Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
This requirement requires a consistent global reserve storage, with a delay of less than one second for renewal and deployment in multiple regions. The DynamoDB global table allows you to write in any area and copy the data to other regions, usually in one second, and each deployment is connected to its own regional endpoint.
Option B: Aurora reading copy only supports reading operations: the reserved writing operation will still be sent to a single writing area and the remote user will be delayed by more than one second.
Option C: RDS has the same writing problem with a copy reading, and the copying delay is significantly higher than that of Aurora.
Option D: An independent database constructed manually through the Lambda function ensures that there is a conflict and that no single state of consistency can be guaranteed.

options.text: Convert the application to use Amazon DynamoDB. Use a global table for the center reservation table. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment.
Migrate the database to an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Deploy Aurora Read Replicas in each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment for access to the database.
Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. Deploy MySQL read replicas in each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment for access to the database.

Migrate the application to an Amazon Aurora Serverless database. Deploy instances of the database to each Region. Use the correct Regional endpoint in each Regional deployment to access the database. Use AWS Lambda functions to process event streams in each Region to synchronize the databases.

question_text:
A company has migrated multiple Microsoft Windows Server workloads to Amazon EC2 instances that run in the us-west-1 Region. The company manually backs up the workloads to create an image as needed.
In the event of a natural disaster in the us-west-1 Region, the company wants to recover workloads quickly in the us-west-2 Region. The company wants no more than 24 hours of data loss on the EC2 instances. The company also wants to automate any backups of the EC2 instances.
Which solutions will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative effort? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
The requirement is an automatic backup and an on-site copy in another area, with data missing for no more than 24 hours. Both options provide for backups twice a day and are automatically copied to us-west-2: one is a label-based EC2-backed AMI life-cycle strategy, which is configured for replication to other regions (B), and the other is a label-based AWS Backup plan, which designates a copy destination (D). In both cases, once the set-up has been completed, no further intervention is required.
Option A: The manual reproduction of mirrors is a manual operation that is explicitly avoided in the requirement and does not guarantee that the data will be lost in quantities not exceeding one day.
Option C: The preparation of a custom function to move a copy is unnecessary as AWS Backup already provides the built-in cross-section reproduction function.
Option E: Movement control is automatic, but reproduction to other regions is still done manually.

options.text: Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily. Copy the image on demand.
Create an Amazon EC2-backed Amazon Machine Image (AMI) lifecycle policy to create a backup based on tags. Schedule the backup to run twice daily. Configure the copy to the us-west-2 Region.

Create backup vaults in us-west-1 and in us-west-2 by using AWS Backup. Create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Create an AWS Lambda function to run as a scheduled job to copy the backup data to us-west-2.

Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Define the destination for the copy as us-west-2. Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily.

Create a backup vault by using AWS Backup. Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan for the EC2 instances based on tag values. Specify the backup schedule to run twice daily. Copy on demand to us-west-2.

question_text:
A company operates a two-tier application for image processing. The application uses two Availability Zones, each with one public subnet and one private subnet. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the web tier uses the public subnets. Amazon EC2 instances for the application tier use the private subnets.
Users report that the application is running more slowly than expected. A security audit of the web server log files shows that the application is receiving millions of illegitimate requests from a small number of IP addresses. A solutions architect needs to resolve the immediate performance problem while the company investigates a more permanent solution.
What should the solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?
explanation_en:
The immediate need is to stop a specific IP address. The explicit rejection rule exists only in the Web Access Control List (network ACLs) and needs to be applied to the web-tier subnets because the load balancers are located in these subnets and the traffic of the attackers reaches them.
Option A: The security team has no rule of refusal: they only allow traffic.
Option C: The same security group limits, combined with the target level, are wrong levels.
Option D: Network Access Control List (network ACL) is the right tool, but it is applied to the application subnets - malicious traffic does not reach these subnets directly, and traffic will continue to load web layer.

options.text: Modify the inbound security group for the web tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
Modify the network ACL for the web tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
Modify the inbound security group for the application tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
Modify the network ACL for the application tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.

question_text:
A global marketing company has applications that run in the ap-southeast-2 Region and the eu-west-1 Region.
Applications that run in a VPC in eu-west-1 need to communicate securely with databases that run in a VPC in ap-southeast-2.
Which network design will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Applications in the eu-west-1 area require access to databases in the ap-southeast-2 region - this requires a cross-regional VPC peer-to-peer connection, an update of route tables in the two networks, and entry rules on the database security group. An important detail is that you cannot quote the security group from another area - a cross-regional peer connection does not support this. Therefore, the rules must specify the IP address or address range of the application server.
Option A: The rule adds an error of location: the entry permission rule needs to be configured on the side of the database, not on the side of the application. The opposite is described.
Option B: The reference to the security group ID in the cross-area peer connection is not supported - the rule cannot be created at all.
Option D: There are similar limitations to the transfer gateway equivalent connection: the security group reference cannot work across the region and the gateway itself is too complex to connect only two networks.

options.text: Create a VPC peering connection between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. Create an inbound rule in the eu-west-1 application security group that allows traffic from the database server IP addresses in the ap-southeast-2 security group.

Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPC. Update the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.

Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPUpdate the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that allows traffic from the eu-west-1 application server IP addresses.

Create a transit gateway with a peering attachment between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. After the transit gateways are properly peered and routing is configured, create an inbound rule in the database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.

question_text:
A company is developing software that uses a PostgreSQL database schema. The company needs to configure multiple development environments and databases for the company's developers. On average, each development environment is used for half of the 8-hour workday.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Reference answer: C; dispute option: B.
Technically, option C (a conventional configured Aurora cluster) is in fact more expensive than an RDS-sole example to stop running at night because the environment is only 4 hours a day compared to 8 hours a day
Deficiencies: Option C is shown as “Aurora as required compatible with PostgreSQL”, which duplicates the original text of option A; according to the intent of the title, “Aurora has no server” - only this option is automatically reduced during free time.
Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-Compatible for original option C is not the product name in the AWS document. The title seems to point to Aurora Servers v2, which can set a minimum of 0 ACU and be automatically suspended, but the original option cannot be regarded as the right one to be deployed directly; the source reference answer is retained and the defect is marked.
The environment is used for only four hours of eight working days, thus making it more advantageous to avoid paying for free time. Key point C, which is interpreted as “usage-based” (i.e., the Aurora database, which is based on consumption), is less expensive than any full-day example of continuous operation. The presentation of the option itself is controversial: “Aurora On-Demand” literally describes an ordinary hourly configuration, in which case option B — an example of a small RDS-only area that stops at night — is cheaper. This question is not sufficiently precise; remember the rationale: irregularity, partial use means that consumption should be paid, rather than keeping examples on an ongoing basis.
Option A: The same Aurora option, with no limit on the use fee: a configured cluster is billed throughout its life, including four free hours per day.
Option B: A strong alternative: the RDS stand-alone area is the least-cost hosting PostgreSQL option that can save the computing resources. The disadvantage is that the RDS automatically restarts seven days after the case has ceased, and the cessation needs to be re-executed to deal with the situation.
Option D: S3 plus S3 Select is not a PostgreSQL database at all: no mode, no service, no index and no connection capability for PostgreSQL protocols. In principle, the need cannot be met.

options.text: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database
Configure each development environment with its own Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instances
Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-Compatible database
Configure each development environment with its own Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon S3 Object Select

question_text:
A company uses AWS Organizations with resources tagged by account. The company also uses AWS Backup to back up its AWS infrastructure resources. The company needs to back up all AWS resources.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
AWS Backup selects resources by label, so unlabelled resources will never enter the backup plan. The key to this problem is to find and label these resources: AWS Config is able to view a list of all resources in each account within the organization and to identify resources that lack the required labels (i.e. required-tags rules), which can then be automatically repaired. Since then, back-up plans will continue to operate on the basis of labels and newly created resources will be automatically included.
Option B: "Not running" is the wrong standard -- whatever the status, all resources need to be backed up. Adding resources manually to a backup volume does not extend.
Option C: Manual audit by account owner is the largest operating cost possible and ensures that there are omissions.
Option D: Amazon Inspectr is used to find gaps in the task load and has no knowledge of tags or backup schemes.

options.text: Use AWS Config to identify all untagged resources. Tag the identified resources programmatically. Use tags in the backup plan.
Use AWS Config to identify all resources that are not running. Add those resources to the backup vault.
Require all AWS account owners to review their resources to identify the resources that need to be backed up.
Use Amazon Inspector to identify all noncompliant resources.

question_text:
A social media company wants to allow its users to upload images in an application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud. The company needs a solution that automatically resizes the images so that the images can be displayed on multiple device types. The application experiences unpredictable traffic patterns throughout the day. The company is seeking a highly available solution that maximizes scalability.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The flow is unpredictable, and solutions require services that are self-extensionable and cost zero while free. A static website is stored in S3; uploading pictures triggers a Lambda function, which creates the size required and returns the result to the S3 bucket. There is no need to plan capacity for the server, and availability is handled by the service itself.
Option B: CloudFront is a content distribution network, not a hosting platform that can "call" StepFunctions, and it is not appropriate to store pictures in a relationship database.
Option C: A single EC2 instance is a single point failure that cannot be extended to respond to a surge in traffic.
Option D: An ECS cluster plus a processor that operates on a separate EC2 instance, which again becomes a bottleneck, remains the infrastructure that needs to be maintained.

options.text: Create a static website hosted in Amazon S3 that invokes AWS Lambda functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.
Create a static website hosted in Amazon CloudFront that invokes AWS Step Functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon RDS database.

Create a dynamic website hosted on a web server that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Configure a process that runs on the EC2 instance to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.

question_text:
A company is running a microservices application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company wants to migrate the application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for scalability. The company must configure the Amazon EKS control plane with endpoint private access set to true and endpoint public access set to false to maintain security compliance. The company must also put the data plane in private subnets. However, the company has received error notifications because the node cannot join the cluster.
Which solution will allow the node to join the cluster?
explanation_en:
When the public endpoint of the EKS control plane is disabled, the node is accessed through a private address inside the VPC - this part is feasible. However, the nodes also need to visit other services that provide public API: ECR (Imagination), S3 (Imaging Layer), Cloudwatch Logs, STS, EC2. In private subnets without NAT, the only way to access these services is through a set of interface VPC terminal nodes (plus the gateway nodes for S3). Without these terminal nodes, nodes would not be able to pull mirrors or join clusters — which is precisely why they cannot join clusters.
Option A: The mandate of the nodal role is indeed important, but its absence creates different errors, and the scene clearly describes the issue of network segregation in private clusters. In addition, the role of AmazonEKSNodeRole usually contains the strategies needed.
Option C: Moving nodes to the public subnet violates the requirement to keep the data plane in the private subnet.
Option D: The security group by default allows out-of-station traffic, which remains inaccessible without the terminal node or NAT gateway.

options.text: Grant the required permission in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to the AmazonEKSNodeRole IAM role.
Create interface VPC endpoints to allow nodes to access the control plane.
Recreate nodes in the public subnet. Restrict security groups for EC2 nodes.
Allow outbound traffic in the security group of the nodes.

question_text:
A company is migrating an on-premises application to AWS. The company wants to use Amazon Redshift as a solution.
Which use cases are suitable for Amazon Redshift in this scenario? (Choose three.)
explanation_en:
Original answer: BCE; source correction answer: ABC.
Option E ( "Global expansion to PB level and millions of requests per minute") describes Amazon DynamoDB rather than Redshift: Redshift clusters are regional and do not have the capacity to process requests at this rate. Option A is described by Redshift data API, which is designed to enable regular, containerized and event driven applications to access the data - so the correct three groups are A, B, C.
Amazon Redshift Data API allows applications to access analytical data; Redshift supports client and service-end encryption, and clusters can be suspended and restored as planned. D is a cache, E is a high-mixed operating database, and F is not an applicable scenario in the title, so the original BCE should read ABC.
The source practice key here has been corrected: the correct three groups are A, B, C. Amazon Redshift does provide a data API, which can be used for traditional, containerization and event-driven applications to access data (A); it supports client and server-end encryption (B); and it is well suited for analytical loads running while the main application is idle, since clusters can be suspended during this period (C).
Option D: Reduces the load of a backend database by cache is a task for ElastiCache or DAX; Redshift is an analytical data repository, not a cache.
Option E: Description of the global expansion to the PB level and millions of requests per minute is the Amazon DynamoDB: Redshift cluster, which is regional and does not have the capacity to process the request rate. This is why the source practice key was corrected.
Option F: Redshift does not have the concept of sub-cluster copies: Error tolerance is based on snapshots and cross-regional snapshots, rather than a copy created through the console.

options.text: Supporting data APIs to access data with traditional, containerized, and event-driven applications
Supporting client-side and server-side encryption
Building analytics workloads during specified hours and when the application is not active
Caching data to reduce the pressure on the backend database
Scaling globally to support petabytes of data and tens of millions of requests per minute
Creating a secondary replica of the cluster by using the AWS Management Console

question_text:
A company provides an API interface to customers so the customers can retrieve their financial information. The company expects a larger number of requests during peak usage times of the year.
The company requires the API to respond consistently with low latency to ensure customer satisfaction. The company needs to provide a compute host for the API.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
Demand remains low at peak loads and operating costs are minimal. The API Gateway combination with the Lambda function completely eliminates server management, while pre-positioning co-opts keep a pre-initialized set of implementation environments in place, so that no cold startup occurs and response times remain stable even in cases of sudden surges in requests.
Option A: An ECS cluster located behind the load balancer needs to be configured to expand and maintain the service.
Option C: EKS adds Kubernetes cluster management to the top -- this is the largest operating cost option.
Option D: Preserve simultaneous distribution only for functions and limit part of the simultaneous dispatch; it does not preheat the environment, so cold start still exists.

options.text: Use an Application Load Balancer and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).
Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency.
Use an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster.
Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with reserved concurrency.

question_text:
A company wants to send all AWS Systems Manager Session Manager logs to an Amazon S3 bucket for archival purposes.
Which solution will meet this requirement with the MOST operational efficiency?
explanation_en:
The session Manager is built into a session log to record a function of S3: simply point to a S3 bucket in the settings, the data will automatically flow into it. No proxy, no intermediate services, and no self-defined codes.
Option B: An agent added from the log group is an unnecessary middle and needs to be manually exported, and a direct setting already exists.
Option C: A Systems Manager document is run daily to collect server logs instead of session logs and adds a custom code and its own schedule.
Option D: The combination of proxy, log subscriptions and delivery streams solves the same problem, but three unnecessary additional components are added.

options.text: Enable S3 logging in the Systems Manager console. Choose an S3 bucket to send the session data to.
Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Export the logs to an S3 bucket from the group for archival purposes.
Create a Systems Manager document to upload all server logs to a central S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge to run the Systems Manager document against all servers that are in the account daily.

Install an Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Create a CloudWatch logs subscription that pushes any incoming log events to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Set Amazon S3 as the destination.

question_text:
An application uses an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. The RDS database is becoming low on disk space. A solutions architect wants to increase the disk space without downtime.
Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of effort?
explanation_en:
The automatic extension of the RDS storage automatically increases volume size when there is insufficient space available, and the process does not interrupt the service. You just have to open this setting once and set a ceiling value.
Option B: Case size determines CPU and memory, not disk capacity.
Option C: Specifies that IOPS will change I/O performance rather than the available storage space.
Option D: Executing backup, increasing storage space and restoring it means that there is a downtime and the largest amount of manual operations, while RDS volumes can be expanded in real time.

Increase the RDS database instance size
Change the RDS database instance storage type to Provisioned IOPS
Back up the RDS database, increase the storage capacity, restore the database, and stop the previous instance

question_text:
A consulting company provides professional services to customers worldwide. The company provides solutions and tools for customers to expedite gathering and analyzing data on AWS. The company needs to centrally manage and deploy a common set of solutions and tools for customers to use for self-service purposes.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
What is required is a catalogue of ready-made solutions, which are self-deployed by the client and centrally managed by the company. This is exactly what AWS Service Catalog offers: a version of a product with version control, start-up restrictions and access controls that allows users to deploy self-service.
Option A: ClaudFormation templates are source materials for the construction of catalogue products, but they are used separately to provide neither self-service shops nor centralized versions and access management.
Option C: Systems Manager documents are used to automate the operation of managed resources; they do not issue deployable solutions to clients.
Option D: Config items are entries in the history of resource allocation; they have nothing to do with the distribution of solutions.

Create AWS Service Catalog products for the customers.
Create AWS Systems Manager templates for the customers.
Create AWS Config items for the customers.

question_text:
A company is designing a new web application that will run on Amazon EC2 Instances. The application will use Amazon DynamoDB for backend data storage. The application traffic will be unpredictable. The company expects that the application read and write throughput to the database will be moderate to high. The company needs to scale in response to application traffic.
Which DynamoDB table configuration will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The key detail is the unpredictability of flows. On a needs basis, DynamoDB is able to adapt immediately to any surge in traffic, and you only have to pay for the actual request: when the load mode cannot be predicted in advance, it is cheaper than to retain a reserve capacity with redundant capacity.
Option A: Preserve capacity with the advantage of automatic expansion under a predictable load; in case of sudden surges, either it cannot be rapidly expanded or it will pay for unused capacity.
Option C: Standard-IA Table Class also exacerbates this problem, which is more expensive to request - and the reading and writing load here is medium to high load.
Option D: Standard-IA Table Category applies to data that are not frequently accessed, rather than active Web applications, by reducing storage costs at the expense of higher request costs.

options.text: Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard table class.
Configure DynamoDB with provisioned read and write by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class. Set DynamoDB auto scaling to a maximum defined capacity.
Configure DynamoDB in on-demand mode by using the DynamoDB Standard Infrequent Access (DynamoDB Standard-IA) table class.

question_text:
A retail company has several businesses. The IT team for each business manages its own AWS account. Each team account is part of an organization in AWS Organizations. Each team monitors its product inventory levels in an Amazon DynamoDB table in the team's own AWS account.
The company is deploying a central inventory reporting application into a shared AWS account. The application must be able to read items from all the teams' DynamoDB tables.
Which authentication option will meet these requirements MOST securely?
explanation_en:
Cross-account access is built on roles and STS within the organization, rather than distributing long-term keys. Creates a role in the accounts of each business module, the strategy of which gives access to the DynamoDB table of the account, and the trust strategy allows the reporting of a specific role in the account to assume that role. The application runs in its own role and calls AssumeRole to access the target account to obtain valid temporary vouchers during the session. There is no key to rotate, and cancellation of access requires only one editing of the trust strategy.
Option A: Access to DynamoDB is authorized by IAM, not by password or connection string. In fact, there is no need to store anything in Secrets Manager.
Option B: There are programmable IAM users in each account, which means that long-term keys need to be stored, distributed and manually rotated every month. That's exactly what the "safest" requires you to avoid.
Option D: DynamoDB does not use ACM certificates to verify the client. There is no such mechanism.

options.text: Integrate DynamoDB with AWS Secrets Manager in the inventory application account. Configure the application to use the correct secret from Secrets Manager to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table. Schedule secret rotation for every 30 days.

In every business account, create an IAM user that has programmatic access. Configure the application to use the correct IAM user access key ID and secret access key to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table. Manually rotate IAM access keys every 30 days.

In every business account, create an IAM role named BU_ROLE with a policy that gives the role access to the DynamoDB table and a trust policy to trust a specific role in the inventory application account. In the inventory account, create a role named APP_ROLE that allows access to the STS AssumeRole API operation. Configure the application to use APP_ROLE and assume the crossaccount role BU_ROLE to read the DynamoDB table.

Integrate DynamoDB with AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Generate identity certificates to authenticate DynamoDB. Configure the application to use the correct certificate to authenticate and read the DynamoDB table.

question_text:
A company runs container applications by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The company's workload is not consistent throughout the day. The company wants Amazon EKS to scale in and out according to the workload.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
Expansion needs to occur at two levels. Within the cluster, horizontal packagings automatically expand the number of control containers and require indicators from Kubernetes Metrics Server (B). When the container space is insufficient, the Kubernetes cluster extension increases the number of nodes (C). Both are standard components and do not require the preparation and maintenance of custom codes.
Option A: A custom function to resize a cluster means that codes need to be prepared and maintained, rather than using built-in mechanisms.
Option D: API Gateway handles incoming requests, unrelated to cluster expansion.
Option E: Observableness and flow management between App Mesh services, but not for capacity management.

options.text: Use an AWS Lambda function to resize the EKS cluster.
Use the Kubernetes Metrics Server to activate horizontal pod autoscaling.
Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to manage the number of nodes in the cluster.
Use Amazon API Gateway and connect it to Amazon EKS.
Use AWS App Mesh to observe network activity.

question_text:
A company runs a microservice-based serverless web application. The application must be able to retrieve data from multiple Amazon DynamoDB tables A solutions architect needs to give the application the ability to retrieve the data with no impact on the baseline performance of the application.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?
explanation_en:
Reference answer: B; dispute option: A.
The pip solver in AWS AppSync is designed to assemble data from multiple sources in a single request — including multiple DynamoDB tables — and does not need to create custom codes on the edges. Option B is based on the argument that the processing of edges is completely unreached to existing applications and therefore has no impact on their underlying performance
AppSync Pipeline Resourcer can combine data from multiple DynamoDB data sources in one request; the edge function of CloudFront is not a direct hosting program that aggregates multiple DynamoDB tables. Source B to A.
Source answer B's original resolution (in conflict with verification results, not accepted):
This is a controversial issue. The source practice material key is option B: The acquisition logic is pushed to the edge of CloudFront, so the underlying application is completely unaffected and the response is closer to the user for cache. A strong alternative is option A: AppSync Pyrolysis is available precisely to access multiple data sources — including multiple DynamoDB tables — sequentially in individual requests and does not require a custom border code or manage its reproduction. From the operational efficiency point of view, A appears to be a more natural option; but B is more appropriate from the point of view of `do not touch existing applications'.
Old Source Option A: Technically, this is the most direct way to obtain data from multiple tables in a single request, and the issue is therefore marked as controversial: the only objection is that it introduced a new API layer in front of the application.
Source old option C: An optimised API Gateway on the edge simply brings the entry point closer to the user; data from multiple tables must still be completed in the function ' s own code, so efficiency is not increased.
The old source option D: Athena Federal Query is designed to analyse queries, whose operation is delayed in seconds and is therefore not suitable for providing data to applications in real time.

options.text: AWS AppSync pipeline resolvers
Amazon CloudFront with [email protected] functions
Edge-optimized Amazon API Gateway with AWS Lambda functions
Amazon Athena Federated Query with a DynamoDB connector

question_text:
A company wants to analyze and troubleshoot Access Denied errors and Unauthorized errors that are related to IAM permissions. The company has AWS CloudTrail turned on.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST effort?
explanation_en:
The simplest way to search is to use Amazon Athena: CloudTrail console to install the "Creation of the Athena Table" feature, which is stored in a compressed JSON file in S3. You can then search for errors in the errorCode and errorMesseage fields (e.g. AccessDenied, Unauthorized Operation) through a regular SQL query and filter by user and time. You do not need a cluster and you do not need to write a code. You simply have to pay for the scan data, which can be limited by the date partition.
Option A: AWS Glue combines with a custom script, meaning that an ETL stream line is constructed, where a ready table can be executed with a SQL query.
Option B: AWS Batch runs a containerization operation. This is an unnecessary infrastructure and an unnecessary code for log resolution.
Option D: QuickSight can build visual charts, but it still needs a table as a data source (usually the same Athena table). For one-time error searches, the use of dashboards would appear to be too complex.

options.text: Use AWS Glue and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
Use AWS Batch and write custom scripts to query CloudTrail logs for the errors.
Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon Athena queries to identify the errors.
Search CloudTrail logs with Amazon QuickSight. Create a dashboard to identify the errors.

question_text:
A company wants to add its existing AWS usage cost to its operation cost dashboard. A solutions architect needs to recommend a solution that will give the company access to its usage cost programmatically. The company must be able to access cost data for the current year and forecast costs for the next 12 months.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The key phrase is "programmatically": the application requires cost data to build the dashboard. Cost Explorer (Cost Explorer) provides API (GetCostAndUsage for actual expenditure, GetCostForecost for forecast) and returns via the NextPageToken page break. The cost explorer can also generate its own 12-month projection. There is no need to deploy any content and therefore operating costs are minimal.
Option B: Downloadable CSV files means manual flow: someone must export them and load them to the dashboard. This is not a procedural visit.
Option C: AWS Budgets (AWS Budgets) apply policy and send notifications, but they do not export data and cannot be used through FTP.
Option D: Budget reports are sent by e-mail and contain only the budgetary status, rather than complete cost and projection data required for procedural processing.

options.text: Access usage cost-related data by using the AWS Cost Explorer API with pagination.
Access usage cost-related data by using downloadable AWS Cost Explorer report .csv files.
Configure AWS Budgets actions to send usage cost data to the company through FTP.
Create AWS Budgets reports for usage cost data. Send the data to the company through SMTP.

question_text:
A solutions architect is reviewing the resilience of an application. The solutions architect notices that a database administrator recently failed over the application's Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database writer instance as part of a scaling exercise. The failover resulted in 3 minutes of downtime for the application.
Which solution will reduce the downtime for scaling exercises with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The three-minute shutdown time was due to the fact that the application remained connected to the old writing example after the failure switch and the need to re-establish those connections manually. RDS Proxy maintains a connective pool and links it to the current writing instance itself, so the failure switch is almost invisible to the application. This change relates only to the replacement of the proxy endpoint with a new endpoint.
Option A: Additional read-only copies have no effect on the time taken to write case failure to switch.
Option B: Use a second cluster and manually perform application failure switching means additional costs, more management operations and no speed increase.
Option C: Memcached Cache Reader Operations without any acceleration for writing instance failure switching.

options.text: Create more Aurora PostgreSQL read replicas in the cluster to handle the load during failover.
Set up a secondary Aurora PostgreSQL cluster in the same AWS Region. During failover, update the application to use the secondary cluster's writer endpoint.
Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster to handle the load during failover.
Set up an Amazon RDS proxy for the database. Update the application to use the proxy endpoint.

question_text:
A company has a regional subscription-based streaming service that runs in a single AWS Region. The architecture consists of web servers and application servers on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in Auto Scaling groups behind Elastic Load Balancers. The architecture includes an Amazon Aurora global database cluster that extends across multiple Availability Zones.
The company wants to expand globally and to ensure that its application has minimal downtime.
Which solution will provide the MOST fault tolerance?
explanation_en:
The maximum tolerance is derived from a complete second site: the Web layer and application layer are deployed in another region, using a global Aurora database (usually delayed within one second) with a storage-level copy, and switching traffic through the Route 53 health check to match the failure-to-routing strategy, with the subsequent upgrading of the secondary cluster to the main cluster.
Option A: An automatic extension group exists in a single area and cannot start an example in a usable area belonging to another area. This option is technically impossible.
Option B: Cross-regional Aurora copies created in a standard way are copied at the logical level at a slower rate than the global database, and demand clearly requires maximum tolerance for errors.
Option C: AWS DMS is a migration tool, not an built-in mechanism for continuous cross-regional Aurora replication. It's an additional component, and it could itself be a failure point.

options.text: Extend the Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and the application tier to deploy instances in Availability Zones in a second Region. Use an Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.

Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Add an Aurora PostgreSQL cross-Region Aurora Replica in the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.

Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Create an Aurora PostgreSQL database in the second Region. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the primary database to the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.

Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Use an Amazon Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.

question_text:
A data analytics company wants to migrate its batch processing system to AWS. The company receives thousands of small data files periodically during the day through FTP. An on-premises batch job processes the data files overnight. However, the batch job takes hours to finish running.
The company wants the AWS solution to process incoming data files as soon as possible with minimal changes to the FTP clients that send the files. The solution must delete the incoming data files after the files have been processed successfully. Processing for each file needs to take 3-8 minutes.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?
explanation_en:
The FTP client cannot change and the processing must start immediately and take three to eight minutes. AWS Transfer Family provides a hosting FTP server that can write files directly to S3; when an object creation event is triggered, a Lambda function is activated to process the file and then delete it. Eight minutes were fully within the 15-minute limit of Lambda, and there were no servers in the programme.
Option A: The Glacier Flexible Retrieval type requires a search step and runs on a daily basis in contradiction to the requirement that documents be processed immediately.
Option B: Deployment and daily operation of a self-managed FTP server on an example means an additional operational burden and violates the requirement to process documents immediately.
Option C: AWS Transport Family cannot write to EBS Volume: S3 and EFS are only supported as storage targets. And the S3 notification does not apply to the documents on the volume.

options.text: Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files as objects in Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the objects nightly from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Delete the objects after the job has processed the objects.

Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the files nightly from the EBS volume. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.

Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use an Amazon S3 event notification when each file arrives to invoke the job in AWS Batch. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.

Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files in Amazon S3 Standard. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the files and to delete the files after they are processed. Use an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function when the files arrive.

question_text:
A company is migrating its workloads to AWS. The company has transactional and sensitive data in its databases.
The company wants to use AWS Cloud solutions to increase security and reduce operational overhead for the databases.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
There are two requirements: to improve security and reduce the operational load on the database while maintaining the service load. Amazon RDS addresses these two problems: it is responsible for patch management, backup, multi-usable areas (Multi-AZ) and monitoring, and uses KMS keys to enable static encryption, covering storage, snapshots, backups and copies. Database connections also use TLS in transfer. Self-managed database engines on EC2 can only obtain the same level of security if you build them yourself.
Option A: The database on EC2 leaves you with patch management, backup, tolerance and monitoring. Operating loads will rise, not fall.
Option C: S3 plus Macie is an object storage plus data classification, not a transaction database. Applications do not have anywhere to run queries and services.
Option D: Cloudwatch Logs. It neither provides static encryption nor data protection.

options.text: Migrate the databases to Amazon EC2. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.
Migrate the databases to Amazon RDS Configure encryption at rest.
Migrate the data to Amazon S3 Use Amazon Macie for data security and protection
Migrate the database to Amazon RDS. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs for data security and protection.

question_text:
A company has an online gaming application that has TCP and UDP multiplayer gaming capabilities. The company uses Amazon Route 53 to point the application traffic to multiple Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in different AWS Regions. The company needs to improve application performance and decrease latency for the online game in preparation for user growth.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The flow is based on TCP and UDP game traffic, and the load balancer has been deployed in multiple areas with the goal of reducing delays. The global accelerator receives the package at the nearest edge of the player, routes it through the AWS core network to the right area and runs it on the 4th floor, which means it supports TCP and UDP. To configure this function, the listener is configured on the same port as the NLB.
Option A: CloudFront is designed for HTTP and cache static content; it does not handle UDP flow of games and max-age parameters are not suitable for dynamic game sessions.
Option B: Apply the load balancer to handle HTTP and HTTPS only - replacing NLB with it would lose UDP support.
Option D: API Gateway is the front end of HTTP API; it will not be deployed after the load balancer and has nothing to do with game traffic.

options.text: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the NLBs. Increase the Cache-Control max-age parameter.
Replace the NLBs with Application Load Balancers (ALBs). Configure Route 53 to use latency-based routing.
Add AWS Global Accelerator in front of the NLBs. Configure a Global Accelerator endpoint to use the correct listener ports.
Add an Amazon API Gateway endpoint behind the NLBs. Enable API caching. Override method caching for the different stages.

question_text:
A company needs to integrate with a third-party data feed. The data feed sends a webhook to notify an external service when new data is ready for consumption. A developer wrote an AWS Lambda function to retrieve data when the company receives a webhook callback. The developer must make the Lambda function available for the third party to call.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
explanation_en:
A third party only needs an ordinary HTTPS address to call the trigger function. Function URL provides this, which is provided directly in the Lambda function, and contains both authentication and CORE configurations, which do not require load balancers or gateways - this is the least possible operational cost.
Option B: The load balancer continues to run and is billed and requires the creation of a target group and rules, and a function setting is sufficient to meet the demand.
Option C: SNS theme is not used to receive a public host name for call: it is responsible for sending messages out, not for accepting arbitrary requests from the network.
Option D: The SQS queue is called through the signed AWS API; you cannot send any webbook to it.

options.text: Create a function URL for the Lambda function. Provide the Lambda function URL to the third party for the webhook.
Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the Lambda function. Provide the ALB URL to the third party for the webhook.
Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Attach the topic to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SNS topic to the third party for the webhook.
Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Attach the queue to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SQS queue to the third party for the webhook.

question_text:
A company has a workload in an AWS Region. Customers connect to and access the workload by using an Amazon API Gateway REST API. The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company wants to provide individual and secure URLs for all customers.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency? (Choose three.)
explanation_en:
The most efficient way to assign an independent and secure URL to each client is through the use of the wildcard subdomain name model. Registered domain name, create a record of *.example.com in the Route 53 Trust Area, pointing to the API Gateway endpoint (A); request a wildcard certificate from ACM in the same area because the regional API certificate must be stored in the API area (D); and create a custom domain name for RET API in the API Gateway and import it (F). Since then, every new customer has been able to obtain its own sub-domain name without any infrastructure change.
Option B: This area is critical: the regional API requires its certificate to be located in the same area and only for the marginal optimization of the API requires a certificate in the region of us-east-1.
Option C: A separate trust area for each client means hundreds of areas, each of which requires a charge and manual maintenance — in contrast to operational efficiency.
Option E: Each client has a separate API endpoint that repeats the same configuration and makes the release of the change painful.

options.text: Register the required domain in a registrar. Create a wildcard custom domain name in a Route 53 hosted zone and record in the zone that points to the API Gateway endpoint.
Request a wildcard certificate that matches the domains in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in a different Region.
Create hosted zones for each customer as required in Route 53. Create zone records that point to the API Gateway endpoint.
Request a wildcard certificate that matches the custom domain name in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region.
Create multiple API endpoints for each customer in API Gateway.
