Option A: This handles running on cloud-based EMR clusters, while HDFS data is transmitted via VPN links: this is contrary to the locality of the data and affects performance.
Option B: DataSync copys the data to the cloud, which means that the data leaves the scene — a direct violation of this requirement.
Option D: Snowball moves the data to S3 and then processes it in the cloud. That demand is the opposite.

options.text: Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN to access the on-premises Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) data and application. Use an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.
Use AWS DataSync to connect to the on-premises Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) cluster. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.
Migrate the Apache Hadoop application and the Apache Spark application to Amazon EMR clusters on AWS Outposts. Use the EMR clusters to process the data.
Use an AWS Snowball device to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EMR cluster to process the data.

question_text:
A company is migrating a large amount of data from on-premises storage to AWS. Windows, Mac, and Linux based Amazon EC2 instances in the same AWS Region will access the data by using SMB and NFS storage protocols. The company will access a portion of the data routinely. The company will access the remaining data infrequently.
The company needs to design a solution to host the data.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
Windows, Mac, and Linux clients read data via SMB and NFS, some of which are less frequently accessed and must minimize operating costs. The S3 file gateway supports both protocols and stores the file as an object in a S3 bucket, and the S3 smart layer storage class automatically moves the less frequently accessed object to a cheaper level without setting rules and without fear of delay in retrieval.
Option A: EFS only supports NFS protocols: Windows and Mac clients that need SMB will not be allowed access.
Option B: FSx for ONTAP supports both protocols, but their cost is significantly higher than S3 and requires additional configurations, including tiered strategies.
Option D: FSx for OpenZFS provides data services through NFS that do not support SMB and do not have automatic cost reduction functionality for data with low access frequency.

options.text: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume that uses EFS Intelligent-Tiering. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to the EFS volume.
Create an Amazon FSx for ONTAP instance. Create an FSx for ONTAP file system with a root volume that uses the auto tiering policy. Migrate the data to the FSx for ONTAP volume.
Create an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Migrate the data to the S3 bucket by using an AWS Storage Gateway Amazon S3 File Gateway.
Create an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system. Migrate the data to the new volume.

question_text:
A manufacturing company runs its report generation application on AWS. The application generates each report in about 20 minutes. The application is built as a monolith that runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The application requires frequent updates to its tightly coupled modules. The application becomes complex to maintain as the company adds new features.
Each time the company patches a software module, the application experiences downtime. Report generation must restart from the beginning after any interruptions. The company wants to redesign the application so that the application can be flexible, scalable, and gradually improved. The company wants to minimize application downtime.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Single-body applications need to be broken down into micro-services so that the individual updating of the modules does not lead to disruption of the entire application and allows for flexible expansion. The use of ECS to support the automatic extension of services, each micro-service can be independently updated by rolling deployment, so that no stoppage occurs during the release process, and a report that takes 20 minutes to produce will not be interrupted.
Option A: The single Lambda function is still equivalent to a single application and 15 minutes execution is shorter than the time required to generate the report.
Option B: Spot instance can be retrieved at any time, and every time a report is interrupted, it restarts from scratch.
Option D: A one-time deployment strategy for a single application environment means that a single application remains intact and each update leads to a downtime.

options.text: Run the application on AWS Lambda as a single function with maximum provisioned concurrency.
Run the application on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances as microservices with a Spot Fleet default allocation strategy.
Run the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) as microservices with service auto scaling.
Run the application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk as a single application environment with an all-at-once deployment strategy.

question_text:
A company wants to rearchitect a large-scale web application to a serverless microservices architecture. The application uses Amazon EC2 instances and is written in Python.
The company selected one component of the web application to test as a microservice. The component supports hundreds of requests each second. The company wants to create and test the microservice on an AWS solution that supports Python. The solution must also scale automatically and require minimal infrastructure and minimal operational support.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Original answer: C; source correction answer: D.
This requirement requires a server-free solution to support Python, automatic expansion and minimal infrastructure and maintenance workload; option C (self-managed EC2 instances in EKS) is the opposite - operating costs are the highest. Only AWS Lambda meets the requirements
Lambda is a native running Python and is automatically scaled up as requested, without having to manage the EC2 or Kubernetes control surface; meet a minimum infrastructure and transport test of a microservice. Source C to D.
The requirements are Python support, automatic expansion, and minimal infrastructure and transport support. The Lambda function meets all these needs at once: the Python code can be run without managing a single server, and when the number of requests reaches hundreds per second, the combined capacity is automatically expanded and the billing is based only on the actual time of execution.
Option A: A preset example still needs to be prepared and maintained, and the interruption makes component testing more difficult.
Option B: Elastic Beanstalk is responsible for deployment management, but there are still EC2 instances and all maintenance work on the ground floor.
Option C: The example of self-managed EC2 in the EKS cluster represents the largest infrastructure and operational support of all options: node needs configuration, patch update and extension. This option is marked as critical in the log, which contradicts the requirements of the non-server — see the details of the audit log.

options.text: Use a Spot Fleet with auto scaling of EC2 instances that run the most recent Amazon Linux operating system.
Use an AWS Elastic Beanstalk web server environment that has high availability configured.
Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Launch Auto Scaling groups of self-managed EC2 instances.
Use an AWS Lambda function that runs custom developed code.

question_text:
A company has an AWS Direct Connect connection from its on-premises location to an AWS account. The AWS account has 30 different VPCs in the same AWS Region. The VPCs use private virtual interfaces (VIFs). Each VPC has a CIDR block that does not overlap with other networks under the company's control.
The company wants to centrally manage the networking architecture while still allowing each VPC to communicate with all other VPCs and on-premises networks.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?
explanation_en:
Thirty VPCs each have their own private virtual interface, which means that 30 objects need to be configured, and there is no connection between these networks. A transmission gateway can address both problems: direct connection connects via a transmission virtual interface (VIF) to the transmission gateway via a direct connection gateway, each VPC connects as an attachment, and manual maintenance of the route chart is no longer required when the route is launched. These networks can then access each other and connect to the company ' s local sites.
Option B: A direct connection gateway provides a connection to all VPC sites, but it does not connect between VPCs: it does not meet the requirement of "each VPC communicates with all other VPCs".
Option C: A transfer VPC with a complete gateway connection is an outmoded and labour-intensive model - the operational burden that the request seeks to avoid.
Option D: 30 VPN connections to replace the existing dedicated connection: a worse delay, limited to the tunnel bandwidth, and still no connection between VPCs.

options.text: Create a transit gateway, and associate the Direct Connect connection with a new transit VIF. Turn on the transit gateway's route propagation feature.
Create a Direct Connect gateway. Recreate the private VIFs to use the new gateway. Associate each VPC by creating new virtual private gateways.
Create a transit VPConnect the Direct Connect connection to the transit VPCreate a peering connection between all other VPCs in the Region. Update the route tables.
Create AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections from on premises to each VPC. Ensure that both VPN tunnels are UP for each connection. Turn on the route propagation feature.

question_text:
A company has applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances connect to Amazon RDS databases by using an IAM role that has associated policies. The company wants to use AWS Systems Manager to patch the EC2 instances without disrupting the running applications.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
One example can only have one role, so "a second role" is impossible -- but there is no need to remove existing strategies. The correct operation is to take the existing role and link it to the AmazonSSMManaged InstanceCore policy, thus retaining the existing access to the RDS. This option is somewhat rigid, but it accurately describes it in terms of meaning: the example retains its original authority and is also authorized by the Systems Manager agent, so the application is not affected.
Option B: Systems Manager manages the example through example roles and agents, not "for an IAM user". This configuration does not exist.
Option C: The default host configuration will automatically assign a role to the example, but it will replace the existing role with its own role, without retaining the RDS access granted to the application.
Option D: Removing the existing strategy would cut off access to the database by the application - a direct violation of the requirement not to interrupt.

options.text: Create a new IAM role. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the new IAM role. Attach the new IAM role to the EC2 instances and the existing IAM role.
Create an IAM user. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the IAM user. Configure Systems Manager to use the IAM user to manage the EC2 instances.
Enable Default Host Configuration Management in Systems Manager to manage the EC2 instances.
Remove the existing policies from the existing IAM role. Add the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the existing IAM role.

question_text:
A company runs container applications by using Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) and the Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler. The workload is not consistent throughout the day. A solutions architect notices that the number of nodes does not automatically scale out when the existing nodes have reached maximum capacity in the cluster, which causes performance issues.
Which solution will resolve this issue with the LEAST administrative overhead?
explanation_en:
A horizontal container auto-scalter increases the number of containers, but when the nodes are full, the new packagings are not run anywhere. This is precisely what Kubernetes solves: it monitors containers in waiting conditions and adds nodes to the group and removes them when they are idle. This is a standard component and does not require the preparation of a custom code.
Option A: Scalability based on memory usage applies to containers and does not solve the problem of exhaustion of the node ' s own capacity.
Option C: A custom function to adjust the EKS cluster requires the preparation and maintenance of codes rather than the use of ready-made components.
Option D: The EC2 auto-scaling group does not itself have the sensory capacity for unscheduled containers: in the absence of a cluster auto-scalter, it does not know when the nodes need to be added.

options.text: Scale out the nodes by tracking the memory usage.
Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to manage the number of nodes in the cluster.
Use an AWS Lambda function to resize the EKS cluster automatically.
Use an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to distribute the workload.

question_text:
A company maintains about 300 TB in Amazon S3 Standard storage month after month. The S3 objects are each typically around 50 GB in size and are frequently replaced with multipart uploads by their global application. The number and size of S3 objects remain constant, but the company's S3 storage costs are increasing each month.
How should a solutions architect reduce costs in this situation?
explanation_en:
The trap lies in the premise itself that "the number and size of S3 objects remain unchanged", but the bill continues to grow. This means that the company is paying for the non-visible content of the object list — that is, the uncompleted segment upload. Each suspended 50 GB object is uploaded with the received subparagraphs; these are counted as storage costs and do not appear in the list of stored barrels. The solution is to configure a life cycle rule that includes the AbortIncomplete MultiPartUpload operation, for example, by suspending it seven days after the upload starts. A useful diagnostic model: the mismatch between the total size of the object and the stored bill almost always refers to this point.
Option A: Transfer Acceleration will speed up the transmission and incur additional costs. The increase in billings was not caused by the speed of uploading, but by the sequences left behind by the suspension of uploading.
Option C: S3 Information is a report of the contents of the S3 buckets. It won't stop any operation and it won't affect the bill.
Option D: CloudFront Caches the response and reduces the cost of transmitting data from the exit station, but it does not change the amount of data stored in S3. The problem is storage, not data transmission.

options.text: Switch from multipart uploads to Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.
Enable an S3 Lifecycle policy that deletes incomplete multipart uploads.
Configure S3 inventory to prevent objects from being archived too quickly.
Configure Amazon CloudFront to reduce the number of objects stored in Amazon S3.

question_text:
A company has deployed a multiplayer game for mobile devices. The game requires live location tracking of players based on latitude and longitude. The data store for the game must support rapid updates and retrieval of locations.
The game uses an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance with read replicas to store the location data. During peak usage periods, the database is unable to maintain the performance that is needed for reading and writing updates. The game's user base is increasing rapidly.
What should a solutions architect do to improve the performance of the data tier?
explanation_en:
The game requires frequent real-time updates and player coordinates. ElastiCache for Redis keeps the data in the memory, supports geospatial data structures and radius search commands, so that it is possible to carry the writing and reading operation of the location at the same time and unload the database burden.
Option A: A Multi-AZ configuration enhances availability, but there is no improvement in performance.
Option B: OpenSearch Service is a search and analysis engine, not a storage service for frequent point coordinates.
Option C: DAX is only compatible with DynamoDB and cannot be deployed in front of the PostgreSQL instance.

options.text: Take a snapshot of the existing DB instance. Restore the snapshot with Multi-AZ enabled.
Migrate from Amazon RDS to Amazon OpenSearch Service with OpenSearch Dashboards.
Deploy Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) in front of the existing DB instance. Modify the game to use DAX.
Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the existing DB instance. Modify the game to use Redis.

question_text:
A company stores critical data in Amazon DynamoDB tables in the company's AWS account. An IT administrator accidentally deleted a DynamoDB table. The deletion caused a significant loss of data and disrupted the company's operations. The company wants to prevent this type of disruption in the future.
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The problem is not the loss of data per se, but the ability to delete the entire table. Deleting protection can be enabled by opening a switch on the table, which simply prevents the operation until it is clearly closed — without any code or backup or recovery plan.
Option A: A combination of logs, rules and restoration functions is the most complex of all constructions, and it reacts only after the deletion operation has taken place.
Option B: A backup plan with a manual recovery means a stop and manual operation, while deletion can be directly and completely stopped.
Option D: Time point restoration saves the data in the table, but if the table itself is deleted, recovery still requires manual action and will interrupt the service.

options.text: Configure a trail in AWS CloudTrail. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for delete actions. Create an AWS Lambda function to automatically restore deleted DynamoDB tables.
Create a backup and restore plan for the DynamoDB tables. Recover the DynamoDB tables manually.
Configure deletion protection on the DynamoDB tables.
Enable point-in-time recovery on the DynamoDB tables.

question_text:
A company has an on-premises data center that is running out of storage capacity. The company wants to migrate its storage infrastructure to AWS while minimizing bandwidth costs. The solution must allow for immediate retrieval of data at no additional cost.
How can these requirements be met?
explanation_en:
There are two binding requirements: to minimize the cost of bandwidth and to provide immediate access to data at no additional cost. Storage Gateway keeps the complete data set on the company's own disk in the memory scroll mode, and transmits the time point to S3. This means that the reading operation comes from a local copy, and the response is instantaneous and does not need to call the cloud, but only data changes are transmitted via a link.
Option A: Glacier storage is for archiving: fast-tracking can generate costs, which directly contradicts the expression "no extra cost".
Option B: Cache roll mode keeps only the usual subset locally, so requests for the remaining data are sent to S3 - which means that there are delays and network traffic.
Option D: A dedicated connection would entail a continuous and relatively high duplication of costs, which would require minimizing bandwidth expenditures rather than establishing a larger link.

options.text: Deploy Amazon S3 Glacier Vault and enable expedited retrieval. Enable provisioned retrieval capacity for the workload.
Deploy AWS Storage Gateway using cached volumes. Use Storage Gateway to store data in Amazon S3 while retaining copies of frequently accessed data subsets locally.
Deploy AWS Storage Gateway using stored volumes to store data locally. Use Storage Gateway to asynchronously back up point-in-time snapshots of the data to Amazon S3.

Deploy AWS Direct Connect to connect with the on-premises data center. Configure AWS Storage Gateway to store data locally. Use Storage Gateway to asynchronously back up point-in-time snapshots of the data to Amazon S3.

question_text:
A company runs a three-tier web application in a VPC across multiple Availability Zones. Amazon EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group for the application tier.
The company needs to make an automated scaling plan that will analyze each resource's daily and weekly historical workload trends. The configuration must scale resources appropriately according to both the forecast and live changes in utilization.
Which scaling strategy should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
At the same time, two things are needed: an analysis based on historical patterns of daily and weekly use, with an advance increase in capacity; and a response to changes in actual use. Predictive expansion builds projections from historical data and increases capacity before demand, while the target tracking strategy adjusts capacity to match the actual load. Both meet both needs together.
Option A: Step-up expands after-action and does not build projections from historical data at all.
Option C: The plan does not automatically analyse historical data and does not respond to deviations from the normal pattern.
Option D: A simple strategy with a longer cooling cycle is slower to react and does not provide a predictive function.

options.text: Implement dynamic scaling with step scaling based on average CPU utilization from the EC2 instances.
Enable predictive scaling to forecast and scale. Configure dynamic scaling with target tracking
Create an automated scheduled scaling action based on the traffic patterns of the web application.
Set up a simple scaling policy. Increase the cooldown period based on the EC2 instance startup time.

question_text:
A package delivery company has an application that uses Amazon EC2 instances and an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. As the application becomes more popular, EC2 instance usage increases only slightly. DB cluster usage increases at a much faster rate.
The company adds a read replica, which reduces the DB cluster usage for a short period of time. However, the load continues to increase. The operations that cause the increase in DB cluster usage are all repeated read statements that are related to delivery details. The company needs to alleviate the effect of repeated reads on the DB cluster.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The scene clearly indicates the reasons: repeat and read the same queries. The memory caches are able to respond directly to these queries and do not require access to databases, so the load of the clusters is immediately reduced and remains at low levels. ElastiCache for Redis costs much less than the additional Aurora reading example and actually solves the problem, not just cover it up.
Option B: One more reading copy is only a temporary delay: the query is still repeated, the load is up again, and eventually you need to pay for a permanent example.
Option C: Automatic expansion to read a copy only means more examples of billing, while the issue of the bottom load source remains unresolved.
Option D: Several examples of writing (multi-principal) can increase the writing capacity, but the problem is with the reading operation, and the configuration itself is more costly.

options.text: Implement an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster between the application and the DB cluster.
Add an additional read replica to the DB cluster.
Configure Aurora Auto Scaling for the Aurora read replicas.
Modify the DB cluster to have multiple writer instances.

question_text:
A company has an application that uses an Amazon DynamoDB table for storage. A solutions architect discovers that many requests to the table are not returning the latest data. The company's users have not reported any other issues with database performance. Latency is in an acceptable range.
Which design change should the solutions architect recommend?
explanation_en:
Some of the requests for returns are not up to date, and this is a sign of eventual unanimous reading, and this is the default of DynamoDB. Consistency of reading resolves this problem by returning to reflect all previously successful outcomes; delays are kept within acceptable limits, as is directly indicated in the scene.
Option A: The concept of reading a copy does not exist in the DynamoDB table.
Option B: The global secondary index is always only final and consistent, thus making data fresher rather than better.
Option D: Ultimately consistency is the act of the present, and it is that act that leads to the problem.

options.text: Add read replicas to the table.
Use a global secondary index (GSI).
Request strongly consistent reads for the table.
Request eventually consistent reads for the table.

question_text:
A company has deployed its application on Amazon EC2 instances with an Amazon RDS database. The company used the principle of least privilege to configure the database access credentials. The company's security team wants to protect the application and the database from SQL injection and other web-based attacks.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
SQL injections and other Web-based attacks arrive through applications and therefore require filtering at the application level — deployment of AWS WAF in front of the application and use of the Management Rules Group. The security team and the cyber firewall did nothing in this scenario: the attack was transmitted internally through a seemingly legitimate request through a permitted port. The latter part of the answer — the RDS parameter group set-up (e.g. request to enable TLS and configure log parameters) — adds defensive measures at the database level, but the key part of the answer is WAF.
Option A: Security group and network ACL filters according to address and port. They cannot identify the malign SQL code embedded in the permitted HTTPS request.
Option C: Network firewall filters VPC network traffic and does not parse HTTP request parameters to detect injection mode.
Option D: Separating database accounts can limit the range of damage, but cannot prevent the attack itself. The company has implemented the principle of minimum competence.

options.text: Use security groups and network ACLs to secure the database and application servers.
Use AWS WAF to protect the application. Use RDS parameter groups to configure the security settings.
Use AWS Network Firewall to protect the application and the database.
Use different database accounts in the application code for different functions. Avoid granting excessive privileges to the database users.

question_text:
An ecommerce company runs applications in AWS accounts that are part of an organization in AWS Organizations.
The applications run on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL databases across all the accounts. The company needs to prevent malicious activity and must identify abnormal failed and incomplete login attempts to the databases.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?
explanation_en:
The company needs to detect unusual and failed login attempts in its database across multiple accounts without having to build its own analytical function. Amazon GuardDuty achieved this through its RDS protection: it analyzed Aurora log-in events, looked for suspicious patterns (violent decomposition attempts, log-in from an abnormal address, unusual users) and displayed the results of the discovery. This feature is enabled at the organizational level through the commissioning of an administrator, so that all accounts can be covered once and without filtering or building storage.
Option A: A SCP refuses to operate; it does not analyse database login attempts.
Option C: Aurora General Log provides the original records in Cloudwatch, but the abnormality detection must be built from scratch: filters, thresholds, correlation analysis are required. This workload is much larger than the existing programme.
Option D: CloudTrail records the call to the RDS Management API instead of the authentication attempt inside the database.

options.text: Attach service control policies (SCPs) to the root of the organization to identity the failed login attempts.
Enable the Amazon RDS Protection feature in Amazon GuardDuty for the member accounts of the organization.
Publish the Aurora general logs to a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Export the log data to a central Amazon S3 bucket.
Publish all the Aurora PostgreSQL database events in AWS CloudTrail to a central Amazon S3 bucket.

question_text:
A company has an AWS Direct Connect connection from its corporate data center to its VPC in the us-east-1 Region. The company recently acquired a corporation that has several VPCs and a Direct Connect connection between its on-premises data center and the eu-west-2 Region. The CIDR blocks for the VPCs of the company and the corporation do not overlap. The company requires connectivity between two Regions and the data centers. The company needs a solution that is scalable while reducing operational overhead.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Following the takeover, two Direct Connect connections and many VPCs were found in different regions. Direct CONNEC Gateway is a global object that allows a single connection to any VPC virtual private gateway in any area, provided that the CIDR block does not overlap - this is confirmed in the scene. Adding a new VPC will require only one associated operation; no additional interface or tunnel is required.
Option A: Cross-regional peer connections connect VPCs, but it does not provide access to data centres and the number of reciprocal connections increases evenly.
Option B: A private virtual interface is connected to a virtual private gateway in the same region as the access point. It can't reach the VPC directly to another area -- this is the design of Direct Contact Gateway.
Option C: A network of self-managed VPN devices in EC2 cases is the maximum possible operational load, while VPN CloudHub connects to a virtual private gateway site, which is not relevant to the scenario described.

options.text: Set up inter-Region VPC peering between the VPC in us-east-1 and the VPCs in eu-west-2.
Create private virtual interfaces from the Direct Connect connection in us-east-1 to the VPCs in eu-west-2.
Establish VPN appliances in a fully meshed VPN network hosted by Amazon EC2. Use AWS VPN CloudHub to send and receive data between the data centers and each VPC.
Connect the existing Direct Connect connection to a Direct Connect gateway. Route traffic from the virtual private gateways of the VPCs in each Region to the Direct Connect gateway.

question_text:
A company is developing a mobile game that streams score updates to a backend processor and then posts results on a leaderboard. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that can handle large traffic spikes, process the mobile game updates in order of receipt, and store the processed updates in a highly available database. The company also wants to minimize the management overhead required to maintain the solution.
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The requirement is to absorb large-scale traffic peaks, to process them strictly in the order of receipt, to store the processed updates in a highly usable database and to minimize the cost of managing them. Kinesis Data Streets keeps the order of records and absorbs peak traffic in the fraction, the Lambda function can read flow without a server, and DynamoDB provides high-availability storage for the rankings.
Option B: Order is maintained, but an EC2 instance cluster needs to be maintained, and Redshift is an analytical repository rather than a high-list database.
Option C: SNS does not guarantee the order in which the message is transmitted, and the SQL database on EC2 implies weaknesses in management and availability.
Option D: Standard SQS queues cannot keep the message order, and the handling of instances still needs to be maintained.

options.text: Push score updates to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Process the updates in Kinesis Data Streams with AWS Lambda. Store the processed updates in Amazon DynamoDB.
Push score updates to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Process the updates with a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances set up for Auto Scaling. Store the processed updates in Amazon Redshift.

Push score updates to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the SNS topic to process the updates. Store the processed updates in a SQL database running on Amazon EC2.

Push score updates to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances with Auto Scaling to process the updates in the SQS queue. Store the processed updates in an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.

question_text:
A company has multiple AWS accounts with applications deployed in the us-west-2 Region. Application logs are stored within Amazon S3 buckets in each account. The company wants to build a centralized log analysis solution that uses a single S3 bucket. Logs must not leave us-west-2, and the company wants to incur minimal operational overhead.
Which solution meets these requirements and is MOST cost-effective?
explanation_en:
Logs are distributed in different account S3 buckets and need to be collected into a S3 bucket and cannot leave the us-west-2 area or rely on manual operations. The S3-regional reproduction function achieves this: the rules for configuration on each source drum will be applied to the target S3 buckets with a different degree of copying of new objects, even across the account, allowing the metadata to be preserved and the target account to have ownership of those objects. You do not need to write a code or set a time plan - you only have to pay for copying operations and storage space. Particular attention is drawn to the fact that, similar to CRRs, copying requires the use of version control and only applies to objects created after it has been enabled.
Option A: The life-cycle rule does not reproduce objects between drums - it only changes storage categories and removes objects from its own drums.
Option C: Scripts running on a daily basis replicate the entire contents of the drum, resulting in the same data being transmitted over and over again: requests are high, independent infrastructure is required to run and a one-day delay is introduced.
Option D: The Lambda function, which is triggered when the object is created, works, but each account needs to prepare a code: it needs to process errors, retest, and limit the number of times, and it incurs the cost of each call when the log is high. This has resulted in more overhead than the built-in reproduction function.

options.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy that copies the objects from one of the application S3 buckets to the centralized S3 bucket.
Use S3 Same-Region Replication to replicate logs from the S3 buckets to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.
Write a script that uses the PutObject API operation every day to copy the entire contents of the buckets to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.

Write AWS Lambda functions in these accounts that are triggered every time logs are delivered to the S3 buckets (s3:ObjectCreated:* event). Copy the logs to another S3 bucket in us-west-2. Use this S3 bucket for log analysis.

question_text:
A company has an application that delivers on-demand training videos to students around the world. The application also allows authorized content developers to upload videos. The data is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-2 Region.
The company has created an S3 bucket in the eu-west-2 Region and an S3 bucket in the ap-southeast-1 Region.
The company wants to replicate the data to the new S3 buckets. The company needs to minimize latency for developers who upload videos and students who stream videos near eu-west-2 and ap-southeast-1.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the application? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
Delays require both lower user upload and user flow media operations, so both require access to the nearest region. A self-selected entry point for the most recent S3 bucket is the S3 Multi-area Access Point, and the application should read and write through its ARN. But if writing can fall into any of the three drums, a one-way reproduction from only us-east-2 is no longer effective: a two-way reproduction (C) between all three regions is required, otherwise the video uploaded in Europe will never appear in Asia. The "lowest changes to the application" are presented as a parallel condition only — the solution must first satisfy two of the delay requirements.
Option A: Copy only from us-east-2 one-way only what is written in us-east-2. Developers cannot benefit from uploading — they still need to be transported across the sea.
Option B: Link "us-east-2 ⁇ eu-west-2 ⁇ ap-southead-1" cannot work by default: a copy will not be further copied unless it is explicitly enabled to modify the sync. In addition, the issue of delays in uploading remains unresolved.
Option D: Multi-area access points are used only for viewing, while uploading is still sent to us-east-2. Half of the delays were not met — just to save one code change in the application.

options.text: Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the eu-west-2 S3 bucket. Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the ap-southeast-1 S3 bucket.
Configure one-way replication from the us-east-2 S3 bucket to the eu-west-2 S3 bucket. Configure one-way replication from the eu-west-2 S3 bucket to the ap-southeast-1 S3 bucket.
Configure two-way (bidirectional) replication among the S3 buckets that are in all three Regions.

Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point. Modify the application to use the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Multi-Region Access Point for video streaming. Do not modify the application for video uploads.
Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point. Modify the application to use the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the Multi-Region Access Point for video streaming and uploads.

question_text:
A company has a new mobile app. Anywhere in the world, users can see local news on topics they choose. Users also can post photos and videos from inside the app.
Users access content often in the first minutes after the content is posted. New content quickly replaces older content, and then the older content disappears. The local nature of the news means that users consume 90% of the content within the AWS Region where it is uploaded.
Which solution will optimize the user experience by providing the LOWEST latency for content uploads?
explanation_en:
What needs to be optimized is the upload process and the content is consumed mainly in the same region where it is uploaded. S3 Transfer Acceleration receives files at the nearest edge of the uploader and then transfers them to the S3 buckets via the AWS backbone network, thereby reducing delays and transmission times - this is the scenario of the functionality design.
Option A: ClaudFront optimizes content distribution; uploading through it does not increase upload speed as it does with Transfer Acceleration.
Option C: The intermediate EC2 instance in each region adds an additional layer, additional costs and additional operations, without any delay advantage.
Option D: Multiple CloudFront distribution configurations are associated with content distribution and have no impact on upload speed.

options.text: Upload and store content in Amazon S3. Use Amazon CloudFront for the uploads.
Upload and store content in Amazon S3. Use S3 Transfer Acceleration for the uploads.
Upload content to Amazon EC2 instances in the Region that is closest to the user. Copy the data to Amazon S3.
Upload and store content in Amazon S3 in the Region that is closest to the user. Use multiple distributions of Amazon CloudFront.

question_text:
A company is building a new application that uses serverless architecture. The architecture will consist of an Amazon API Gateway REST API and AWS Lambda functions to manage incoming requests.
The company wants to add a service that can send messages received from the API Gateway REST API to multiple target Lambda functions for processing. The service must offer message filtering that gives the target Lambda functions the ability to receive only the messages the functions need.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
One message needs to be transmitted to multiple recipients, each of whom only obtains the required content. This is how the SNS theme model is combined with the subscription filter policy: the theme distributes messages, filters remove irrelevant content, and the SQS queue in front of the function provides a buffer and a mechanism for retrying when a failure occurs.
Option B: EventBridge can also filter and call multiple targets, but this scenario involves the distribution of applied messages, SNS-coated filters are simpler and less costly, and EventBridge cannot provide buffers before the function.
Option C: Amazon MSK is a Kafka cluster that needs configuration and mobility and cannot be published directly into a function.
Option D: Each recipient uses a separate queue which means that filtering and distribution logic must be built manually at source.

options.text: Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues to the SNS topic. Configure the target Lambda functions to poll the different SQS queues.
Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to Amazon EventBridge. Configure EventBridge to invoke the target Lambda functions.
Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK). Configure Amazon MSK to publish the messages to the target Lambda functions.
Send the requests from the API Gateway REST API to multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Configure the target Lambda functions to poll the different SQS queues.

question_text:
A company migrated millions of archival files to Amazon S3. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution that will encrypt all the archival data by using a customer-provided key. The solution must encrypt existing unencrypted objects and future objects.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The task is divided into two parts: encryption of millions of objects already uploaded, and ensuring that future uploads are also encrypted. For existing objects, the standard practice is to use the S3 Information report, which shows the encryption status of each object, which, combined with the S3 Watch Operations operation, will be copied with the required encryption. Requires the use of the "Custom Key" to point to SSE-C, where the client provides the key in each request, and S3 never stores the key. A reasonable comment on the issue itself is that SSE-C is not actually able to choose between default encryption settings (providing only the SSE-S3, SSE-KMS and DSSE-KMS options), so the second half of this option is not technically accurate - but none of the other options will solve the task.
Option B:Storage Lens displays the aggregated stored barrel statistical information instead of the unencrypted list of objects, and it does not affect objects already uploaded. In addition, SSE-KMS is not " a key provided by a customer ". "
Option C: AWS Batch is a mechanism for bulk calculation of containerized batch processing, not for mass operation of S3 objects - this is the use of S3 Batch Operations. Moreover, it was re-emphasized that it was not the critical type required.
Option D: Default encryption settings affect only newly uploaded objects. Millions of documents that have been uploaded will remain unencrypted.

options.text: Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering an Amazon S3 Inventory report. Configure an S3 Batch Operations job to encrypt the objects from the list with a server-side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C). Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C).
Use S3 Storage Lens metrics to identify unencrypted S3 buckets. Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).

Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering the AWS usage report for Amazon S3. Configure an AWS Batch job to encrypt the objects from the list with a server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
Create a list of unencrypted objects by filtering the AWS usage report for Amazon S3. Configure the S3 default encryption feature to use a server-side encryption with a customer-provided key (SSE-C).

question_text:
The DNS provider that hosts a company's domain name records is experiencing outages that cause service disruption for a website running on AWS. The company needs to migrate to a more resilient managed DNS service and wants the service to run on AWS.
What should a solutions architect do to rapidly migrate the DNS hosting service?
explanation_en:
A managed and flexible DNS service is required and should be achieved as soon as possible. A Route 53 public trust area, together with a regional file of the provider prior to import, can complete the migration of all records one step at a time; the only remaining task is to change the register's NS records. Route 5 3 is based on anycast network and provides 100% availability of SLA.
Option B: A private trust area is parsed only within the specified VPC. Public users will be completely unable to decipher the name of the site.
Option C: Simple AD and AWS Managed Microsoft AD are directory services for the Windows domain, not a public DNS area hosting service.
Option D: Resolver entrance handles queries from local networks about VPC resources. It does not make Route 53 an authoritative DNS service for public domain names, and it still makes companies dependent on previous providers.

options.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 public hosted zone for the domain name. Import the zone file containing the domain records hosted by the previous provider.
Create an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone for the domain name. Import the zone file containing the domain records hosted by the previous provider.
Create a Simple AD directory in AWS. Enable zone transfer between the DNS provider and AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for the domain records.

Create an Amazon Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the VPC. Specify the IP addresses that the provider's DNS will forward DNS queries to. Configure the provider's DNS to forward DNS queries for the domain to the IP addresses that are specified in the inbound endpoint.

question_text:
A company is building an application on AWS that connects to an Amazon RDS database. The company wants to manage the application configuration and to securely store and retrieve credentials for the database and other services.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?
explanation_en:
There are two clear tasks: application configuration and key. AWS AppConfig is used to store and publish configurations to support validation and incremental deployment, while Secrets Manager is used to store encryption certificates, distributed by character and automatically rotate key for RDS. Each tool is used for its design and no code is required. A useful distinction: Parameter Store applies to parameters and simple keys and is less costly but does not have built-in automatic rotation.
Option B: Lambda is a code execution environment, not a configuration storage. Parameter Store cannot automatically rotate the database password.
Option C: File stored in a barrel means manually updated, manually rotated, and you need to build your own access controls. The largest workload.
Option D: Storage of the database evidence in the database itself is circular: you need to connect to the database to read the password, but you need a password to connect to the database.

options.text: Use AWS AppConfig to store and manage the application configuration. Use AWS Secrets Manager to store and retrieve the credentials.
Use AWS Lambda to store and manage the application configuration. Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to store and retrieve the credentials.
Use an encrypted application configuration file. Store the file in Amazon S3 for the application configuration. Create another S3 file to store and retrieve the credentials.
Use AWS AppConfig to store and manage the application configuration. Use Amazon RDS to store and retrieve the credentials.

question_text:
To meet security requirements, a company needs to encrypt all of its application data in transit while communicating with an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance. A recent security audit revealed that encryption at rest is enabled using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS), but data in transit is not enabled.
What should a solutions architect do to satisfy the security requirements?
explanation_en:
Static encryption has been activated; the remaining problem is the protection of the transmission channel. RDS defaults to provide TLS connections, but the client must trust the server 's certificate: This means that the AWS root certificate package (global-bundle package) needs to be downloaded and quoted in the connection string and the authentication is enabled (for MySQL, VERIFY_CA or VERIFY_INTY mode). In addition, the parameter group can require all connections to use TLS - For MySQL, require_security_transport.
Option A: IAM database authentication changes the way you log in to the database, not whether the application traffic is encrypted. It does not address the security needs in the transmission.
Option B: The self-signed certificate is useless here: the server will provide its own certificate issued by the AWS certificate issuer, and the client must trust the certificate.
Option C: A snapshot and recovery operation to enable encryption is a security measure for static data, which is described in the title as having been enabled.

options.text: Enable IAM database authentication on the database.
Provide self-signed certificates. Use the certificates in all connections to the RDS instance.
Take a snapshot of the RDS instance. Restore the snapshot to a new instance with encryption enabled.
Download AWS-provided root certificates. Provide the certificates in all connections to the RDS instance.

question_text:
A company is designing a new web service that will run on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. However, many of the web service clients can only reach IP addresses authorized on their firewalls.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet the clients’ needs?
explanation_en:
Original answer: C; source correction answer: A.
NLB supports a flexible IP for each available area, which is not supported by ALB; option C (Accounting to the flexible IP address) does not describe a configuration valid before the ELB. examtopics t1 q744
NLB can map a fixed Elastic IP in a usable area for a customer's firewall; AALB cannot bind Elastic IP directly. The Route 53A record of source C cannot point an Elastic IP to a changing load balancer target, and change it to A.
The client only allows traffic through an authorized address through the firewall, so the load balancer requires a fixed IP address. A flexible IP address can only be assigned to the Network Load Balancer (A) - one for each available area.
Option B: ALB does not support flexible IP addresses: it has only one DNS name and the address behind it changes. This load equalizer cannot be added to the permitted list.
Option C: A record pointing to a flexible IP address does not by itself describe a valid configuration: the address still requires an additional object and cannot be attached to the ALB.
Option D: The placement of an EC2 agent in front of the load balancer provides a static address, but it introduces a self-managed node and a new failure point, while NLB solves the problem.

options.text: A Network Load Balancer with an associated Elastic IP address.
An Application Load Balancer with an associated Elastic IP address.
An A record in an Amazon Route 53 hosted zone pointing to an Elastic IP address.
An EC2 instance with a public IP address running as a proxy in front of the load balancer.

question_text:
A company has established a new AWS account. The account is newly provisioned and no changes have been made to the default settings. The company is concerned about the security of the AWS account root user.
What should be done to secure the root user?
explanation_en:
Basic health measures for the new account: Stop using the root account for daily operations and protect it through multifactorial certification. The IAM user should be used for daily tasks (or better access through roles or IAM Infrastructure Center), while the root account is reserved for only a few operations that cannot be performed elsewhere — closing the account, changing the support plan, restoring the account. The root account will never create access keys, and if such keys exist, they should be deleted immediately.
Option A: Root user cannot disable or delete: it exists throughout the life of the account. It can only be protected.
Option C: Create access keys for root and use them as opposed to the recommendation: such keys cannot be limited by strategy.
Option D: Giving a root certificate to a particular person does not make the account safer: the operation cannot be traced back to a specific individual and the authority remains unrestricted.

options.text: Create IAM users for daily administrative tasks. Disable the root user.
Create IAM users for daily administrative tasks. Enable multi-factor authentication on the root user.
Generate an access key for the root user. Use the access key for daily administration tasks instead of the AWS Management Console.
Provide the root user credentials to the most senior solutions architect. Have the solutions architect use the root user for daily administration tasks.

question_text:
A company is deploying an application that processes streaming data in near-real time. The company plans to use Amazon EC2 instances for the workload. The network architecture must be configurable to provide the lowest possible latency between nodes.
Which combination of network solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
The minimum delay between nodes is achieved at two levels. A cluster placement group wraps examples as closely as possible within a single available area (Availability Zone), thus achieving maximum throughput and minimum nodal delay (C). An ENA enhancement with SR-IOV support eliminates virtualization costs and reduces dithering (A).
Option B: Distribution of examples in different accounts does not have an impact on network delays and will only add to the complexity of management.
Option D: Multiple network interfaces on the example add address and traffic isolation but do not reduce delays.
Option E: EBS optimizes the allocation of a separate bandwidth path to disk operations, independent of traffic between nodes.

options.text: Enable and configure enhanced networking on each EC2 instance.
Group the EC2 instances in separate accounts.
Run the EC2 instances in a cluster placement group.
Attach multiple elastic network interfaces to each EC2 instance.
Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) optimized instance types.

question_text:
A financial services company wants to shut down two data centers and migrate more than 100 TB of data to AWS.
The data has an intricate directory structure with millions of small files stored in deep hierarchies of subfolders.
Most of the data is unstructured, and the company’s file storage consists of SMB-based storage types from multiple vendors. The company does not want to change its applications to access the data after migration.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The defining details are the SMB protocol and the requirement that no change be made to the application. This means that the target storage must remain file type and supports SMB - that is, Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. AWS DataSync is responsible for migration: it is capable of handling millions of small files and deep nested directories, maintaining structures and privileges, validating data integrity and achieving incremental operation.
Option A: S3 is an object storage that does not support SMB protocols: an application needs to be rewrited and DirectConnect cannot move data alone.
Option B: FSx for Lustre is designed for high performance calculations, using the Lustre protocol instead of SMB.
Option D: Volume gateway provides a block volume through iSCSI instead of SMB file sharing: the way the application accesss data will change.

options.text: Use AWS Direct Connect to migrate the data to Amazon S3.
Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon FSx for Lustre.
Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.
Use AWS Direct Connect to migrate the data on-premises file storage to an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway.

question_text:
A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage AWS accounts that contain applications. The company sets up a dedicated monitoring member account in the organization. The company wants to query and visualize observability data across the accounts by using Amazon CloudWatch.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Collecting indicators, logs and tracking data from multiple accounts and concentrating them in one place is an built-in function of Cloudwatch - cross-account detectability. This feature is activated in the observer account in the form of a monitoring account, while a small template is deployed in the source account to achieve data sharing. Then the dashboards and queries in the monitored account will see all the data from the connection account, without copying or creating a role for each query.
Option B: SCPs limits permissions only. They will not grant access to data from another account.
Option C: Each account has an IAM user and its strategy that means that long-term vouchers and each account need to be configured manually, and that data still need to be viewed on an account-by-account basis.
Option D: Adopt the same scheme, i.e. user and cross-account strategies: this option is feasible but requires role-to-play, and does not provide a uniform view in the Cloudwatch console.

options.text: Enable CloudWatch cross-account observability for the monitoring account. Deploy an AWS CloudFormation template provided by the monitoring account in each AWS account to share the data with the monitoring account.
Set up service control policies (SCPs) to provide access to CloudWatch in the monitoring account under the Organizations root organizational unit (OU).

Configure a new IAM user in the monitoring account. In each AWS account, configure an IAM policy to have access to query and visualize the CloudWatch data in the account. Attach the new IAM policy to the new IAM user.
Create a new IAM user in the monitoring account. Create cross-account IAM policies in each AWS account. Attach the IAM policies to the new IAM user.

question_text:
A company’s website is used to sell products to the public. The site runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). There is also an Amazon CloudFront distribution, and AWS WAF is being used to protect against SQL injection attacks. The ALB is the origin for the CloudFront distribution. A recent review of security logs revealed an external malicious IP that needs to be blocked from accessing the website.
What should a solutions architect do to protect the application?
explanation_en:
The entry is CloudFront, and WAF has been attached, so just add an IP matching rule to the existing web ACL for the wrong address. The request was discarded at the edge and never reached the load balancer or instance. Network access control lists (Network ACLs) and security units are useless here: when the flow arrives, it already comes from CloudFront and ALB, not from the original address of the client.
Option A: ClaudFront distributed service does not have a web access control list: it is a global service, not a resource within you VPC.
Option C: The example shows the address of the load balancer, not the address of the client, and therefore prevents an address at the subnet level without effect.
Option D: Same reason: The security group filters the source address of the example, which is ALB.

options.text: Modify the network ACL on the CloudFront distribution to add a deny rule for the malicious IP address.
Modify the configuration of AWS WAF to add an IP match condition to block the malicious IP address.
Modify the network ACL for the EC2 instances in the target groups behind the ALB to deny the malicious IP address.
Modify the security groups for the EC2 instances in the target groups behind the ALB to deny the malicious IP address.

question_text:
A company sets up an organization in AWS Organizations that contains 10 AWS accounts. A solutions architect must design a solution to provide access to the accounts for several thousand employees. The company has an existing identity provider (IdP). The company wants to use the existing IdP for authentication to AWS.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Thousands of employees, ten accounts, and already existing identity providers -- this is the scene of IAM Identity Center. It connects to an external identity provider via SAML, the user and group synchronizes through SCIM, and access to the account is granted by assigning the permission set to the group. The employee uses his or her business certificate to log in and obtain a temporary role. Do not need to create any IAM user.
Option A: The number of IAM users in each account, for thousands of employees, is the cumbersome manual work that Identity Center eliminates. The Identity Federation is not about "IAM users" configuration -- it's about role configuration.
Option B: An account has only one root user and is not designed for employees. It is neither possible nor safe to synchronize it with the directory.
Option D: AWS RAM shares resources between accounts; it does not grant access to accounts.

options.text: Create IAM users for the employees in the required AWS accounts. Connect IAM users to the existing IdP. Configure federated authentication for the IAM users.
Set up AWS account root users with user email addresses and passwords that are synchronized from the existing IdP.
Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Connect IAM Identity Center to the existing IdP. Provision users and groups from the existing IdP.
Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share access to the AWS accounts with the users in the existing IdP.

question_text:
A solutions architect is designing an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) authorization model for a company's AWS account. The company has designated five specific employees to have full access to AWS services and resources in the AWS account.
The solutions architect has created an IAM user for each of the five designated employees and has created an IAM user group.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Five staff members need full access, and the simplest option is to give them one-time access to a group. Full access is described by the Administrator Access management strategy and is an identity-based strategy: it is attached to the user, group or role. Resource-based strategies are resources (e.g., S3 buckets, queues, KMS keys) that cannot be added to the IAM group - this distinction is the basis of the wrong option.
Option A: Administrator Access is an addition to the subject (i.e. identity) and is an identity-based strategy. It is not a resource-based strategy.
Option B: SystemAdministrator grants a wide range of access rights, but not full access: Several operations, including IAM and billing management, are excluded. The title calls for full access.
Option D: The policy type name is wrong and the policy does not itself grant full access.

options.text: Attach the AdministratorAccess resource-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
Attach the SystemAdministrator identity-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
Attach the AdministratorAccess identity-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.
Attach the SystemAdministrator resource-based policy to the IAM user group. Place each of the five designated employee IAM users in the IAM user group.

question_text:
A company has a multi-tier payment processing application that is based on virtual machines (VMs). The communication between the tiers occurs asynchronously through a third-party middleware solution that guarantees exactly-once delivery.
The company needs a solution that requires the least amount of infrastructure management. The solution must guarantee exactly-once delivery for application messaging.
Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
Accurate single delivery and minimal infrastructure management are essential. In AWS, only the SQS FIFO queue ensures an accurate processing - it also keeps the message in order (D). No server calculation is provided by AWS Lambda, which supports reading (A) from such queues.
Option B: The EC2 instance requires round-the-clock maintenance - which contradicts the requirement to minimize management.
Option C: SNS guarantees at least one delivery and may deliver the message several times: this is not acceptable for payment.
Option E: An EKS cluster means managing nodes and the Kubernetes platform itself.

options.text: Use AWS Lambda for the compute layers in the architecture.
Use Amazon EC2 instances for the compute layers in the architecture.
Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) as the messaging component between the compute layers.
Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues as the messaging component between the compute layers.
Use containers that are based on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) for the compute layers in the architecture.

question_text:
A company has a nightly batch processing routine that analyzes report files that an on-premises file system receives daily through SFTP. The company wants to move the solution to the AWS Cloud. The solution must be highly available and resilient. The solution also must minimize operational effort.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
Minimum operating costs are achieved by not running a self-managed SFTP server: AWS Transport Family is a managed, highly available service, while S3 provides a level 119 persistence. The night batch operation is operated by an example initiated by the Movement Control Team Auto Scaling, which pulls files from the S3 buckets, processes them and then closes them.
Option A: The service and calculation choice is correct, but the EFS is more expensive as a storage than S3 and does not need to: the file needs to be written once, read once at night.
Option B: Running a self-managed SFTP server on an instance requires patching and maintenance, and EBS rolls are tied to a single available area - less robust and more operational.
Option C: The same self-managed SFTP server and all its operating expenses: Replace EBS with EFS does not change this.

options.text: Deploy AWS Transfer for SFTP and an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for storage. Use an Amazon EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group with a scheduled scaling policy to run the batch operation.

Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance that runs Linux and an SFTP service. Use an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for storage. Use an Auto Scaling group with the minimum number of instances and desired number of instances set to 1.

Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance that runs Linux and an SFTP service. Use an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for storage. Use an Auto Scaling group with the minimum number of instances and desired number of instances set to 1.

Deploy AWS Transfer for SFTP and an Amazon S3 bucket for storage. Modify the application to pull the batch files from Amazon S3 to an Amazon EC2 instance for processing. Use an EC2 instance in an Auto Scaling group with a scheduled scaling policy to run the batch operation.

question_text:
A company has users all around the world accessing its HTTP-based application deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions. The company wants to improve the availability and performance of the application. The company also wants to protect the application against common web exploits that may affect availability, compromise security, or consume excessive resources. Static IP addresses are required.
What should a solutions architect recommend to accomplish this?
explanation_en:
Reference answer: D; disputed option: B.
Static IP address requirements met by Global Accelerator(B) - CloudFront does not have static IP address; also, option B is attached to ALB with WAF working correctly
Global Accerator provides fixed IP and performance/facility transfer for cross-regional ALB; WAF can hang on ALB to protect against common Web attacks. Former D-Claud Front does not provide the required fixed access IP to B; the direct deployment of WAF on NLB A/C is not valid.
Source answer D's original resolution (in conflict with verification results, not accepted):
The title points to three requirements, the third of which is decisive: "The need for static IP addresses. " Only AWS Global Accelerator provides static address - CloudFront has no fixed IP address; its address will change. The second requirement, to prevent a common Web attack, is provided by AWS WAF, which can be attached to ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway, AppSync and Cognito, but cannot be attached to NLB. The intersectional pointer option B for two conditions: each region uses ALB, WAF attached to ALB, where Global Accerator is located. The source practice material key points to D, where the WAF is located correctly, but there is no static address - the issue is therefore marked as controversial.
Source old option A: AWS WAF cannot be attached to the Network Load Balancer: NLB runs on the 4th floor and does not belong to the resource type supported by WAF.
Source old option B: This is the only option that meets all three requirements, including static IP addresses from Global Accerator. And that's exactly what it's at odds with the source's practice material, Key.
Source old option C: The same WAF attachment error to NLB plus CloudFront does not provide the static IP address requested by the title.

options.text: Put the EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the NLBs. Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator and register the NLBs as endpoints.
Put the EC2 instances behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the ALBs. Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator and register the ALBs as endpoints.

Put the EC2 instances behind Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in each Region. Deploy AWS WAF on the NLBs. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the NLBs.

Put the EC2 instances behind Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in each Region. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the ALBs. Deploy AWS WAF on the CloudFront distribution.

question_text:
A company’s data platform uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. The database has multiple read replicas and multiple DB instances across different Availability Zones. Users have recently reported errors from the database that indicate that there are too many connections. The company wants to reduce the failover time by 20% when a read replica is promoted to primary writer.
Which solution will meet this requirement?
explanation_en:
Symptoms of "too many connections" and the goal of accelerated failure switching are addressed through the same tool. RDS Proxy maintains and reuses to clusters' connectors pools, which mitigates the depletion of connections, and when a copy is upgraded to write to an example, it re-directs the connection to the new write-in itself — which, according to AWS, reduces the failure time by more than 60 per cent and clearly exceeds the required 20 per cent.
Option A: Switch from Aurora to RDS is a regression of the rate of the failure switch: Aurora's failure switch is faster.
Options C: DynamoDB and DAX imply rewrite applications that have nothing to do with the failure rate of the Aurora cluster.
Option D: Redshift is an analytical data repository; it does not process the transactional load.

options.text: Switch from Aurora to Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ cluster deployment.
Use Amazon RDS Proxy in front of the Aurora database.
Switch to Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for read connections.
Switch to Amazon Redshift with relocation capability.

question_text:
A company stores text files in Amazon S3. The text files include customer chat messages, date and time information, and customer personally identifiable information (PII).
The company needs a solution to provide samples of the conversations to an external service provider for quality control. The external service provider needs to randomly pick sample conversations up to the most recent conversation. The company must not share the customer PII with the external service provider. The solution must scale when the number of customer conversations increases.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The data must have removed the personal information, always reflect the most up-to-date content of the dialogue and not repeat the document. S3 Object Lambda inserts a function directly into the object 's reading path: the provider access point, the function removes personal data in real time while running, the source drum remains unchanged and the extension occurs automatically.
Option B: Batch processing on an example will create a second copy of each document, lag behind the latest conversation content and require the maintenance of a machine.
Option C: Run a web application on an example that requires more customized codes and infrastructure for the same task.
Option D: Moving part of the data to a table changes the output format and still requires the maintenance of a handler for each new file.

options.text: Create an Object Lambda Access Point. Create an AWS Lambda function that redacts the PII when the function reads the file. Instruct the external service provider to access the Object Lambda Access Point.

Create a batch process on an Amazon EC2 instance that regularly reads all new files, redacts the PII from the files, and writes the redacted files to a different S3 bucket. Instruct the external service provider to access the bucket that does not contain the PII.

Create a web application on an Amazon EC2 instance that presents a list of the files, redacts the PII from the files, and allows the external service provider to download new versions of the files that have the PII redacted.

Create an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create an AWS Lambda function that reads only the data in the files that does not contain PII. Configure the Lambda function to store the non-PII data in the DynamoDB table when a new file is written to Amazon S3. Grant the external service provider access to the DynamoDB table.

question_text:
A company is running a legacy system on an Amazon EC2 instance. The application code cannot be modified, and the system cannot run on more than one instance. A solutions architect must design a resilient solution that can improve the recovery time for the system.
What should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The application cannot be modified and cannot run on multiple instances, so horizontal expansion is not feasible - the only adjustable option is to speed up recovery. When the StatusCheckFailed_System indicator triggers the claudwatch alarm, the resumption of the operation will reset the example to ensure that it runs on health hardware, thus retaining its example ID, the private IP address and the attached volume.
Option A: Termination of protection will prevent accidental deletion, but no restoration operation will be performed in case of hardware failure.
Option B: EC2 instance does not have multi-usable area (Multi-AZ) configuration: this is the attribute of the hosting database.
Option D: RAID between volumes prevents a single disk from malfunctioning, but not the example itself or its bottom host.

options.text: Enable termination protection for the EC2 instance.
Configure the EC2 instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to recover the EC2 instance in case of failure.
Launch the EC2 instance with two Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes that use RAID configurations for storage redundancy.

question_text:
A company wants to deploy its containerized application workloads to a VPC across three Availability Zones. The company needs a solution that is highly available across Availability Zones. The solution must require minimal changes to the application.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
Packagings, three available areas, minimal changes to the application and minimum operations -- this is Amazon ECS. The automatic extension of services to match target tracking functions maintains the number of tasks required, with at least three missions ensuring that each available area exists and that the decentralized placement strategy on the attributes of the available area will evenly spread the tasks to each available area.
Option B: Self-managed EKS nodes imply that the company needs to operate the Kubernetes cluster and its nodes simultaneously: there is a marked increase in the operational workload.
Option C: The EC2 instance in the placement group gives up packaging organization and reverts to the task of managing the machine.
Option D: Convert containerization applications to the Lambda function requires a rewrite of the code, while the requirement explicitly requires minimal changes.
