options.text: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Configure Amazon ECS Service Auto Scaling to use target tracking scaling. Set the minimum capacity to 3. Set the task placement strategy type to spread with an Availability Zone attribute.
Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) self-managed nodes. Configure Application Auto Scaling to use target tracking scaling. Set the minimum capacity to 3.
Use Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances. Launch three EC2 instances in a spread placement group. Configure an Auto Scaling group to use target tracking scaling. Set the minimum capacity to 3.
Use an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to connect to a VPC. Configure Application Auto Scaling to use Lambda as a scalable target. Set the minimum capacity to 3.

question_text:
A media company stores movies in Amazon S3. Each movie is stored in a single video file that ranges from 1 GB to 10 GB in size.
The company must be able to provide the streaming content of a movie within 5 minutes of a user purchase. There is higher demand for movies that are less than 20 years old than for movies that are more than 20 years old. The company wants to minimize hosting service costs based on demand.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Demand splits were clearly identified: new films were viewed with high frequency and unpredictable frequency, while old films were rarely seen. In the case of new films, the use of smart stratification storage without speculation and without search costs; in the case of old films, the use of Glacier Flexible Retrieval, the cheapest storage category, still allows quick access to files. The requirement of " within five minutes of the user's purchase" is met by quick retrieval, and this feature can be returned to the archive within one to five minutes. It is worth noting that in practical applications: fast-tracking of archived files of up to 250 MB sizes makes it optimistic to commit to five minutes for 10 GB films - but in the examination, fast-tracking is considered an answer that meets the 'minutes' requirement.
Option A: "Moving only once when demand falls" is not a function that life-cycle rules can achieve: it is based on the age of the object rather than on demand. In addition, a single smart stratification storage category cannot provide two different price points for two different types of film.
Option B: Standard smart layer storage allows immediate return of the file, thus meeting the time requirement, but storage of old films costs about three times as much as Glacier. Costs have not been minimized.
Option D: Bulk search from Glacier Flexible Retrieval takes 5-12 hours. A user who just paid for the film won't wait so long.

options.text: Store all media content in Amazon S3. Use S3 Lifecycle policies to move media data into the Infrequent Access tier when the demand for a movie decreases.

Store newer movie video files in S3 Standard. Store older movie video files in S3 Standard-infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). When a user orders an older movie, retrieve the video file by using standard retrieval.

Store newer movie video files in S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Store older movie video files in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. When a user orders an older movie, retrieve the video file by using expedited retrieval.
Store newer movie video files in S3 Standard. Store older movie video files in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. When a user orders an older movie, retrieve the video file by using bulk retrieval.

question_text:
A solutions architect needs to design the architecture for an application that a vendor provides as a Docker container image. The container needs 50 GB of storage available for temporary files. The infrastructure must be serverless.
Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The infrastructure must be server-free and the packaging requires 50 GB space for temporary files. ECS runs pre-built mirrors on Fargate without a single example and an EFS volume will be added to the task, providing the space required and without the need for capacity planning. There is no need to manage anything: no no nodes, no disk.
Option A: S3 drums cannot be mounted as a volume on the Lambda function and the temporary storage space for the function is limited to 10 GB.
Option B: EBS volume cannot be attached to the Lambda function: this function does not exist.
Option D: The EC2 start-up type means that there is a need to manage case clusters on its own, so infrastructure is no longer a server-free structure.

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the Docker container image with an Amazon S3 mounted volume that has more than 50 GB of space.
Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the Docker container image with an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that has more than 50 GB of space.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses the AWS Fargate launch type. Create a task definition for the container image with an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. Create a service with that task definition.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that uses the Amazon EC2 launch type with an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that has more than 50 GB of space. Create a task definition for the container image. Create a service with that task definition.

question_text:
A company needs to use its on-premises LDAP directory service to authenticate its users to the AWS Management Console. The directory service is not compatible with Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML).
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
The catalogue does not support SAML and therefore no standard federal identification can be achieved. The rest is the classic identification agent mode: a custom application authenticates user identification against LDAP, then calls AWS STS (AssumeRole or GetFederationToken) and transmits a temporary voucher and a console login URL to the user. The core idea is that access to AWS is always obtained through temporary STS certificates, and that prior to that, authentication methods could be used in any way.
Option A: IAM Infrastructure Center connects external providers through SAML or through AD. A directory that does not support SAML cannot be integrated in this way.
Option B: IAM policy is not "embedded in LDAP": it describes privileges in AWS, not an authentication mechanism.
Option C: synchronizing with LDAP passwords will leave a long-standing IAM key with a certificate that does not provide a single point login. This is a self-study synchronization programme, not a federal identification programme.

options.text: Enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) between AWS and the on-premises LDAP.
Create an IAM policy that uses AWS credentials, and integrate the policy into LDAP.
Set up a process that rotates the IAM credentials whenever LDAP credentials are updated.
Develop an on-premises custom identity broker application or process that uses AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to get short-lived credentials.

question_text:
A company stores multiple Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) in an AWS account to launch its Amazon EC2 instances. The AMIs contain critical data and configurations that are necessary for the company’s operations. The company wants to implement a solution that will recover accidentally deleted AMIs quickly and efficiently.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The task is to quickly recover an AMI that was accidentally deleted and to operate as little as possible. AWS provides a wastebin function, which is designed for this purpose: once the rules are set, the removed mirrors and snapshots will be placed in the wastebin and retained for the duration of the configuration, which can be restored through a single operation. No copy is required, no additional account is required, no script is required.
Option A: Snapshots in different accounts imply self-constructing reproduction automation and manual restoration of mirror images from the snapshot.
Option B: Scripts, plans and extra storage space are required to copy mirrors to another account on a regular basis.
Option D: AMIs cannot simply upload to S3 cans: they are not files, but EC2 service entities.

options.text: Create Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshots of the AMIs. Store the snapshots in a separate AWS account.
Copy all AMIs to another AWS account periodically.
Create a retention rule in Recycle Bin.
Upload the AMIs to an Amazon S3 bucket that has Cross-Region Replication.

question_text:
A company has 150 TB of archived image data stored on-premises that needs to be moved to the AWS Cloud within the next month. The company’s current network connection allows up to 100 Mbps uploads for this purpose during the night only.
What is the MOST cost-effective mechanism to move this data and meet the migration deadline?
explanation_en:
Mathematical calculations: 150 TB data are uploaded at 100 Mbps only at night, taking about one year to complete the transmission, and the deadline is only one month. The possibility of network connectivity can be ruled out by arithmetic alone, so data must be transmitted by physical means. Multiple Snowball equipment can be ordered in parallel, filled and shipped to AWS; the only costs incurred are rental and freight costs.
Option A: Snowmobile is a truck-scale device for dozens of petabytes: for 150 TB data, it is too expensive and organized in an unbalanced and lengthy manner.
Option C: Transfer Acceleration can speed up uploading, but it is still limited to the original 100 Mbps connection of the company: transmission cannot be completed by the deadline.
Option D: An end point and a VPN cannot increase the bandwidth of the connection: the arithmetic calculation remains unchanged.

options.text: Use AWS Snowmobile to ship the data to AWS.
Order multiple AWS Snowball devices to ship the data to AWS.
Enable Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration and securely upload the data.
Create an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint and establish a VPN to upload the data.

question_text:
A company wants to migrate its three-tier application from on premises to AWS. The web tier and the application tier are running on third-party virtual machines (VMs). The database tier is running on MySQL.
The company needs to migrate the application by making the fewest possible changes to the architecture. The company also needs a database solution that can restore data to a specific point in time.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The task is to relocate all three tiers in a minimally modified manner and to restore the point of time. Virtual machine migration to EC2 instance, database migration to Amazon RDS for MySQL: The same engine, which already contains time point restoration. Both application levels are located in a privately owned subnet, consistent with the fact that servers in local data centres are not directly exposed to the Internet; only load balancers are external.
Option B: Aurora MySQL is a different cluster engine, which implies a larger structural change than is necessary, and the web layer migrates to the public subnet.
Option C: The database selection is correct, but the configuration of the web example to have a public address is an unnecessary change to the network model compared to the original structure.
Option D: The location of the database in the public subnet is a serious security error and the engine is changed again and is not necessary at all.

options.text: Migrate the web tier and the application tier to Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon RDS for MySQL in private subnets.
Migrate the web tier to Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Migrate the application tier to EC2 instances in private subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon Aurora MySQL in private subnets.
Migrate the web tier to Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Migrate the application tier to EC2 instances in private subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon RDS for MySQL in private subnets.
Migrate the web tier and the application tier to Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Migrate the database tier to Amazon Aurora MySQL in public subnets.

question_text:
A development team is collaborating with another company to create an integrated product. The other company needs to access an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue that is contained in the development team's account. The other company wants to poll the queue without giving up its own account permissions to do so.
How should a solutions architect provide access to the SQS queue?
explanation_en:
Partners need to read queues in another account while still using their own vouchers. This is what the resource-based strategy on the queue itself provides — a SQS access strategy that designates the subject from the partner account and grants the sqs:ReceivedMessage and sqs:DeleteMessage privileges on that particular queue. Partners use their own role to visit the queue, neither implement role assumptions nor transmit any authority. General rule: For resources that support a resource-based strategy, cross-account access may be granted directly without the use of AssumeRole.
Option A: The instance profile attachments a role to an EC2 instance in your account. It has nothing to do with the delegation of authority to another account.
Option B: The IAM policy in your account describes the permissions of your own subject. It would not grant any authority to the subject of another account in the absence of authority on the side of the resource.
Option D: SNS theme strategy controls access to the subject, rather than access to SQS queues.

options.text: Create an instance profile that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
Create an IAM policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
Create an SQS access policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.
Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) access policy that provides the other company access to the SQS queue.

question_text:
A company’s developers want a secure way to gain SSH access on the company's Amazon EC2 instances that run the latest version of Amazon Linux. The developers work remotely and in the corporate office.
The company wants to use AWS services as a part of the solution. The EC2 instances are hosted in a VPC private subnet and access the internet through a NAT gateway that is deployed in a public subnet.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Developers work both in offices and remotely, for example in private sub-networks, where companies need to provide access in the cheapest way. Ssession Manager can solve this problem without any additional resources: the proxy in the example will establish an outward connection to the service, so there is no need to jumpboard, open port, VPN or SSH keys. The example is given a role with the AmazonSSMManaged InstanceCore strategy. Developer access is described by the IAM policy and the session will be recorded. The service is free of charge per se - you only have to pay for examples.
Option A: The jumper set in the same private subnet cannot be accessed from the outside, and ec2: CreateVpnConnect permissions are not related to EC2 Information. The programme is unable to work.
Option B: Two separate VPN configurations — one for the office and one for remote work — mean that each equipment requires a continuing cost and configuration.
Option C: A jumper set in a public subnet means additional examples, an open SSH port, and the management of the key and address list. It's more expensive and less secure than the President Manager.

options.text: Create a bastion host in the same subnet as the EC2 instances. Grant the ec2:CreateVpnConnection IAM permission to the developers. Install EC2 Instance Connect so that the developers can connect to the EC2 instances.

Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the corporate network and the VPC. Instruct the developers to use the Site-to-Site VPN connection to access the EC2 instances when the developers are on the corporate network. Instruct the developers to set up another VPN connection for access when they work remotely.

Create a bastion host in the public subnet of the VPConfigure the security groups and SSH keys of the bastion host to only allow connections and SSH authentication from the developers’ corporate and remote networks. Instruct the developers to connect through the bastion host by using SSH to reach the EC2 instances.

Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore IAM policy to an IAM role that is associated with the EC2 instances. Instruct the developers to use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to access the EC2 instances.

question_text:
A pharmaceutical company is developing a new drug. The volume of data that the company generates has grown exponentially over the past few months. The company's researchers regularly require a subset of the entire dataset to be immediately available with minimal lag. However, the entire dataset does not need to be accessed on a daily basis. All the data currently resides in on-premises storage arrays, and the company wants to reduce ongoing capital expenses.
Which storage solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The company wants to reduce capital expenditure on its local arrays, but researchers need an available subset of instant access to data, whereas complete data sets are not required on a daily basis. Cache roll gateways meet this demand in the cache scroll mode: complete data sets are stored in S3 and the frequently used portion is kept in local caches, thus keeping the delay in the working subset to a minimum and local arrays no longer need to be expanded.
Option A: DataSync moves the data to S3 as planned, but it does not provide local applications with quick access to the subset or retain familiar access.
Option B: The file gateway solves the problem of file sharing, but the data exists in block storage arrays rather than on the file server.
Option D: Access to EFS through VPN tunnels means that each visit produces a chain delay: it does not meet the demand for immediate access to the work subset.

options.text: Run AWS DataSync as a scheduled cron job to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket on an ongoing basis.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway with an Amazon S3 bucket as the target storage. Migrate the data to the Storage Gateway appliance.
Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway with cached volumes with an Amazon S3 bucket as the target storage. Migrate the data to the Storage Gateway appliance.
Configure an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection from the on-premises environment to AWS. Migrate data to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system.

question_text:
A company has a business-critical application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application stores data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company must be able to revert the table to any point within the last 24 hours.
Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
Restores the table to any point of time in the last 24 hours is a typical description of DynamoDB's mid-point recovery. It is open through a switch, provides second-level precision and maintains a 35-day historical record — no code or set-up plan.
Option B: AWS Backup will create a copy as planned: You cannot restore it to any minute between two copies.
Option C: An hourly backup by a function means that a custom code is required and may result in the loss of data for up to one hour.
Option D: Change stream provides log records, but you need to prepare your own recovery logic.

options.text: Configure point-in-time recovery for the table.
Use AWS Backup for the table.
Use an AWS Lambda function to make an on-demand backup of the table every hour.
Turn on streams on the table to capture a log of all changes to the table in the last 24 hours. Store a copy of the stream in an Amazon S3 bucket.

question_text:
A company hosts an application used to upload files to an Amazon S3 bucket. Once uploaded, the files are processed to extract metadata, which takes less than 5 seconds. The volume and frequency of the uploads varies from a few files each hour to hundreds of concurrent uploads. The company has asked a solutions architect to design a cost-effective architecture that will meet these requirements.
What should the solutions architect recommend?
explanation_en:
The processing time was less than five seconds and the load fluctuated from several documents per hour to hundreds and was uploaded. A direct call to the Lambda function for an S3 object creation notification is complete: you pay for the actual call, the automatic extension is achieved and no intermediate service is required.
Option A: ClaudTrail log records delays in API calls and is not used for trigger processing, while AppSync is a GraphQL API service.
Option C: Kinesis Data Streams increases billing flow and fraction management, and standard drum notifications are sufficient.
Option D: The SNS theme itself does not process the file, which is designed to store the unnecessary connection between the drum and the function.

options.text: Configure AWS CloudTrail trails to log S3 API calls. Use AWS AppSync to process the files.
Configure an object-created event notification within the S3 bucket to invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the files.
Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process and send data to Amazon S3. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the files.
Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to process the files uploaded to Amazon S3. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to process the files.

question_text:
A company’s application is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances and uses AWS Lambda functions for an event-driven architecture. The company uses nonproduction development environments in a different AWS account to test new features before the company deploys the features to production.
The production instances show constant usage because of customers in different time zones. The company uses nonproduction instances only during business hours on weekdays. The company does not use the nonproduction instances on the weekends. The company wants to optimize the costs to run its application on AWS.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The two loads have different usage characteristics and therefore require different pricing models. Production examples run day-to-day - For these examples, the Compute Savings Plan offers discounts and does not need to bind to a particular instance family. The non-production examples are required only for the business hours of the working day: to pay for their use and to shut down the machinery on demand, so that there is no cost when they are not used — in fact, the cost of free time is zero.
Option A: Specialized hosts are more expensive than normal examples and no discounts are provided for the test environment.
Option B: No cost savings will be achieved by shutting down machines because of the continuous billing of pre-encumbered examples of non-production environments.
Option D: A dedicated host for the production environment is the most costly option, and for an environment that operates only a quarter of a week, the savings plan will not be available for most of the time.

options.text: Use On-Demand Instances for the production instances. Use Dedicated Hosts for the nonproduction instances on weekends only.
Use Reserved Instances for the production instances and the nonproduction instances. Shut down the nonproduction instances when not in use.
Use Compute Savings Plans for the production instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the nonproduction instances. Shut down the nonproduction instances when not in use.
Use Dedicated Hosts for the production instances. Use EC2 Instance Savings Plans for the nonproduction instances.

question_text:
A company stores data in an on-premises Oracle relational database. The company needs to make the data available in Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL for analysis. The company uses an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to connect its on-premises network to AWS.
The company must capture the changes that occur to the source database during the migration to Aurora PostgreSQL.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Switching the database engine from Oracle to the code that PostgreSQL needs to convert mode and store - this is done by the AWS Mode Conversion Tool (AWS SCT). AWS DMS transports data through full loading and data change capture: it first moves existing records and then sustains changes in the source database during migration. Connection already exists - a VPN connection from site to site.
Option A: The migration using only full load tasks is only a migration snapshot and does not capture changes, while the demand clearly requires that changes be captured.
Option B: DataSync transfer files, rather than the content of the relationship database, and does not provide a change capture function at all.
Option D: Snowball is a one-time physical data transfer; it does not transmit changes that occurred during the migration, and the VPN connection is sufficient here.

options.text: Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to convert the Oracle schema to Aurora PostgreSQL schema. Use the AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) full-load migration task to migrate the data.
Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Import the S3 data to Aurora PostgreSQL by using the Aurora PostgreSQL aws_s3 extension.

Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to convert the Oracle schema to Aurora PostgreSQL schema. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the existing data and replicate the ongoing changes.
Use an AWS Snowball device to migrate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Import the S3 data to Aurora PostgreSQL by using the Aurora PostgreSQL aws_s3 extension.

question_text:
A company built an application with Docker containers and needs to run the application in the AWS Cloud. The company wants to use a managed service to host the application.
The solution must scale in and out appropriately according to demand on the individual container services. The solution also must not result in additional operational overhead or infrastructure to manage.
Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
The application has been containerized and the company needs hosting services that can be expanded as needed without the need to maintain any infrastructure. Both organisers running on Fargate are eligible: ECS and Fargate(A) and EKS and Fargate(B) can run tasks and container groups without a single server management and are configured at the service or container group level.
Option C: The Lambda function does not run any container service as an application running for long periods; in Lambda, mirrors are only packing formats for function codes.
Option D: The EC2 working node of the ECS still needs to be updated and expanded with your patches.
Option E: EKS has the same problem as the EC2 node combination: it re-introduces the infrastructure that needs to be maintained.

options.text: Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate.
Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate.
Provision an Amazon API Gateway API. Connect the API to AWS Lambda to run the containers.
Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes.
Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes.

question_text:
An ecommerce company is running a seasonal online sale. The company hosts its website on Amazon EC2 instances spanning multiple Availability Zones. The company wants its website to manage sudden traffic increases during the sale.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The surge is sudden but not permanent: what is needed is the capacity that emerges with the increase in flows and disappears after sales have ended. An automatic extension group with an extended strategy and based on pre-configured AMI-built start-up templates meets this need - new examples can be activated quickly because configured applications are already included in the mirror and no additional machines are running beyond peak hours.
Option A: A stop example will not be used as an automatic extension group for backup capacity: it starts a new example from a template instead of a start on an existing example.
Option B: Setting the minimum group to a peak load means paying the peak capacity around the clock.
Option C: Cache dynamic content in CloudFront and ElastiCache, and then reduce the size of the example is a complex and unreliable design: the flow pattern changes and the reduced example queue does not respond to the cache.

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group that is large enough to handle peak traffic load. Stop half of the Amazon EC2 instances. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the stopped instances to scale out when traffic increases.
Create an Auto Scaling group for the website. Set the minimum size of the Auto Scaling group so that it can handle high traffic volumes without the need to scale out.

Use Amazon CloudFront and Amazon ElastiCache to cache dynamic content with an Auto Scaling group set as the origin. Configure the Auto Scaling group with the instances necessary to populate CloudFront and ElastiCache. Scale in after the cache is fully populated.
Configure an Auto Scaling group to scale out as traffic increases. Create a launch template to start new instances from a preconfigured Amazon Machine Image (AMI).

question_text:
A solutions architect must provide an automated solution for a company's compliance policy that states security groups cannot include a rule that allows SSH from 0.0.0.0/0. The company needs to be notified if there is any breach in the policy. A solution is needed as soon as possible.
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The mission is to quickly and without the need to customize security groups that allow SSH to be open to the Internet as a whole. AWSConfig has a restricted SSH management rule for this scene: it checks the source of the port 22 of the entry rule at 0.0.0.0/0 and marks a security group that does not comply with the norm. The notification function is based on standard service construction: compliance changes are published in EventBridge, then forwarded by EventBridge to a SNS theme. There's no line of code -- so "as soon as possible" and minimum effort.
Option A: Custom scripts mean that development, scheduling, page breaks and continuous maintenance are required. Config can achieve the same result by pre-positioning the rules.
Option C: A role that has the authority to open up a security unit and triggers a notification when the role is assumed cannot detect an existing violation or prevent a direct modification of the security team.
Option D: Stops non-administrators from changing the security team will disrupt the workflow and the security group rules that are already open cannot be found.

options.text: Write an AWS Lambda script that monitors security groups for SSH being open to 0.0.0.0/0 addresses and creates a notification every time it finds one.
Enable the restricted-ssh AWS Config managed rule and generate an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification when a noncompliant rule is created.

Create an IAM role with permissions to globally open security groups and network ACLs. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to generate a notification every time the role is assumed by a user.

Configure a service control policy (SCP) that prevents non-administrative users from creating or editing security groups. Create a notification in the ticketing system when a user requests a rule that needs administrator permissions.

question_text:
Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with Amazon EC2 worker nodes.
A company has deployed an application in an AWS account. The application consists of microservices that run on AWS Lambda and Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). A separate team supports each microservice.
The company has multiple AWS accounts and wants to give each team its own account for its microservices.
A solutions architect needs to design a solution that will provide service-to-service communication over HTTPS (port 443). The solution also must provide a service registry for service discovery.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?
explanation_en:
Microservices are distributed among different accounts, operating on Lambda and EKS, requiring HTTPS communications and a service registration centre - precisely for the design of Amazon VPC Lattice. You create a service network, register every microservice into the network, configure HTTPS listening devices and targets (functions, Pods or examples) and connect VPCs that need to be visited to the network. Service discovery, route and authorization are all built-in functions and do not need to create a reciprocal connection or endpoint manually.
Option A: A check VPC with a firewall can only achieve flow filters. It does not provide service registration or discovery and is more complex in design.
Option C: PrivateLink can work, but each service consumer needs to be equipped with a peer service and an interface endpoint. As the number of teams grows, this will create a large number of audiences and there will be no single registration centre at all.
Option D: Reciprocal connections and prefix lists will grow evenly, with no service detection functionality at all, and each change will require manual editing of the route chart.

options.text: Create an inspection VPC. Deploy an AWS Network Firewall firewall to the inspection VPC. Attach the inspection VPC to a new transit gateway. Route VPC-to-VPC traffic to the inspection VPC. Apply firewall rules to allow only HTTPS communication.

Create a VPC Lattice service network. Associate the microservices with the service network. Define HTTPS listeners for each service. Register microservice compute resources as targets. Identify VPCs that need to communicate with the services. Associate those VPCs with the service network.

Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) with an HTTPS listener and target groups for each microservice. Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service for each microservice. Create an interface VPC endpoint in each VPC that needs to consume that microservice.

Create peering connections between VPCs that contain microservices. Create a prefix list for each service that requires a connection to a client. Create route tables to route traffic to the appropriate VPC. Create security groups to allow only HTTPS communication.

question_text:
A company has a mobile game that reads most of its metadata from an Amazon RDS DB instance. As the game increased in popularity, developers noticed slowdowns related to the game's metadata load times. Performance metrics indicate that simply scaling the database will not help. A solutions architect must explore all options that include capabilities for snapshots, replication, and sub-millisecond response times.
What should the solutions architect recommend to solve these issues?
explanation_en:
The key requirement is a submarisecond response time, with snapshots and copying. This description is consistent with ElastiCache for Redis: a memory cache can respond in milliseconds, supports duplicates transferred through automatic failure and allows the preservation of snapshots of data. Indicators show that simply expanding the database will not solve the problem and that what is needed is a cache layer.
Option A: Aurora can speed up reading by copy, but this is still an extended database, which has been shown to be of no use and no submarisecond response time.
Option B: DynamoDB Global Table addresses the availability of multi-area writing, not submarisecond response times, and requires rewrite applications.
Option D: Memcached is fast, but does not support snapshots or copying - two of the three explicit requirements are not met.

options.text: Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora with Aurora Replicas.
Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB with global tables.
Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis layer in front of the database.
Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached layer in front of the database.

question_text:
A company uses AWS Organizations for its multi-account AWS setup. The security organizational unit (OU) of the company needs to share approved Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) with the development OU. The AMIs are created by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encrypted snapshots.
Which solution will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
Sharing an encrypted AMI is still two operations, but within the organization these can be done at the organizational unit (OU) level. First: Add the ARN of the target OU to the AMI startup permission list - AMIs can be shared with the entire organization or with specific OUs since 2021, not just with a single account. Second: Allows the same OU to use an encrypted snapshot KMS key by updating the key policy (usually using aws:PrircipalOrgPaths condition). Without the second step, the developers can see the mirror but cannot start the example from the mirror. The same mechanism for individual accounts is described in question 80.
Option B: Organizational root ARN will open the mirror to every account in the company, but only with the development of OU, which is broader than actual demand.
Option D: ARN for a single account will exclude access to other accounts in the OU development, and the demand is to be shared with the OU as a whole.
Option E: Recreate key will render encrypted snapshots unreadable, and grant permission to the organization root more broadly than the actual needs.

options.text: Add the development team's OU Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to the launch permission list for the AMIs.
Add the Organizations root Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to the launch permission list for the AMIs.
Update the key policy to allow the development team's OU to use the AWS KMS keys that are used to decrypt the snapshots.
Add the development team’s account Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to the launch permission list for the AMIs.
Recreate the AWS KMS key. Add a key policy to allow the Organizations root Amazon Resource Name (ARN) to use the AWS KMS key.

question_text:
A data analytics company has 80 offices that are distributed globally. Each office hosts 1 PB of data and has between 1 and 2 Gbps of internet bandwidth.
The company needs to perform a one-time migration of a large amount of data from its offices to Amazon S3. The company must complete the migration within 4 weeks.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Mathematical calculations: data from 1 PB per office, transmitted via the network of 2 Gbps, require about one and a half months of continuous transmission in a single office, while the deadline for the entire 80 offices is only four weeks. Network links are not mathematically feasible. Only physical equipment was left: a group of Snowball Edge Storage Optimized equipment ordered in parallel and sent to all office sites for filling and then back to AWS. You only have to pay for the rental and transportation of equipment.
Option A: 80 new 10 Gbps connections mean a significant ongoing cost of several months of configuration and one migration.
Option C: Snowmobile is a truck that can process dozens of PB data; it is not available in every country and it is physically impossible to visit 80 offices around the globe within four weeks.
Option D: A volume storage gateway transmits data via the existing Internet connection to the office and applies to ongoing mixed storage instead of a one-time PB-level data migration.

options.text: Establish a new 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to each office. Transfer the data to Amazon S3.
Use multiple AWS Snowball Edge storage-optimized devices to store and transfer the data to Amazon S3.
Use an AWS Snowmobile to store and transfer the data to Amazon S3.
Set up an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway to transfer the data to Amazon S3.

question_text:
A company has an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that contains a reference dataset. The company has applications on Amazon EC2 instances that need to read the dataset. However, the applications must not be able to change the dataset. The company wants to use IAM access control to prevent the applications from being able to modify or delete the dataset.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The request is specific - access restrictions must be made using IAM, not settings when mounted. EFS provides a resource-based strategy for file systems to deny access to the example role for the elicanfilesystem:ClitWrite operation, while retaining the Clitmount Mount and ClitRootAccess to meet demand. The refusal took effect at the service level and the application could not be written even if it was mounted in a regular reading and writing mode.
Option A: Read-only mount is a client-end setting: any user with case root privileges can remount the volume as a writeable mode. And that's not what the title calls "IAM access control."
Option C: Identity policy is attached to the subject, not "add to the file system". It describes a structure that does not exist.
Option D: EFS access points with POSIX privileges can be restricted at filesystem level, but this is not an IAM mechanism, and the root permissions on the example can circumvent that limit.

options.text: Mount the EFS file system in read-only mode from within the EC2 instances.
Create a resource policy for the EFS file system that denies the elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite action to the IAM roles that are attached to the EC2 instances.
Create an identity policy for the EFS file system that denies the elasticfilesystem:ClientWrite action on the EFS file system.
Create an EFS access point for each application. Use Portable Operating System Interface (POSIX) file permissions to allow read-only access to files in the root directory.

question_text:
A company has hired an external vendor to perform work in the company’s AWS account. The vendor uses an automated tool that is hosted in an AWS account that the vendor owns. The vendor does not have IAM access to the company’s AWS account. The company needs to grant the vendor access to the company’s AWS account.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?
explanation_en:
This almost entirely repeats Question 222: An external supplier works in its own AWS account. The correct design is to create a role in your account that has the required operation strategy and a confidence strategy that allows the subject from the supplier account to assume that role. The supplier calls AssumeRole and obtains a temporary certificate. You can always withdraw access by editing a trust policy. In practice, an external ID is added.
Option B: An IAM user with a password means that a long-term voucher is distributed externally and needs to be manually revoked. There is greater insecurity in all its aspects.
Option C: You cannot add another account to your own IAM group: a group is valid only in a single account.
Option D: Permission borders limit the maximum permission of the subject, but do not allow another account to perform the operation in your account. That is the wrong mechanism.

options.text: Create an IAM role in the company’s account to delegate access to the vendor’s IAM role. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the role for the permissions that the vendor requires.

Create an IAM user in the company’s account with a password that meets the password complexity requirements. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.

Create an IAM group in the company’s account. Add the automated tool’s IAM user from the vendor account to the group. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the group for the permissions that the vendor requires.

Create an IAM user in the company’s account that has a permission boundary that allows the vendor’s account. Attach the appropriate IAM policies to the user for the permissions that the vendor requires.

question_text:
A company wants to run its experimental workloads in the AWS Cloud. The company has a budget for cloud spending. The company's CFO is concerned about cloud spending accountability for each department. The CFO wants to receive notification when the spending threshold reaches 60% of the budget.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
There are two requirements: to identify who is responsible for the expenditure and to be notified when the expenditure reaches 60 per cent of the budget. The first requirement is achieved through cost-allocation labels: the resource is marked as the owner or department, the label is activated in the management account, and the expenditure is then broken down by these labels. The second requirement is to set a 60% alarm threshold in AWS Budgets. It should be noted that Cost Explorer ' s projections cannot be used to identify the owner: the projections show future amounts, not who is responsible for these expenditures.
Option B: Forecast that the owner of the resource cannot be identified and that the cost abnormality test is used to identify anomalies rather than a percentage of a budget.
Option C: C: Credible consultants provide recommendations for optimization rather than threshold notifications related to sector budgets.
Option D: Half is right (i.e. setting a budget with a threshold), but Cost Explorer's projections do not identify the owner of the expenditure - that's what labels are for.

options.text: Use cost allocation tags on AWS resources to label owners. Create usage budgets in AWS Budgets. Add an alert threshold to receive notification when spending exceeds 60% of the budget.
Use AWS Cost Explorer forecasts to determine resource owners. Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to create alert threshold notifications when spending exceeds 60% of the budget.

question_text:
A company wants to deploy an internal web application on AWS. The web application must be accessible only from the company's office. The company needs to download security patches for the web application from the internet.
The company has created a VPC and has configured an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to the company's office.
A solutions architect must design a secure architecture for the web application.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The application can only be accessed from the office of the company, but external access is still required to download updates. The example is located in a privately owned subnet, followed by an internal load balancer, whose entry rules allow only the address segment of the office network to reach through the configured tunnel. The NAT gateway in the public subnet provides the required outreach to obtain patch updates.
Option A: A public load balancer with a source address of 0.0.0.0/0 that exposes an internal application to the entire Internet.
Option C: Examples in public subnets are exposed externally, NAT gateways in private subnets are not operational, and rules are set for out-of-station traffic rather than in-site traffic.
Option D: Another public load equalizer again allows applications to be accessed from the Internet without any restrictions on access from outside.

options.text: Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets behind a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). Attach an internet gateway to the VPC. Set the inbound source of the ALB's security group to 0.0.0.0/0.

Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets behind an internal Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy NAT gateways in public subnets. Attach an internet gateway to the VPC. Set the inbound source of the ALB's security group to the company's office network CIDR block.

Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets behind an internal Application Load Balancer (ALB). Deploy NAT gateways in private subnets. Attach an internet gateway to the VPSet the outbound destination of the ALB’s security group to the company's office network CIDR block.

Deploy the web application on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets behind a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). Attach an internet gateway to the VPC. Set the outbound destination of the ALB’s security group to 0.0.0.0/0.

question_text:
A company maintains its accounting records in a custom application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to migrate the data to an AWS managed service for development and maintenance of the application data. The solution must require minimal operational support and provide immutable, cryptographically verifiable logs of data changes.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
This requirement is an immutable, encrypted record of data changes — this is exactly the literally written description of Amazon QLDB: the journal of the account book is protected by Hashi, history cannot be rewrited and the service itself is fully hosted.
Option A: Redshift is an analytical repository; it does not provide encryption authentication for non-variability or historical records.
Option B: Neptune storage chart structure and build for relationship queries rather than for verifiable change logs.
Option C: Timestream is dedicated to the optimization of time series data, and also does not provide encrypted authentication of historical records.

options.text: Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Redshift cluster.
Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Neptune cluster.
Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Timestream database.
Copy the records from the application into an Amazon Quantum Ledger Database (Amazon QLDB) ledger.

question_text:
A company's marketing data is uploaded from multiple sources to an Amazon S3 bucket. A series of data preparation jobs aggregate the data for reporting. The data preparation jobs need to run at regular intervals in parallel. A few jobs need to run in a specific order later.
The company wants to remove the operational overhead of job error handling, retry logic, and state management.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Mishandling, re-testing and state management need to be detached from the corporate level. While AWS Glue DataBrew can complete the data preparation without having to write a code, the StepFunctions status machine coordinates the operation of the operation - part in parallel, part in a strict sequence - and incorporates retesting, branching and state management functions.
Option A: A set of Lambda functions means that retrying, sorting and status must be done manually.
Option B: Athena executes queries, but does not coordinate or manage the operation chain.
Option D: AWS Data Pipeline is an outmoded service that runs in the morning at a time that contradicts the requirement for regular parallel operations.

options.text: Use an AWS Lambda function to process the data as soon as the data is uploaded to the S3 bucket. Invoke other Lambda functions at regularly scheduled intervals.
Use Amazon Athena to process the data. Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to invoke Athena on a regular internal.
Use AWS Glue DataBrew to process the data. Use an AWS Step Functions state machine to run the DataBrew data preparation jobs.
Use AWS Data Pipeline to process the data. Schedule Data Pipeline to process the data once at midnight.

question_text:
A solutions architect is designing a payment processing application that runs on AWS Lambda in private subnets across multiple Availability Zones. The application uses multiple Lambda functions and processes millions of transactions each day.
The architecture must ensure that the application does not process duplicate payments.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The core requirement is that none of the payments be processed twice. A SQS FIFO queue can provide an accurate one-time processing: repeat messages that appear in the heavy window will be discarded and the message will be sent to another consumer only after they have been confirmed. This is the only option to provide that assurance.
Option A: The S3 event notification is delivered at least once, so there may be repeated calls — and duplicate payments.
Option B: Standard SQS queues also guarantee only at least one delivery and allow repeat messages.
Option D: DynamoDB flows are also likely to call the processor multiple times and cannot prevent duplicate payments.

options.text: Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket with an event notification to invoke another Lambda function to process the due payments.

Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure another Lambda function to poll the SQS queue and to process the due payments.

Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Publish the due payments to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Configure another Lambda function to poll the FIFO queue and to process the due payments.
Use Lambda to retrieve all due payments. Store the due payments in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure streams on the DynamoDB table to invoke another Lambda function to process the due payments.

question_text:
A company runs multiple workloads in its on-premises data center. The company's data center cannot scale fast enough to meet the company's expanding business needs. The company wants to collect usage and configuration data about the on-premises servers and workloads to plan a migration to AWS.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The task is to collect pre-removal data on the use and configuration of local servers. This is precisely the design purpose of AWS Application Discovery Service: an agent-based or non-agent-based collector can capture CPU loads, memory, disks and network connection data, and these results are entered in AWS Migration Hub, where the source area is preset before migration.
Option A: Systems Manager manages connected nodes, which do not apply to asset counts and dependencies maps prior to relocation.
Option C: Schema Transformation Tool is used for database mode conversion, and Trusted Advisor analyses resources within AWS instead of local servers.
Option D: Both tools are used for database migration and do not collect any data on server loads.

options.text: Set the home AWS Region in AWS Migration Hub. Use AWS Systems Manager to collect data about the on- premises servers.
Set the home AWS Region in AWS Migration Hub. Use AWS Application Discovery Service to collect data about the on-premises servers.
Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to create the relevant templates. Use AWS Trusted Advisor to collect data about the on-premises servers.
Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to create the relevant templates. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to collect data about the on-premises servers.

question_text:
A company has an organization in AWS Organizations that has all features enabled. The company requires that all API calls and logins in any existing or new AWS account must be audited. The company needs a managed solution to prevent additional work and to minimize costs. The company also needs to know when any AWS account is not compliant with the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices (FSBP) standard.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
An organization-wide hosting environment is required: audit of each API call and login in existing and new accounts, and compliance monitoring in accordance with FSBP standards. AWS Control Tower is deployed in the management account of the organization, automatically activates the organization-wide CloudTrail tracking and aggregation logs, and the new account created by Account Factory pre-configures this feature. The Security Hub, in conjunction with the Foundation Security Best Practice standards, provides an ongoing compliance assessment for all accounts.
Option B: Control Tower is specifically deployed in the management account of the organization: this environment cannot be set up from the member account.
Option C: AMS Accelerate is a fee-based hosting service that requires a RFC application process at higher cost and slower. GuardDuty is used to detect threats, not to check FSBP compliance.
Option D: Security Hub is the right choice, but the AMS Accelerate and RFC application process cannot be cost- or speed-resistant against a ready-made control Tower.

options.text: Deploy an AWS Control Tower environment in the Organizations management account. Enable AWS Security Hub and AWS Control Tower Account Factory in the environment.
Deploy an AWS Control Tower environment in a dedicated Organizations member account. Enable AWS Security Hub and AWS Control Tower Account Factory in the environment.
Use AWS Managed Services (AMS) Accelerate to build a multi-account landing zone (MALZ). Submit an RFC to self-service provision Amazon GuardDuty in the MALZ.
Use AWS Managed Services (AMS) Accelerate to build a multi-account landing zone (MALZ). Submit an RFC to self-service provision AWS Security Hub in the MALZ.

question_text:
A company has stored 10 TB of log files in Apache Parquet format in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company occasionally needs to use SQL to analyze the log files.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Data has been stored in S3 in column Parquet format, and queries are running only occasionally. The cheapest option would be to completely avoid creating any clusters: the reptiles of AWS Glue found data structures and created tables in the data catalogue, and Amazon Athena could run a query directly to the object and charge the bytes of the scan. Parquet also significantly reduces the amount of data to be scanned.
Option A: The migration of decabytes to Aurora means that there is a need to pay for the storage and running of examples, only for occasional queries.
Option B: Redshift Spectrum can be read from S3, but it requires an active Redshift cluster, which will be billed on an ongoing basis.
Option D: EMR clusters will also charge time for running nodes: this is more expensive for occasional queries than for scanned data.

options.text: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Migrate the data from the S3 bucket into Aurora by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Issue SQL statements to the Aurora database.
Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Use Redshift Spectrum to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.
Create an AWS Glue crawler to store and retrieve table metadata from the S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.
Create an Amazon EMR cluster. Use Apache Spark SQL to run SQL statements directly on the data in the S3 bucket.

question_text:
A company needs a solution to prevent AWS CloudFormation stacks from deploying AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) resources that include an inline policy or “*” in the statement. The solution must also prohibit deployment of Amazon EC2 instances with public IP addresses. The company has AWS Control Tower enabled in its organization in AWS Organizations.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Original answer: D; source correction answer: A.
SCP operates the API call and condition, and cannot see the content of the CloudFormation template - they cannot stop the interconnective policy with wildcards in the template statement. This is AWS Control Tower's active control -- based on the ClaudFormation Hooks inspection, preventing deployment before resources are created.
Control Tower policy controls inspect resources before deployment; existing controls can intercept broad wildcard privileges in EC2 public IP and IAM inline policy. If the title requires a ban on any inline policy (even if there is no wildcard), ready-made controls cannot be fully satisfied; A is retained under the usual consideration for high-priority inline policy.
The key to the source practice information (option D) was amended in the audit. The requirement is to prevent deployment, and the conditions are based on template content: an inline strategy, wildcards in statements, public web IP on examples. One SCP operates the API call and request conditions, and cannot see the content of the CloudFormation template, so it is not possible to check if "the template contains an inline policy with wildcards". This is the active control of AWS Control Tower: through the ClaudFormation Hooks, templates are validated before resources are created to stop non-conforming stacks. It is important to distinguish between three types of control: preventive control (SCP, restricted operation), test control (AWS Config, after detection of problems) and active control (validation of templates before deployment).
Option B: Test controls detect and report non-compliance with existing resources. They cannot prevent deployment.
Option C: AWS Config also reacts ex post and automatically removes the created resources as a high-risk, rough way to achieve compliance.
Option D: This is the original source practice key. SCP can reject ec2: RunInstances call, with an example-based public Internet IP, but cannot decipher the content of IAM resources in the template to find inline strategies with wildcards. Half of the requirements remain unmet.

options.text: Use AWS Control Tower proactive controls to block deployment of EC2 instances with public IP addresses and inline policies with elevated access or “*”.
Use AWS Control Tower detective controls to block deployment of EC2 instances with public IP addresses and inline policies with elevated access or “*”.
Use AWS Config to create rules for EC2 and IAM compliance. Configure the rules to run an AWS Systems Manager Session Manager automation to delete a resource when it is not compliant.
Use a service control policy (SCP) to block actions for the EC2 instances and IAM resources if the actions lead to noncompliance.

question_text:
A company's web application that is hosted in the AWS Cloud recently increased in popularity. The web application currently exists on a single Amazon EC2 instance in a single public subnet. The web application has not been able to meet the demand of the increased web traffic.
The company needs a solution that will provide high availability and scalability to meet the increased user demand without rewriting the web application.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
The application cannot be rewritten and must therefore build scalability and usability on its current basis. Examples are moved to an automatic extension group in a private subnet in several available areas (B), while the application load balancer in the public subnet receives and distributes traffic to the public network (E). The application itself will not change.
Option A: The larger example is still a single machine: there is no increase in availability and no horizontal expansion.
Option C: NAT gateway is used to transfer traffic out; it cannot be used to respond to the income station request.
Option D: The same problem as option A: Single point failure still exists.

options.text: Replace the EC2 instance with a larger compute optimized instance.
Configure Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling with multiple Availability Zones in private subnets.
Configure a NAT gateway in a public subnet to handle web requests.
Replace the EC2 instance with a larger memory optimized instance.
Configure an Application Load Balancer in a public subnet to distribute web traffic.

question_text:
A company has AWS Lambda functions that use environment variables. The company does not want its developers to see environment variables in plaintext.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
By default, the Lambda environment variable is encrypted in a static state using the AWS-managed key, but its value is visible in the console and API in an explicit form to any person who has the right to read a function configuration. In order to prevent developers from seeing these values, encryption assistants are enabled: variables are encrypted in the console using the client-managed KMS key, stored only in secret, and function decrypts them through a code call. The key authority has been granted to the executing role, as described in questions 550, 640.
Option A: Switch to EC2 has nothing to do with the task: the key in the case configuration is equally visible to anyone who has access to it.
Option B: There is no expression "to provide SSL encryption for the Lambda function through ClaudHSM": ClaudHSM is not integrated with environmental variables, and SSL protects communication channels rather than stored values.
Option C: ACM certificates are used for TLS on load balancers, Cloud Front and the API Gateway. They cannot be used for encrypted environment variables.

options.text: Deploy code to Amazon EC2 instances instead of using Lambda functions.
Configure SSL encryption on the Lambda functions to use AWS CloudHSM to store and encrypt the environment variables.
Create a certificate in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM). Configure the Lambda functions to use the certificate to encrypt the environment variables.
Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Enable encryption helpers on the Lambda functions to use the KMS key to store and encrypt the environment variables.

question_text:
An analytics company uses Amazon VPC to run its multi-tier services. The company wants to use RESTful APIs to offer a web analytics service to millions of users. Users must be verified by using an authentication service to access the APIs.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
explanation_en:
The authentication of millions of end-users before accessing RET API is done using the Cognito user pool plus API Gateway and matching the Cognito authorization group. The user pool is responsible for registration, login, password recovery and multifactor authentication, and a JWT; API Gateway validates the token through an built-in authorized agent without having to write any code. Please make a clear distinction between the two Cognito concepts: the user pool is a user directory and authentication mechanism, while the identification pool is used to exchange tokens for temporary AWS certificates, subject to authentication by the user.
Option B: The identification pool does not authenticate the user: it issues AWS vouchers to an accredited user. Validation of login requires a user pool.
Option C: Custom Lambda authorization requires the preparation and maintenance of codes, while the built-in Cognito authorization is ready to be used immediately.
Option D: IAM users cannot be used as a login mechanism for millions of clients: IAM is designed for the subject in the account, not for the end user of the application.

options.text: Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool for user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway REST APIs with a Cognito authorizer.
Configure an Amazon Cognito identity pool for user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs with a Cognito authorizer.
Configure an AWS Lambda function to handle user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway REST APIs with a Lambda authorizer.
Configure an IAM user to handle user authentication. Implement Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs with an IAM authorizer.

question_text:
A company has a mobile app for customers. The app’s data is sensitive and must be encrypted at rest. The company uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).
The company needs a solution that prevents the accidental deletion of KMS keys. The solution must use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send an email notification to administrators when a user attempts to delete a KMS key.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The removal of KMS keys will not occur immediately: scheduled deletions will wait between 7 and 30 days, and can be deleted by calling CancelKeyDeletion throughout the window. This solution is based on the fact that an EventBridge rule captures the ScheduleKeyDescription event from CloudTrail, triggers a runbook of Systems Manager Automation, and also sends messages to a SNS subject to inform the administrator. Each component is managed without a custom code.
Option A: An AWS Config rule assesses resource compliance and cannot be the target of the EventBridge rule to cancel an operation. The mechanism of this option cannot be achieved.
Option B: A custom Lambda function with an additional Cloudwatch alarm that contains the elimination logic is an additional code and more components, and an off-the-shelf running book is sufficient.
Option D: CloudTrail with indicator filters and alarm settings only inform administrators. It cannot by itself cancel deletion, but requires that the key be prevented from being lost.

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts when a user tries to delete a KMS key. Configure an AWS Config rule that cancels any deletion of a KMS key. Add the AWS Config rule as a target of the EventBridge rule. Create an SNS topic that notifies the administrators.

Create an AWS Lambda function that has custom logic to prevent KMS key deletion. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is activated when a user tries to delete a KMS key. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the Lambda function when the DeleteKey operation is performed. Create an SNS topic. Configure the EventBridge rule to publish an SNS message that notifies the administrators.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts when the KMS DeleteKey operation is performed. Configure the rule to initiate an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Configure the runbook to cancel the deletion of the KMS key. Create an SNS topic. Configure the EventBridge rule to publish an SNS message that notifies the administrators.

Create an AWS CloudTrail trail. Configure the trail to deliver logs to a new Amazon CloudWatch log group. Create a CloudWatch alarm based on the metric filter for the CloudWatch log group. Configure the alarm to use Amazon SNS to notify the administrators when the KMS DeleteKey operation is performed.

question_text:
A company wants to analyze and generate reports to track the usage of its mobile app. The app is popular and has a global user base. The company uses a custom report building program to analyze application usage.
The program generates multiple reports during the last week of each month. The program takes less than 10 minutes to produce each report. The company rarely uses the program to generate reports outside of the last week of each month The company wants to generate reports in the least amount of time when the reports are requested.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The report is produced for less than 10 minutes and is almost always requested within a single week of a month. A Lambda function is activated immediately upon trigger of the EventBridge rule, fully compliant with the 15-minute limit, and is only charged on the basis of actual running time - no cost outside the reporting cycle.
Option A: Throughout the last week of the last month, examples continue to run, even if they are in a busy state for only a few minutes, they are billed.
Option C: ECS missions are cheaper than examples, but start at a slower rate than a function and at a more crude particle-level interval, which results in significant overpayment for a 10-minute operation.
Option D: Spot examples are cheaper, but they will still run for a week, and volume recovery may interrupt reporting during the production of the report.

options.text: Run the program by using Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to start the EC2 instances when reports are requested. Run the EC2 instances continuously during the last week of each month.
Run the program in AWS Lambda. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to run a Lambda function when reports are requested.
Run the program in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Schedule Amazon ECS to run the program when reports are requested.

Run the program by using Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Create an Amazon EventBndge rule to start the EC2 instances when reports are requested. Run the EC2 instances continuously during the last week of each month.

question_text:
A company is designing a tightly coupled high performance computing (HPC) environment in the AWS Cloud. The company needs to include features that will optimize the HPC environment for networking and storage.
Which combination of solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
A well-connected high-performance load can be attributed to two things: network and file storage between nodes. Elastic Fabric Adapter provides examples of low delays (D) in operating systems for nuclear bypass and MPI libraries. For storage, FSx for Lustre provides the maximum throughput and the lowest price under effacement mode, and lack of copying is not a problem (B).
Option A: The Global Accelerator optimizes the path of user traffic to the application without affecting the communication between computing nodes.
Option C: CloudFront distributes content to end-users via HTTP, unrelated to high performance calculations.
Option E: Elastic Beanstalk deploys Web applications; it does not have network or storage optimization for computing tasks.

options.text: Create an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure custom routing for the accelerator.
Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Configure the file system with scratch storage.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the viewer protocol policy to be HTTP and HTTPS.
Launch Amazon EC2 instances. Attach an Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) to the instances.
Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk deployment to manage the environment.

question_text:
A company needs a solution to prevent photos with unwanted content from being uploaded to the company's web application. The solution must not involve training a machine learning (ML) model.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Training models are not feasible and require ready-made services. Amazon Rekognation has built in the detection of undesirable content in the image (content audit) without training. The application activates the function by calling the Lambda function when uploading a photograph.
Option A: SageMaker Autopilot training model - this is a direct violation.
Option C: Comprehend analyzes text rather than images, and CloudFrontFunctions restricts the use of external services too strictly.
Option D: Rekognition Video is designed for video streaming and recording content, but here it is uploading photos: a normal image analysis function is required.

options.text: Create and deploy a model by using Amazon SageMaker Autopilot. Create a real-time endpoint that the web application invokes when new photos are uploaded.
Create an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon Rekognition to detect unwanted content. Create a Lambda function URL that the web application invokes when new photos are uploaded.
Create an Amazon CloudFront function that uses Amazon Comprehend to detect unwanted content. Associate the function with the web application.
Create an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon Rekognition Video to detect unwanted content. Create a Lambda function URL that the web application invokes when new photos are uploaded.

question_text:
A company uses AWS to run its ecommerce platform. The platform is critical to the company's operations and has a high volume of traffic and transactions. The company configures a multi-factor authentication (MFA) device to secure its AWS account root user credentials. The company wants to ensure that it will not lose access to the root user account if the MFA device is lost.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
AWS allows you to register more than one MFA device (up to eight) for a single root user, which is standard practice for preventing access rights from being lost. The second equipment should be stored in a separate location - e.g., a hardware key stored in a safe. Attention is also drawn to cases of total loss: if root access is lost, restoration of access requires confirmation through the account ' s e-mail address and telephone number, so these contacts must be kept up to date and the root account ' s e-mail address should be a distribution list rather than a personal mailbox.
Option A: No other account can replace the root account: some operations (closing the account, changing the support plan, restoring the account) are open only to the root account.
Option C: Once access is lost, no new administrator can be created - and no root access can be restored.
Option D: Attaching the administrator policy to another user will not grant root privileges and will not solve the problem of missing MFA devices.

options.text: Set up a backup administrator account that the company can use to log in if the company loses the MFA device.
Add multiple MFA devices for the root user account to handle the disaster scenario.
Create a new administrator account when the company cannot access the root account.
Attach the administrator policy to another IAM user when the company cannot access the root account.

question_text:
A social media company is creating a rewards program website for its users. The company gives users points when users create and upload videos to the website. Users redeem their points for gifts or discounts from the company's affiliated partners. A unique ID identifies users. The partners refer to this ID to verify user eligibility for rewards.
The partners want to receive notification of user IDs through an HTTP endpoint when the company gives users points. Hundreds of vendors are interested in becoming affiliated partners every day. The company wants to design an architecture that gives the website the ability to add partners rapidly in a scalable way.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?
explanation_en:
There are hundreds of partners each day, each of whom needs to send notifications to its own HTTP endpoint. SNS theme supports HTTP and HTTPS subscription protocols: Adding a partner requires only one subscription and the extension of the broadcast is done by the service itself. The number of subscribers does not need to be a concern for the release application.
Option A: Timestream is a time-series database that must be manually prepared and expanded for broadcast delivery.
