Amazon EFS mounts all examples through NFS, data are stored across multiple available areas and there is no limit to the size of a single file - 25 GB or larger large files that can be processed in origin.
Option A: S3 is stored through objects that are accessed through API: People and applications need to change the way they process files.
Option B: The snapshot is restored to a separate volume that connects to a single instance in a single available area. There are no shared visits and copies are immediately divided.
Option D: Examples are easily stored and are limited to each machine locally: data cannot be shared and will be lost when the case stops.

options.text: Migrate all the files to an Amazon S3 bucket. Instruct the employees to access the files from the S3 bucket.
Take a snapshot of the existing EBS volume. Mount the snapshot as an EBS volume across the EC2 instances. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.
Mount an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system across all the EC2 instances. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the EC2 instances. Configure new EC2 instances from the AMI that use an instance store volume. Instruct the employees to access the files from the EC2 instances.

question_text:
A company is running a highly sensitive application on Amazon EC2 backed by an Amazon RDS database.
Compliance regulations mandate that all personally identifiable information (PII) be encrypted at rest.
Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement with the LEAST amount of changes to the infrastructure?
explanation_en:
Original answer: C; source correction answer: D.
The backup key C describes SSL, the encryption in the transmission, although it requires static storage encryption; option D covers two storage layers: EBS and RDS storage of examples, both encrypted using KMS keys
Static encryption to overwrite EC2 EBS instance volume and RDS database storage, respectively, enable EBS encryption and RDS encryption with KMS managed keys; former C confused SSL transfer encryption with static volume encryption with D. Unencrypted resources still need to be migrated or recovered from encrypted snapshots.
The key points of the source ' s practice information (option C) were corrected during the audit: it recommended that "the database volume be encrypted with KMS keys ", but that SSL only protect data during transmission, and that the requirement explicitly relate to static data encryption. The data exist in two locations: EBS and RDS storage for EC2 instances. Therefore, both EBS and RDS have enabled the encryption of KMS keys. Changes in infrastructure are very limited: for EBS, only the creation of an encryption volume (or the opening of the default encryption at the account level) is required; for RDS, it means restoring the example from a encrypted snapshot copy, as described in question 121.
Option A: AWS issues TLS certificates for secure connections, but cannot be used to encrypt database volumes.
Option B: CloudHSM provides you with complete control over encryption, but requires deployment and maintenance of an HSM cluster. When KMS can achieve the same effect by configuration, this is not proportionate to the requirement of “minimum change”.
Option C: This is the original storage key: the SSL protects the data in the transfer, while the problem is static data. The expression "SSL encryption of volumes using KMS keys" confuses two different mechanisms.

options.text: Deploy AWS Certificate Manager to generate certificates. Use the certificates to encrypt the database volume.
Deploy AWS CloudHSM, generate encryption keys, and use the keys to encrypt database volumes.
Configure SSL encryption using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt database volumes.
Configure Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) encryption and Amazon RDS encryption with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys to encrypt instance and database volumes.

question_text:
A company runs an AWS Lambda function in private subnets in a VPC. The subnets have a default route to the internet through an Amazon EC2 NAT instance. The Lambda function processes input data and saves its output as an object to Amazon S3.
Intermittently, the Lambda function times out while trying to upload the object because of saturated traffic on the NAT instance's network. The company wants to access Amazon S3 without traversing the internet.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The problem is that all traffic is passing through NAT and is limited by its bandwidth. The correct solution is to add a path to the S3 gateway endpoint to the list of private subnets: traffic is no longer going through NAT and will never enter the Internet, bandwidth restrictions disappear, and the end point itself is not expensive.
Option A: A managed NAT gateway is easier to expand than an example, but traffic still needs to pass through the Internet and is charged by the processing gigabyte. The requirement to avoid Internet access cannot be met.
Option B: A larger example of NAT simply pushes the saturation point back, but does not change the flow path through the Internet.
Option D: The transfer gateway is used to connect to the network; S3 cannot connect to it and has no impact on the route to the S3 bucket.

options.text: Replace the EC2 NAT instance with an AWS managed NAT gateway.
Increase the size of the EC2 NAT instance in the VPC to a network optimized instance type.
Provision a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPUpdate the route tables of the subnets accordingly.
Provision a transit gateway. Place transit gateway attachments in the private subnets where the Lambda function is running.

question_text:
A news company that has reporters all over the world is hosting its broadcast system on AWS. The reporters send live broadcasts to the broadcast system. The reporters use software on their phones to send live streams through the Real Time Messaging Protocol (RTMP).
A solutions architect must design a solution that gives the reporters the ability to send the highest quality streams.
The solution must provide accelerated TCP connections back to the broadcast system.
What should the solutions architect use to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
What needs to be speeded up is the TCP connection between reporters from all over the world to the broadcasting system. The global accelerator receives connections at the nearest edge and relays them through the AWS backbone network: shorter paths, fewer throws and shakes, and any fixedcast address. This is the function needed for the RTMP stream running through TCP.
Option A: CloudFront optimizes the distribution and cache of content to the audience, rather than the flow that is received from the source.
Option C: Clear VPN provides secure network access, but does not speed up the network path and does not provide any fixedcast address.
Option D: Examples of flexible IP addresses configured to receive traffic via the ordinary Internet: no path to accelerate.

options.text: Amazon CloudFront
AWS Global Accelerator
AWS Client VPN
Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Elastic IP addresses

question_text:
A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) to run its self-managed database. The company has 350 TB of data spread across all EBS volumes. The company takes daily EBS snapshots and keeps the snapshots for 1 month. The daily change rate is 5% of the EBS volumes.
Because of new regulations, the company needs to keep the monthly snapshots for 7 years. The company needs to change its backup strategy to comply with the new regulations and to ensure that data is available with minimal administrative effort.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Daily snapshots are already working — they are incremental snapshots, and they are kept for a month. In order to achieve the seven-year monthly snapshot reservation, there is a standard level called EBS Snapshots Archive: the fast notes are moved to the filing level at a cost of about three quarters lower than the standard storage. The process is managed through a life-cycle strategy, which means that no manual operations are required.
Option A: EBS snapshots cannot be copied directly to Glacier Deep Archive: unlike the two services, there is no such operation.
Option C: Maintain a monthly snapshot of seven years in the standard level, which will be several times more expensive than the filing level.
Option D: EBS direct API allows the reading of snapshots, but export 350 TB per month using its own tools will result in significant costs and maximum manual operation.

options.text: Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier for 1 month. Copy the monthly snapshot to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive with a 7-year retention period.
Continue with the current EBS snapshot policy. Add a new policy to move the monthly snapshot to Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive with a 7-year retention period.
Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier for 1 month. Keep the monthly snapshot in the standard tier for 7 years. Use incremental snapshots.

Keep the daily snapshot in the EBS snapshot standard tier. Use EBS direct APIs to take snapshots of all the EBS volumes every month. Store the snapshots in an Amazon S3 bucket in the Infrequent Access tier for 7 years.

question_text:
A company runs an application on several Amazon EC2 instances that store persistent data on an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. The company needs to replicate the data to another AWS Region by using an AWS managed service solution.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Original answer: A; source correction answer: D.
"EFS-to-EFS backup" is a legacy AWS Solutions product based on ClubFormation, not a hosting service; cross-section EFS copy processed by AWS Backup
AWS Backup can create a daily schedule for the EFS and copy the backup to another area, which is a hosting scheme; source A does not refer to EFS-to-EFS backup solution as the standard hosting cross-regional backup path to be selected for this subject, to D.
The hosting service is required to enable cross-regional copying of EFS data, AWS Backup (D) is responsible for backup movement, retention and cross-regional copying, and the file system is assigned to the backup plan only.
Option A: "EFS-to-EFS backup" is a legacy AWS SolutionsCloudFormation deployment -- a set of resources you need to deploy and maintain. It's not a hosting service.
Option B: Write S3 daily scripts with CRRs means that a custom code, a schedule and your side monitor are required, while data models change: the file becomes an object.
Option C: Use rsync through VPC peer-to-peer is a fully self-built solution: you need your own example, your own retest mechanism, your own integrity verification.

options.text: Use the EFS-to-EFS backup solution to replicate the data to an EFS file system in another Region.
Run a nightly script to copy data from the EFS file system to an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable S3 Cross-Region Replication on the S3 bucket.
Create a VPC in another Region. Establish a cross-Region VPC peer. Run a nightly rsync to copy data from the original Region to the new Region.
Use AWS Backup to create a backup plan with a rule that takes a daily backup and replicates it to another Region. Assign the EFS file system resource to the backup plan.

question_text:
An ecommerce company is migrating its on-premises workload to the AWS Cloud. The workload currently consists of a web application and a backend Microsoft SQL database for storage.
The company expects a high volume of customers during a promotional event. The new infrastructure in the AWS Cloud must be highly available and scalable.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?
explanation_en:
Availability, scalability and minimization management are all necessary. The Web layer is deployed in an automatic expansion group across two available areas and is deployed through the application of a load balancer, which absorbs the surge in traffic generated by promotional activities, while the SQL Server database migrates to the example of a multi-usable area RDS management with automatic failure switching.
Option A: Two fixed examples cannot cope with a surge in traffic, and reading a copy does not replace the multi-usable area configuration for error tolerance.
Option B: Databases on EC2 instances across different regions mean management costs that are managed for replication and maximization.
Option D: The three static examples and the database distributed on the three EC2 machines do not have automatic extension and do not use the managed database.

options.text: Migrate the web application to two Amazon EC2 instances across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server with read replicas in both Availability Zones.

Migrate the web application to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to two EC2 instances across separate AWS Regions with database replication.

Migrate the web application to Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon RDS with Multi-AZ deployment.

Migrate the web application to three Amazon EC2 instances across three Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to three EC2 instances across three Availability Zones.

question_text:
A company has an on-premises business application that generates hundreds of files each day. These files are stored on an SMB file share and require a low-latency connection to the application servers. A new company policy states all application-generated files must be copied to AWS. There is already a VPN connection to AWS.
The application development team does not have time to make the necessary code modifications to move the application to AWS.
Which service should a solutions architect recommend to allow the application to copy files to AWS?
explanation_en:
The application cannot be rewrited, it will write to a SMB share and will require a low delay and already exist with AWS. The AWS Service Gateway file gateway model has been deployed locally to present the application with its expected familiar SMB sharing, while each file is stored as an object in S3: the company ' s policy is met, the code is not changed and the delay is controlled by local caches.
Option A: EFS uses the NFS protocol and is at the cloud end: protocol error is clearly detectable by delay via VPN.
Option B: FSx for Windows File Server supports SMB, but it is at the cloud end: each operation passes through a tunnel and does not meet the low delay requirement.
Option C: Snowball is a one-time batch transfer device, and the file is generated daily and requires continuous reproduction.

options.text: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
AWS Snowball
AWS Storage Gateway

question_text:
A company has 15 employees. The company stores employee start dates in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company wants to send an email message to each employee on the day of the employee's work anniversary.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
explanation_en:
The task is very simple, running only once a day. The Lambda function of a planned task scans a table with 15 lines and sends mail through SNS, which contains an email delivery protocol. There is no need for a server or for a self-constructor.
Option A: Cron script running on an EC2 instance means that a machine runs all day, working only a few seconds a day.
Option B: The same unnecessary machine, and worse, SQS does not send mail: it's just a message queue.
Option D: Schedule is correct, but you cannot send mail through SQS queues - this requires SNS or SES.

options.text: Create a script that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Use a cron job to run this script every day on an Amazon EC2 instance.

Create a script that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Use a cron job to run this script every day on an Amazon EC2 instance.

Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Schedule this Lambda function to run every day.

Create an AWS Lambda function that scans the DynamoDB table and uses Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to send email messages to employees when necessary. Schedule this Lambda function to run every day.

question_text:
A company’s application is running on Amazon EC2 instances within an Auto Scaling group behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. Based on the application's history, the company anticipates a spike in traffic during a holiday each year. A solutions architect must design a strategy to ensure that the Auto Scaling group proactively increases capacity to minimize any performance impact on application users.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The time when peaks occur is known in advance — the holidays occur again every year. A cyclical plan operation increases the capacity of the auto-extension group before the expected peak, so the example is ready before the user arrives. This is precisely the proactive expansion required by the scene.
Option A: CPU utilization alerts are triggered only when users already feel reduced performance — a reaction, not a preparation.
Option C: Manually adjust the limits during peak periods every year.
Option D: Notification of the initiation of the example will only be notified to the administrator and will not increase the capacity.

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to scale up the EC2 instances when CPU utilization exceeds 90%.
Create a recurring scheduled action to scale up the Auto Scaling group before the expected period of peak demand.
Increase the minimum and maximum number of EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group during the peak demand period.
Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification to send alerts when there are autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCH events.

question_text:
A company uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases for its data tier. The company must implement password rotation for the databases.
Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
Rotation database passwords are exactly what Secrets Manager does and do not need to write codes: the key is stored encrypted using KMS keys, whereas for RDS PostgreSQL, AWS provides an i.e. type rotation function, with only opening and setting rotation cycles. The password is read by the application through its role caller GetSecretValue, so the password change is not visible to the application. Keep service boundaries clear: Secrets Manager is a key that needs to be rotated, Parameter Store is a simple key used for parameters and does not need to be rotated, and KMS is used for encryption keys, not passwords.
Option B: Parameter Store does not have an built-in automatic rotation function: it cannot be achieved by "enable it on parameters".
Option C: Customized rotation functions mean codes, privileges, tests and maintenance are required. The same effect can be achieved by configuration.
Option D: KMS rotates the encryption key instead of the database user password. It cannot resolve this task.

options.text: Store the password in AWS Secrets Manager. Enable automatic rotation on the secret.
Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Enable automatic rotation on the parameter.
Store the password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Write an AWS Lambda function that rotates the password.
Store the password in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Enable automatic rotation on the AWS KMS key.

question_text:
A company runs its application on Oracle Database Enterprise Edition. The company needs to migrate the application and the database to AWS. The company can use the Bring Your Own License (BYOL) model while migrating to AWS. The application uses third-party database features that require privileged access.
A solutions architect must design a solution for the database migration.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The application uses Oracle features that require privileged access - while standard RDS for Oracle does not provide SYS level privileges or operating system access. Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle is specifically designed for this situation: it is a hosting service that still provides access to the bottom operating system and database set-up and supports the Bring Your Own Licence model.
Option A: Standard RDS for Oracle does not provide privileged access, and replacing third-party supplier functions with the Lambda function means that the application needs to be rewritten.
Option C: DynamoDB is a non-relative storage service: Migration from Oracle means that data models and queries must be fully rewrited.
Option D: Move to PostgreSQL and rewrite the code, which is contrary to both the requirement to use an existing licence and the minimum cost requirement.

options.text: Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for Oracle by using native tools. Replace the third-party features with AWS Lambda.
Migrate the database to Amazon RDS Custom for Oracle by using native tools. Customize the new database settings to support the third-party features.
Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Customize the new database settings to support the third-party features.
Migrate the database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Rewrite the application code to remove the dependency on third-party features.

question_text:
A large international university has deployed all of its compute services in the AWS Cloud. These services include Amazon EC2, Amazon RDS, and Amazon DynamoDB. The university currently relies on many custom scripts to back up its infrastructure. However, the university wants to centralize management and automate data backups as much as possible by using AWS native options.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Backup needs to be centralized and automated through the AWS primary tool. AWS Backup is designed for this purpose: it supports EC2, RDS, DynamoDB and many other services, defines backup plans with plans, schedules and retention cycles, manages backup repositories, centralizes the status of each operation and replaces custom scripts.
Option A: Third-party software and virtual tape banks are not AWS raw tools or centralized schemes - they simply continue old methods.
Option C: AWS Config is used to track configuration compliance and does not support a regular snapshot.
Option D: State Manager maintains the desired configuration on the node, but it is not a backup service.

options.text: Use third-party backup software with an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway virtual tape library.
Use AWS Backup to configure and monitor all backups for the services in use.
Use AWS Config to set lifecycle management to take snapshots of all data sources on a schedule.
Use AWS Systems Manager State Manager to manage the configuration and monitoring of backup tasks.

question_text:
A company wants to build a map of its IT infrastructure to identify and enforce policies on resources that pose security risks. The company's security team must be able to query data in the IT infrastructure map and quickly identify security risks.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
An infrastructure map is the resource and its interrelationship — a map. Amazon Neptune stores this data as tops and edges and allows you to search for it in the chart search language (including SPARQL), so questions like "What resources are connected to this vulnerable node" can be answered through a single query without having to build the infrastructure yourself.
Option A: In the relation database, relationships are carried out through duplicate table connections: queries become complex and slow.
Option C: Redshift is designed for analysis on large-scale data sets, not for relationships across objects.
Option D: DynamoDB key storage items; PartiQL will not convert them to a graphic database and will not be able to pass through relationships.

options.text: Use Amazon RDS to store the data. Use SQL to query the data to identify security risks.
Use Amazon Neptune to store the data. Use SPARQL to query the data to identify security risks.
Use Amazon Redshift to store the data. Use SQL to query the data to identify security risks.
Use Amazon DynamoDB to store the data. Use PartiQL to query the data to identify security risks.

question_text:
A large company wants to provide its globally located developers separate, limited size, managed PostgreSQL databases for development purposes. The databases will be low volume. The developers need the databases only when they are actively working.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Reference answer: B; dispute option: C.
Aurora Servers will shrink during their free time, more accurately meeting the requirement of "only for running"
ServiceCatalog for B limits the specification of the example, but does not have a mechanism to stop the database while the developers are idle; C is written as the same Aurora Servers system that activates several independent databases with only default capacity and does not guarantee that the developers ' independence will be suspended on demand. Existing options lack a complete configuration of independent databases, size limits and costing only when used; source B is retained for identification purposes only.
The key phrases are "only when they actually run" and "limited in size". The cheapest solution is one that does not cost for free time while at the same time preventing developers from creating large clusters at will. The key option is B: a Service Catalog product with a size limit - size is always controlled and started by the developers themselves. The weakness of the key point is that the deployed Aurora example will continue to be billed at night and the developers will be spread over different time zones. Option C adds Aurora Servers to the same Service Catalog method, which, because of its automatic indentation during free time, more precisely meets the requirement of "run only when required".
Option A: A manual start/stop schedule does not work for developers in different time zones and the overall responsibility lies with the transportation team. In addition, there are no size limits here -- anyone can start a big example.
Option C: A strong alternative: Servers automatically inflate when they are free, so that the billing is consistent with actual usage. The reason for the objection is that the default capacity set-up does not meet the requirement to limit the size of the database.
Option D: Trusted Advisor discovers an idle database after the problem has occurred and automatically deletes data that would destroy the developers, rather than simply suspending the data. This is a response to the problem, not a solution.

options.text: Give the developers the ability to launch separate Amazon Aurora instances. Set up a process to shut down Aurora instances at the end of the workday and to start Aurora instances at the beginning of the next workday.
Develop an AWS Service Catalog product that enforces size restrictions for launching Amazon Aurora instances. Give the developers access to launch the product when they need a development database.
Create an Amazon Aurora Serverless cluster. Develop an AWS Service Catalog product to launch databases in the cluster with the default capacity settings. Grant the developers access to the product.
Monitor AWS Trusted Advisor checks for idle Amazon RDS databases. Create a process to terminate identified idle RDS databases.

question_text:
A company is building a web application that serves a content management system. The content management system runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. Users are constantly adding and updating files, blogs, and other website assets in the content management system.
A solutions architect must implement a solution in which all the EC2 instances share up-to-date website content with the least possible lag time.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
All examples require the same website content, with as little delay as possible, and users constantly change their content. A shared Amazon EFS file system is mounted on each example, and writing operations on a machine are immediately visible to other machines: no synchronization, no delay.
Option A: Copying from the "recently activated" instance at startup means delay and complete confusion at the time of the simultaneous change, and the load balancer is unable to change the route to a specific machine.
Option C: Synchronization per hour means a delay of up to one hour, while the requirement is as small as possible.
Option D: EBS snapshots provide each machine with a copy that is frozen at the time of the snapshot: changes in one instance will never be seen in another.

options.text: Update the EC2 user data in the Auto Scaling group lifecycle policy to copy the website assets from the EC2 instance that was launched most recently. Configure the ALB to make changes to the website assets only in the newest EC2 instance.

Copy the website assets to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Configure each EC2 instance to mount the EFS file system locally. Configure the website hosting application to reference the website assets that are stored in the EFS file system.

Copy the website assets to an Amazon S3 bucket. Ensure that each EC2 instance downloads the website assets from the S3 bucket to the attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Run the S3 sync command once each hour to keep files up to date.

Restore an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) snapshot with the website assets. Attach the EBS snapshot as a secondary EBS volume when a new EC2 instance is launched. Configure the website hosting application to reference the website assets that are stored in the secondary EBS volume.

question_text:
A company's web application consists of multiple Amazon EC2 instances that run behind an Application Load Balancer in a VPC. An Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance contains the data. The company needs the ability to automatically detect and respond to suspicious or unexpected behavior in its AWS environment. The company already has added AWS WAF to its architecture.
What should a solutions architect do next to protect against threats?
explanation_en:
WAF has deployed and filtered known attack patterns. The next level is the detection of unusual behaviour in accounts and networks, and this is Amazon GuardDuty: it analyzes Claudia Trail, VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs and data events to detect detection, calls to known malicious addresses and unusual API activities. Automatic responses are based on standard build modules: found results flow into EventBridge, and then a Lambda function adds default IP addresses to the IP concentration in Web ACL.
Option B: Firewall Manager deploys WAF, Shield and Network Firewall policies between accounts. It does not conduct threat tests and does not produce findings.
Option C: Inspector detects gaps in mirrors and examples, rather than suspicious behaviour, and it does not update WAF rules.
Option D: Macie classifys sensitive data in S3. It has nothing to do with detecting threats in the environment.

options.text: Use Amazon GuardDuty to perform threat detection. Configure Amazon EventBridge to filter for GuardDuty findings and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to adjust the AWS WAF rules.
Use AWS Firewall Manager to perform threat detection. Configure Amazon EventBridge to filter for Firewall Manager findings and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to adjust the AWS WAF web ACL.
Use Amazon Inspector to perform threat detection and to update the AWS WAF rules. Create a VPC network ACL to limit access to the web application.
Use Amazon Macie to perform threat detection and to update the AWS WAF rules. Create a VPC network ACL to limit access to the web application.

question_text:
A company is planning to run a group of Amazon EC2 instances that connect to an Amazon Aurora database. The company has built an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy the EC2 instances and the Aurora DB cluster. The company wants to allow the instances to authenticate to the database in a secure way. The company does not want to maintain static database credentials.
Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
explanation_en:
This requirement is not supported by the maintenance of static databases. The problem was solved by the IAM database authentication: the IAM authentication was launched on the Aurora cluster, a database user with rds_iam privileges was created, and the application in the example calledgenerate-db-auth-token and used the temporary token (valid for 15 minutes) to connect. rds-db: connect permission comes from role attached to example - therefore identity comes from role, and no password exists.
Option A: Transmission of user names and passwords as template parameters remains static and will eventually occur in stacking parameters and case profiles.
Option B: Parameter Store only stores the same static password, which still needs to be rotated manually. This requirement not to maintain static evidence has not been met.
Option D: IAM users cannot "associate with examples": Examples are role-based. The database username does not need to match the IAM username when using IAM authentication.

options.text: Create a database user with a user name and password. Add parameters for the database user name and password to the CloudFormation template. Pass the parameters to the EC2 instances when the instances are launched.

Create a database user with a user name and password. Store the user name and password in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure the EC2 instances to retrieve the database credentials from Parameter Store.

Configure the DB cluster to use IAM database authentication. Create a database user to use with IAM authentication. Associate a role with the EC2 instances to allow applications on the instances to access the database.

Configure the DB cluster to use IAM database authentication with an IAM user. Create a database user that has a name that matches the IAM user. Associate the IAM user with the EC2 instances to allow applications on the instances to access the database.

question_text:
A company wants to configure its Amazon CloudFront distribution to use SSL/TLS certificates. The company does not want to use the default domain name for the distribution. Instead, the company wants to use a different domain name for the distribution.
Which solution will deploy the certificate without incurring any additional costs?
explanation_en:
The custom domain name on the CloudFront requires a public certificate and the public certificate issued by ACM is free of charge. Important details: The certificate for CloudFront must be located in the area of us-east-1, regardless of where the source station is located.
Option A: Private certificates are issued by AWS Private CA, which is a fee-paying service; the browser does not trust them either by default.
Option B: Certificates here are both private and in the wrong area.
Option D: Certificates are public and free, but area error: CloudFront accepts only certificates from the us-east-1 area.

options.text: Request an Amazon issued private certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.
Request an Amazon issued private certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-west-1 Region.
Request an Amazon issued public certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the us-east-1 Region.

question_text:
A company creates operations data and stores the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. For the company's annual audit, an external consultant needs to access an annual report that is stored in the S3 bucket. The external consultant needs to access the report for 7 days.
The company must implement a solution to allow the external consultant access to only the report.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
explanation_en:
The requirement is to grant limited time access to a single object to an outside person without creating an account for them. This is the role of the pre-signed URL: the link uses your permission to sign with expiry time, and the recipient simply downloads the file via HTTPS. No content needs to be created and subsequently removed - the link will expire itself. A useful figure: a pre-signed URL with a long-term certificate can survive for up to seven days (604,800 seconds), which is exactly the time required; and a URL signed with a temporary character certificate will stop working as soon as the document is invalidated.
Option A: Moves the operating data into a publicly accessible web S3 bucket and exposes the entire data set to the entire Internet for a report. The risks are greatest and the benefits are minimal.
Option B: A week of public access for the entire drum is the same mistake: the consultant needs only a report, but all the company's data is exposed.
Option C: Create an IAM user and access key for outsiders is a long-term voucher that needs to be created, passed through secure channels and must be remembered for revocation. The workload is higher and the risks are higher.

options.text: Create a new S3 bucket that is configured to host a public static website. Migrate the operations data to the new S3 bucket. Share the S3 website URL with the external consultant.
Enable public access to the S3 bucket for 7 days. Remove access to the S3 bucket when the external consultant completes the audit.
Create a new IAM user that has access to the report in the S3 bucket. Provide the access keys to the external consultant. Revoke the access keys after 7 days.
Generate a presigned URL that has the required access to the location of the report on the S3 bucket. Share the presigned URL with the external consultant.

question_text:
A company plans to run a high performance computing (HPC) workload on Amazon EC2 Instances. The workload requires low-latency network performance and high network throughput with tightly coupled node-to-node communication.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Closely calibrated calculations require extremely low delays and high throughput between nodes. A cluster placement group will bring together examples within a single available area to the extent possible, providing low-delayed, full bandwidth network connections — a standard solution for high performance calculations.
Option B: The exclusive tenants affect the hardware you share, not the network delay between nodes.
Option C: Predatory examples change pricing models and are recoverable - not related to network characteristics.
Option D: The capacity reservation guarantee example can be activated, but there is no guarantee that the example will be placed close enough.

options.text: Configure the EC2 instances to be part of a cluster placement group.
Launch the EC2 instances with Dedicated Instance tenancy.
Launch the EC2 instances as Spot Instances.
Configure an On-Demand Capacity Reservation when the EC2 instances are launched.

question_text:
A company has primary and secondary data centers that are 500 miles (804.7 km) apart and interconnected with high-speed fiber-optic cable. The company needs a highly available and secure network connection between its data centers and a VPC on AWS for a mission-critical workload. A solutions architect must choose a connection solution that provides maximum resiliency.
Which solution meets these requirements?
explanation_en:
The maximum tolerance recommended by AWS is achieved when each failure point is eliminated: each data centre has two connections that are terminated at two different DirectConnect positions, connecting to different devices. As a result, failure of routers, failure of the DirectConnect position, cable failure or failure of the entire data centre will not disrupt VPC connectivity.
Option A: Connections are only initiated from the primary data centre: their failure will completely disrupt connectivity and the secondary site has never been truly connected.
Option B: One location and one device are two shared failure points for two connections.
Option D: The device is different, but only one location, and each data centre has only one connection running: error tolerance is far from maximum.

options.text: Two AWS Direct Connect connections from the primary data center terminating at two Direct Connect locations on two separate devices
A single AWS Direct Connect connection from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at one Direct Connect location on the same device
Two AWS Direct Connect connections from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at two Direct Connect locations on two separate devices
A single AWS Direct Connect connection from each of the primary and secondary data centers terminating at one Direct Connect location on two separate devices

question_text:
A company runs several Amazon RDS for Oracle On-Demand DB instances that have high utilization. The RDS DB instances run in member accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations.
The company's finance team has access to the organization's management account and member accounts. The finance team wants to find ways to optimize costs by using AWS Trusted Advisor.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
This answer consists of two parts. View location: the use of Trusted Advisor in the management accounts of the organization allows one-time access to all member accounts, so that the financial team does not have to check them individually (A). View content: These examples are used at a high rate and are running on a continuous basis, so the savings come from the purchase commitment - RDS retention cases optimized to show where the benefit is to be derived from changing from the required example to the retention example (C).
Option B: Checking each member ' s account is unnecessary: the results of the check have been aggregated in the organisational view in Trusted Advisor.
Option D: Free DB case checks will find examples of low usage, and the scene clearly indicates high usage. It does not give rise to any suggestions in this scene.
Option E: Compute Optimizer and the computational optimization check apply to EC2, Lambda and other computing resources, while this scenario is for RDS.

options.text: Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations in the management account.
Use the Trusted Advisor recommendations in the member accounts where the RDS DB instances are running.
Review the Trusted Advisor checks for Amazon RDS Reserved Instance Optimization.
Review the Trusted Advisor checks for Amazon RDS Idle DB Instances.
Review the Trusted Advisor checks for compute optimization. Crosscheck the results by using AWS Compute Optimizer.

question_text:
A solutions architect is creating an application. The application will run on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets across multiple Availability Zones in a VPC. The EC2 instances will frequently access large files that contain confidential information. These files are stored in Amazon S3 buckets for processing. The solutions architect must optimize the network architecture to minimize data transfer costs.
What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The goal is to reduce the cost of data transmission when visiting large and medium-sized S3 files on a regular basis. The gateway endpoint for S3 is completely free: there is no hourly fee, no gilabyte processing fee, and traffic will remain in the AWS internal network. The only operation that is required is to add a route to the list of private subsystems.
Option B: A NAT gateway means a fee per gigabyte for processing, as well as cross-regional flows from other regional examples. This is the most expensive option for large documents.
Option C: S3 exists at the interface endpoint, but it is charged hourly and per gigabyte for processing, while the gateway endpoint is free of charge. It records work through an address and DNS, not through the route list entries.
Option D: Each region is equipped with a NAT gateway that removes the cross-regional component, but the cost of processing each Gi byte still exists and increases as the number of large files increases.

options.text: Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC. In the route tables for the private subnets, add an entry for the gateway endpoint.
Create a single NAT gateway in a public subnet. In the route tables for the private subnets, add a default route that points to the NAT gateway.
Create an AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPIn the route tables for the private subnets, add an entry for the interface endpoint.

Create one NAT gateway for each Availability Zone in public subnets. In each of the route tables for the private subnets, add a default route that points to the NAT gateway in the same Availability Zone.

question_text:
A company wants to relocate its on-premises MySQL database to AWS. The database accepts regular imports from a client-facing application, which causes a high volume of write operations. The company is concerned that the amount of traffic might be causing performance issues within the application.
How should a solutions architect design the architecture on AWS?
explanation_en:
The problem is directly stated: writing operations are large and I/O performance is suspected to be inadequate. An example of a manager with preset IOPS SSD storage RDS for MySQL provides a manageable assurance that the IOPS, CloudWatch indicator shows the real situation, and can increase its value if needed without changing the structure.
Option B: A ElastiCache cache can be read faster, but the load here is written: bottlenecks remain. The query cannot be simply redirected to a cache rather than a database.
Option C: DocumentDB compatible with MongoDB instead of MySQL: Applications and data models need to be rewrited.
Option D: EFS is a file system, not a relationship database. The storage of MySQL databases on EFS under high-written loads is a bad option for performance and integrity.

options.text: Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with Provisioned IOPS SSD storage. Monitor write operation metrics by using Amazon CloudWatch. Adjust the provisioned IOPS if necessary.

Provision an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance with General Purpose SSD storage. Place an Amazon ElastiCache cluster in front of the DB instance. Configure the application to query ElastiCache instead.

Provision an Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) instance with a memory optimized instance type. Monitor Amazon CloudWatch for performance-related issues. Change the instance class if necessary.

Provision an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system in General Purpose performance mode. Monitor Amazon CloudWatch for IOPS bottlenecks. Change to Provisioned Throughput performance mode if necessary.

question_text:
A company runs an application in the AWS Cloud that generates sensitive archival data files. The company wants to rearchitect the application's data storage. The company wants to encrypt the data files and to ensure that third parties do not have access to the data before the data is encrypted and sent to AWS. The company has already created an Amazon S3 bucket.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The key phrase is: "The third party has no access to the data until the data is encrypted and sent to AWS". All server-end encryption is done inside AWS and is not performed until data is received, and therefore neither SSE-KMS nor double-layer DSSE-KMS meet the requirements. Data must be encrypted by the application before being sent - this is the client encryption. It is convenient to keep the key in KMS: the application requests the data key from KMS, encrypts the file locally using the key and sends the secret to S3 with a encrypted copy of the data key (i.e. the Envelope Encryption Program)
Option A: "Current encryption using S3 management keys" is not a real configuration: the SSE-S3 key will never leave the service, and the client encryption is configured in the application, not in the S3 bucket.
Option B: SSE-KMS encrypts objects after they are received by S3. Until then, the data had not been protected — that was what needed to be avoided.
Option C: DSSE-KMS adds a second layer of encryption, but all operations are still done at the service end and only after the object has been received.

options.text: Configure the S3 bucket to use client-side encryption with an Amazon S3 managed encryption key. Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
Configure the S3 bucket to use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
Configure the S3 bucket to use dual-layer server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Configure the application to use the S3 bucket to store the archival files.
Configure the application to use client-side encryption with a key stored in AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Configure the application to store the archival files in the S3 bucket.

question_text:
A company uses Amazon RDS with default backup settings for its database tier. The company needs to make a daily backup of the database to meet regulatory requirements. The company must retain the backups for 30 days.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
RDS already has an automatic backup feature - just change the backup retention period to 30 days. The backup is automatically completed daily by the service itself and can be kept for a maximum of 35 days without any additional operation or code.
Option A: A custom function is used for daily snapshots, repeats built-in functions and requires continuous maintenance.
Option C: The system manager maintains the window to handle the managed resource movement, while the backup retention cycle for RDS is configured on the example itself.
Option D: Creating a snapshot manually every day through the CLI is the greatest operational effort possible.

options.text: Write an AWS Lambda function to create an RDS snapshot every day.
Modify the RDS database to have a retention period of 30 days for automated backups.
Use AWS Systems Manager Maintenance Windows to modify the RDS backup retention period.
Create a manual snapshot every day by using the AWS CLI. Modify the RDS backup retention period.

question_text:
A company that runs its application on AWS uses an Amazon Aurora DB cluster as its database. During peak usage hours when multiple users access and read the data, the monitoring system shows degradation of database performance for the write queries. The company wants to increase the scalability of the application to meet peak usage demands.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The reading operation interferes with the writing operation and therefore requires separation. Aurora reading copy in the same cluster is delayed to read data from shared storage only in milliseconds and added in one step: the application sends the reading operation to the reading end and the writing operation to the cluster end. This is the cheapest approach — to add only one example, which is not replicated by itself.
Option A: A second cluster with a copy operation means a doubling of storage costs, data delays and ongoing maintenance workload.
Option B: DAX is the cache of DynamoDB - it is completely incompatible with Aurora.
Option D: RedShift is an analytical data repository that also requires a separate loading conduit: it is expensive and not suitable for daily queries from applications.

options.text: Create a second Aurora DB cluster. Configure a copy job to replicate the users’ data to the new database. Update the application to use the second database to read the data.

Create an Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster in front of the existing Aurora DB cluster. Update the application to use the DAX cluster for read-only queries. Write data directly to the Aurora DB cluster.
Create an Aurora read replica in the existing Aurora DB cluster. Update the application to use the replica endpoint for read-only queries and to use the cluster endpoint for write queries.
Create an Amazon Redshift cluster. Copy the users' data to the Redshift cluster. Update the application to connect to the Redshift cluster and to perform read-only queries on the Redshift cluster.

question_text:
A company's near-real-time streaming application is running on AWS. As the data is ingested, a job runs on the data and takes 30 minutes to complete. The workload frequently experiences high latency due to large amounts of incoming data. A solutions architect needs to design a scalable and serverless solution to enhance performance.
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
The minimum operating cost for ingestion of data streams requires Kinesis Data Firehose: it expands automatically and buffers and transmits data without the need to manage the fraction (A). The processing takes 30 minutes, which is twice the limit of the Lambda function, so the remaining no server option is AWS Fargate running on ECS - the time required for the task to continue without managing the server (E).
Option B: The performance limit for the Lambda function is 15 minutes, and the task takes 30 minutes. Even if work is to be split using Step Forces, the logic needs to be rewritten.
Option C: DMS Migration Database Data - It is not used for ingestion of stream data.
Option D: A set of EC2 instances is an infrastructure that needs to be maintained, and a server-free solution is needed.

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to ingest the data.
Use AWS Lambda with AWS Step Functions to process the data.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to ingest the data.
Use Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to process the data.
Use AWS Fargate with Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to process the data.

question_text:
A company runs a web application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. The application needs to write sensitive data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The data cannot be sent over the public internet.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The requirement is that data should not be transmitted through the public Internet. The endpoint of the S3 gateway will add a path to the service prefix in the VPC routeboard, and the call to the barrel will be kept inside the AWS network. In addition, drums can be restricted by the aws:sourceVpce condition so that they can only accept requests for passage through the endpoint.
Option B: S3 drums cannot be registered as the goal of the load balancer: it is a service, not a network resource with an internal VPC address.
Option C: Cannot place drums inside VPC - S3 is a regional service located outside your network.
Option D: Connect the company 's local site directly to AWS, but the example is already inside AWS.

options.text: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3. Create a route in the VPC route table to the endpoint.
Create an internal Network Load Balancer that has the S3 bucket as the target.
Deploy the S3 bucket inside the VPCreate a route in the VPC route table to the bucket.
Create an AWS Direct Connect connection between the VPC and an S3 regional endpoint.

question_text:
A company runs its production workload on Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. A solutions architect needs to analyze the current EBS volume cost and to recommend optimizations. The recommendations need to include estimated monthly saving opportunities.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Recommendations on the size, type and cost of EBS volumes, including monthly savings estimates, from AWS Compute Optimizer: it analyses the Cloudwatch indicators of recent weeks and proposes, for example, IOPS from gp2 to gp3 or lower distributions to demonstrate the estimated savings. In addition to EBS, it covers EC2 instances, Auto Scaling, the Lambda function and ECS tasks on Fargate.
Option A: Inspector detects a loophole, but does not recommend any storage cost at all.
Option B: Systems Manager manages the whole set of examples: includes asset lists, patch management, access controls. It does not process volume cost optimization.
Option C: Cloudwatch provides indicators, but does not translate them into recommendations and estimated savings - it is the Compute Optimizer that does this function on the basis of the same indicators.

options.text: Use Amazon Inspector reporting to generate EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
Use AWS Systems Manager reporting to determine EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics reporting to determine EBS volume recommendations for optimization.
Use AWS Compute Optimizer to generate EBS volume recommendations for optimization.

question_text:
A global company runs its workloads on AWS. The company's application uses Amazon S3 buckets across AWS Regions for sensitive data storage and analysis. The company stores millions of objects in multiple S3 buckets daily. The company wants to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Option A is missing in source PDF
S3 Storage Lens has a Versioning-enabled Bucket count indicator that identifies unenabled S3 buckets by the bucket dimension, so there is a basis for B; however, the source title A is missing and cannot be considered a complete comparable option, B is retained and the missing item is marked.
This is an inventory task: in many of the S3 buckets in multiple regions, those that are not controlled by the unused version are identified. Of the options, only S3 Service Lens can perform a one-time aggregated analysis of the drums in all regions and all accounts in the organization, and one of the indicators is the percentage of the drums controlled by the user version. This report clearly shows which drums fall short of the standards. In practice, AWS Config with the s3-buchet-versioning-enabled rule can also solve the same task - option A is missing in source PDF, probably for that reason.
Option C: IAM Access Analyzer for S3 will search for accessable barrels from outside the account or organization. It does not check the version control status.
Option D: Multi-area access points are the entry points for requests to different S3 buckets in different areas. It does not generate configuration reports.

options.text: Use Amazon S3 Storage Lens to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
Enable IAM Access Analyzer for S3 to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.
Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point to identify all S3 buckets that are not versioning-enabled across Regions.

question_text:
A company wants to enhance its ecommerce order-processing application that is deployed on AWS. The application must process each order exactly once without affecting the customer experience during unpredictable traffic surges.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The requirement is that each order be processed strictly only once and that it be able to withstand an unpredictable surge in flows. A SQS FIFO queue achieves a strictly one-time processing by discarding duplicate messages, while the buffer line smooths the surge in traffic: the Lambda function handles orders at its own rhythm and customers are completely undetected.
Option B: A standard SNS theme will process the message at least once and will not buffer the surge in traffic - orders may be processed twice or lost during a malfunction.
Option C: AppFlow moves data between SaaS services; it does not process orders.
Option D: X-Ray tracking request; "Claudwatch to extract an order" is not any sort of processing mechanism.

options.text: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Put all the orders in the SQS queue. Configure an AWS Lambda function as the target to process the orders.
Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) standard topic. Publish all the orders to the SNS standard topic. Configure the application as a notification target.
Create a flow by using Amazon AppFlow. Send the orders to the flow. Configure an AWS Lambda function as the target to process the orders.
Configure AWS X-Ray in the application to track the order requests. Configure the application to process the orders by pulling the orders from Amazon CloudWatch.

question_text:
A company has two AWS accounts: Production and Development. The company needs to push code changes in the Development account to the Production account. In the alpha phase, only two senior developers on the development team need access to the Production account. In the beta phase, more developers will need access to perform testing.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Original answer: D; source correction answer: C.
The key points are contradictory: the group in the production account is named as the subject of the trust strategy, which itself refers to the production account; cross-account access should be achieved through a role in the production account that trusts the development account
Cross-account access to IAM lole should be based on the target Production account and use trust policy to trust the authorized subject in the Development account; the authority to assume the role should be adjusted with the additional tester. The IAM group of source D cannot be used as trust policy paper, as C.
A role has always been created in the location of resources: in the production account, its confidence strategy points to the development account (C). The developer expands access by assuming the role through STS, while at the Beta stage, by adding people to the source account - the role itself does not need to change.
Option A: The manual preparation of two strategies in each account does not build trust between the accounts: without a trust strategy, the role cannot be assumed. And it's not going to go well.
Option B: The role in the development account cannot be delegated the authority to produce the resource: the authority is granted by the account with the resource.
Option D: The IAM group cannot be the subject of a trust policy, while the production account trusts itself without giving developers any authority.

options.text: Create two policy documents by using the AWS Management Console in each account. Assign the policy to developers who need access.
Create an IAM role in the Development account. Grant the IAM role access to the Production account. Allow developers to assume the role.
Create an IAM role in the Production account. Define a trust policy that specifies the Development account. Allow developers to assume the role.
Create an IAM group in the Production account. Add the group as a principal in a trust policy that specifies the Production account. Add developers to the group.

question_text:
A company wants to restrict access to the content of its web application. The company needs to protect the content by using authorization techniques that are available on AWS. The company also wants to implement a serverless architecture for authorization and authentication that has low login latency.
The solution must integrate with the web application and serve web content globally. The application currently has a small user base, but the company expects the application's user base to increase.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Same as in question 345: no server authentication, global distribution and minimal login delay. Cognito is responsible for user administration and issuance of tokens, and CloudFront provides applications from the edges, which are verified directly at the edges in the Lambda@Edge function, so the user can complete the authorization without having to reach the source area. The design is linearly expanded with the growth of the user base.
Option B: The hosting Microsoft AD is a fee-based catalogue service that is too complex for applications with a smaller user base, and ALB cannot achieve global content distribution.
Option C: An ordinary Lambda function runs in a single area, which increases the authorized delay, and S3 transmissions accelerate only the speed of uploading the S3 buckets and cannot be used to provide the content of the website.
Option D: AD directories are once again too complex and Elastic Beanstalk means using servers rather than without server structures.

options.text: Configure Amazon Cognito for authentication. Implement Lambda@Edge for authorization. Configure Amazon CloudFront to serve the web application globally.
Configure AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Implement AWS Lambda for authorization. Use an Application Load Balancer to serve the web application globally.
Configure Amazon Cognito for authentication. Implement AWS Lambda for authorization. Use Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration to serve the web application globally.
Configure AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory for authentication. Implement Lambda@Edge for authorization. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to serve the web application globally.

question_text:
A development team uses multiple AWS accounts for its development, staging, and production environments.
Team members have been launching large Amazon EC2 instances that are underutilized. A solutions architect must prevent large instances from being launched in all accounts.
How can the solutions architect meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
This restriction must be effective in all accounts, cannot be bypassed locally and needs to be maintained from a single location. This is the Service Control Policy (SCP): Organizations create a strategy to set the rejection conditions for the ec2: RunInstances operation in this strategy, provided that the type of instance is not in the allowed list (ec2: InstanceType) and that the policy is attached to the relevant account or organizational unit (OU). SCP is effective for every subject (including root users) in the account, so the developer is unable to circumvent this limitation through its own created strategy. The same technology appears in question 492.
Option A: IAM policies must be maintained separately in each account and account administrators can change them. They are not valid for root users at all.
Option B: AWS RAM shares resources between accounts. It is not possible to reject the type of instance.
Option C: A character does not reject any operation by itself: the developer can perform the operation without passing through the role. In addition, the role still needs to be created and maintained in each account.

options.text: Update the IAM policies to deny the launch of large EC2 instances. Apply the policies to all users.
Define a resource in AWS Resource Access Manager that prevents the launch of large EC2 instances.
Create an IAM role in each account that denies the launch of large EC2 instances. Grant the developers IAM group access to the role.

Create an organization in AWS Organizations in the management account with the default policy. Create a service control policy (SCP) that denies the launch of large EC2 instances, and apply it to the AWS accounts.

question_text:
A company has migrated a fleet of hundreds of on-premises virtual machines (VMs) to Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run a diverse fleet of Windows Server versions along with several Linux distributions. The company wants a solution that will automate inventory and updates of the operating systems. The company also needs a summary of common vulnerabilities of each instance for regular monthly reviews.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
There are two requirements: to centralize automated inventory and operating system updates in a variety of equipment groups and to obtain monthly summary reports of gaps. The first requirement is covered by Systems Manager: Inventory collects lists of installed software, Patch Manager updates the Windows and Linux systems based on patches and displays compliance status. The second requirement is covered by Amazon Inspector: continuous CVE database scanning of software packages to generate reports for monthly review.
Option A: Security Hub aggregates the findings from other services, but does not find a loophole in itself: without Inspector, there is nothing to build the report.
Option C: Shield Advanced is used against DDoS attacks, while AWS Config records configuration information does not install updates.
Option D: GuardDuty detects suspicious activity, not a loophole, and AWS Config is not a patch management tool.

options.text: Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to manage all the EC2 instances. Configure AWS Security Hub to produce monthly reports.
Set up AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager to manage all the EC2 instances. Deploy Amazon Inspector, and configure monthly reports.
Set up AWS Shield Advanced, and configure monthly reports. Deploy AWS Config to automate patch installations on the EC2 instances.
Set up Amazon GuardDuty in the account to monitor all EC2 instances. Deploy AWS Config to automate patch installations on the EC2 instances.

question_text:
A company hosts its application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. The application connects to an Amazon DynamoDB table.
For disaster recovery (DR) purposes, the company wants to ensure that the application is available from another AWS Region with minimal downtime.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST downtime?
explanation_en:
Original answer: C; source correction answer: A.
The key description is light-weight start-up (the infrastructure is created only after a disaster occurs); given the minimum downtime requirements, what is needed is heat readiness, i.e. the automatic stretching group and the ERB are already operating in the disaster recovery area
At a minimum, the stopover requires the pre-run of the ASG and ERB, DynamoDB Global Tables, which are continuously copied and transferred by DNS health check failure. Original C deploys the balance of calculations and loads after failure and recovers for longer periods; read A
The minimum downtime requirement corresponds to the heat preparation: an automatic stretcher group and load balancer are already operating in the disaster recovery area, DynamoDB is operating as a global table, switching to DNS failure transfer (A). There is no need to wait for infrastructure to be created.
Option B: Examples, load balancers and tables created through ClaudFormation in the event of a disaster are in the `light start-up' mode: deployment takes only a few minutes — this is the stop time that is required to be avoided.
Option C: The same lightweight start-up mode: The global table already exists, but the computational layer is created only when the disaster actually occurs.
Option D: The infrastructure here is ready, but switch to a Cloudwatch alert (10 minutes assessment cycle) and a Lambda function. This would add at least the same 10-minute stop time to the Route 53 health check-up in a few seconds.

question_text:

explanation_en:
The flow of S3 must not go through the public Internet and solutions need to be inexpensive. The end point of the S3 gateway adds a service prefix to the private sub-network's route chart and is completely free of charge: there is no hourly fee and there is no cost per gigabyte of processing.

question_text:
A company hosts an application on Amazon EC2 instances that run in a single Availability Zone. The application is accessible by using the transport layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model. The company needs the application architecture to have high availability.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
The "OSI model's transmission layer" is the fourth level, meaning TCP or UDP, which requires a network load balancer (B). High availability comes from automatic extension groups distributed across multiple available areas and uses applied health checks: failure of a single available area or case is automatically compensated (D). This combination is the least costly option — without additional services and without manual operation.
Option A: Route 53 allocates the address, but it does not remove the example of a failure or restore the capacity immediately. The manual addition of examples is not highly usable.
Option C: The configuration of a second load balancer for HTTP is unnecessary: the scene has been assigned a transfer layer, and the additional ALB only increases costs.

explanation_en:
Fewer than 100 visits per month meant that there was no reason to charge for an ongoing server. The form is serviced and processed through the post-API Gateway Lambda function and the company is notified by posting messages to SNS themes with e-mail subscriptions. The cost of this setting is zero in idle state. A similar process is shown in question 285.

question_text:
A company creates dedicated AWS accounts in AWS Organizations for its business units. Recently, an important notification was sent to the root user email address of a business unit account instead of the assigned account owner. The company wants to ensure that all future notifications can be sent to different employees based on the notification categories of billing, operations, or security.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?
explanation_en:
Reference answer: A; dispute option: D.
The content of the option allows every account owner to access the same mailbox, which contradicts the most secure requirements
The root e-mail should be managed by a controlled centralized mailbox or aliases, and should not be shared by all business account holders to access the same root mailbox; separate sets for Billing, Security, and Operations alternate contacts can be delivered by category. Source A ' s extensive shared root mailbox is not safe enough to read D.
Source answer A's original resolution (in conflict with verification results, not accepted):
That requirement was the most stringent in terms of security, and each notification must therefore be sent only to its designated addressee. The correct AWS is achieved by retaining the root address in the company-managed distribution list (rather than in the individual employee's mailbox) and by allocating the back-up contact — billings to the Treasury and security incidents to the security team — by category (e.g. billing, operation and security). Option A gives the source practice information key, which is its weakness: it proposes a shared mailbox accessible to all account owners, in direct violation of the minimum permission principle. Option A describes the alternate contact correctly; the dispute is only at the location to which the root address is directed.
Old Source Option B: This is the strongest option from a security point of view: each business module has its own distribution list for root addresses and sets up a stand-by contact by category. No one will read emails from other accounts.
Old Source Option C: Linking root addresses to a person ' s personal mailbox is a well-known error: restoration of access to the account is lost when an employee takes leave or leaves. AWS explicitly recommends the use of distribution lists rather than individual mailboxes.
Old Source Option D: A centralized mailbox is more convenient to reconcile account records with aliases, but it also means that a shared mailbox receives all account root notifications. This went beyond what was necessary and failed to achieve a separate distribution list for each business module.

question_text:
A company runs an ecommerce application on AWS. Amazon EC2 instances process purchases and store the purchase details in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.
Customers are experiencing application timeouts during times of peak usage. A solutions architect needs to rearchitect the application so that the application can scale to meet peak usage demands.
Which combination of actions will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
The problem of time overruns during peak loads is resolved through two separate technologies. Purchase requests are entered into a SQS queue and will be processed on the basis of examples from the Auto Scaling group with the extended queue length: peaks are smoothed and no order is lost (C). The read load of the database is unloaded (B) through the ElastiCache cache in front of the Aurora cluster. These steps are cheaper than upgrading the database capacity.
Option A: Unbuffered retry will only exacerbate the storm of requests for already loaded databases, and RDS Proxy addresses the connection pool, not the peak handling load.
Option D: Retesting in the Lambda function has the same disadvantage: there is no queue, so the load is not smoothed.
Option E: The use schedule in API Gateway limits the client, meaning that it will discard some of the purchase requests rather than process them.

explanation_en:
Cost and use reports are stored as files in S3, so the dashboard is constructed by the chain "Athena Reads the file, QuickSight Visualizes it". Athena converts the export to a SQL table and divides it into a month, QuickSight connects it to a data source and allows you to share the dashboard with management. For requested slices, just filter the rows according to the NAT gateway service and group them according to the number of days of the current month.

Option C: Cloudwatch is built from the indicator build dashboard instead of from the report file in S3 and cannot query them.
