question_text:
A company is hosting a high-traffic static website on Amazon S3 with an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has a default TTL of 0 seconds. The company wants to implement caching to improve performance for the website.
However, the company also wants to ensure that stale content is not served for more than a few minutes after a deployment.
Which combination of caching methods should a solutions architect implement to meet these requirements?
(Choose two.)
explanation_en:
Reference answer: AC; dispute option: AE.
Cache-Control: pirvate completely disables the cache of CloudFront, contrary to the purpose of the cache; it is more rational to use TTL in conjunction with invalid operations when deployed
Cache-Control: Private usually makes CloudFront unquenchable and cannot be used to raise the edge Cache Cache Rate. The 24-hour max-age co-opt each deployment to initiate invalidation of all changes; two minutes of A default TTL only works when the source is not specified, and objects max-age encountering E will be overridden. So AE is an optional combination, but A has no additional effect on objects over E and needs to wait for invalidation to take effect.
Source answer AC original resolution (in conflict with verification results, not accepted):
TTL is currently zero, which means Claude Front returns to S3 every request. Caches need to be activated, but it is important to ensure that after deployment, expired content does not survive for more than a few minutes. The direct solution is option A: the default TTL is 2 minutes, so the object automatically expires within 2 minutes of the release. The second key point is controversial: the Cache-Control: Private directive prohibits caches in shared caches, including CloudFront, which effectively negates the purpose of the entire programme. The A logic matches option E: a longer max-age plus deployment cache failure. Remember the difference: TTL limits the time during which content may expire without intervention, while the cache lapses when the object is removed from the cache at the time of the specified event.
Source old option B: No TTL settings for an S3 S3 bucket. Cache is valid for Cache-Control headup settings for cache actions or objects distributed by Cloud Front.
Source old option D: Lambda@Edge modifies the response head sent to the end client in the audience response after the object has passed the CloudFront cache, which does not affect the retention time of the object at the edge. In addition, it would add additional codes and additional costs.
Old Source Option E: A powerful alternative: A maximum cache time of 24 hours will maximize the cache liferate, while the ineffectiveness of each deployment ensures that new content reaches all locations immediately. The key points prefer shorter TTLs, because even if invalid operations are forgotten, they prevent the content from becoming obsolete.

explanation_en:
Developers need to be warned about expenditures and when budget ceilings are exhausted, the creation of new resources must be stopped automatically. This is precisely what the AWS budget function achieves: setting a budget for each account, alerting real and projected values, and applying a rejection strategy to the developers ' IAM role through budget actions when the threshold is reached. question_text:
A solutions architect is designing a three-tier web application. The architecture consists of an internet-facing Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a web tier that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. The application tier with the business logic runs on EC2 instances in private subnets. The database tier consists of Microsoft SQL Server that runs on EC2 instances in private subnets. Security is a high priority for the company.
Which combination of security group configurations should the solutions architect use? (Choose three.)
explanation_en:
The rule is simple: each level receives traffic only from its previous level and only on the required port, and the source address is specified by reference to the security group instead of the IP address. The Web level receives HTTPS traffic from the ALB Security Group (A), the Application Level receives HTTPS traffic from the Web Level Security Group (E) and the Database receives SQL Server traffic from the Application Level Security Group (C).

question_text:
A company plans to rehost an application to Amazon EC2 instances that use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) as the attached storage.
A solutions architect must design a solution to ensure that all newly created Amazon EBS volumes are encrypted by default. The solution must also prevent the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Original answer: B; source correction answer: A.
AWS Config only detects irregularities; preventing unencrypted volumes from being created by "always encrypt new EBS volumes"
The EC2/EBS encryption by default settings allow the account number and area to always be encrypted by creating a new EBS volume, even if the request does not explicitly require encryption. The AWS Config rule only detects a fait accompli of non-compliance and cannot be stopped before it is created; source B is changed to A.
There are two requirements: encryption of all new volumes and complete prevention of the creation of unencrypted ones. The EC2 account attribute "encryption by default" (A) is preventive - attempts to create unencrypted volumes in the region will fail directly.
Option B: AWS Config to mark irregularities after an event and to trigger repair, but will not prevent the volume from being created. It doesn't meet the requirements of "stop creating."
Option C: Systems Manager creates encrypted copies to manually fix existing volumes, rather than to prevent the creation of new ones.
Option D: Create KMS key and configure Migration Hub does not prevent any operation: simply the key itself does not force encryption to take effect.

question_text:
A company needs to optimize its Amazon S3 storage costs for an application that generates many files that cannot be recreated. Each file is approximately 5 MB and is stored in Amazon S3 Standard storage.
The company must store the files for 4 years before the files can be deleted. The files must be immediately accessible. The files are frequently accessed in the first 30 days of object creation, but they are rarely accessed after the first 30 days.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Same as the requirement in question 66: immediate access, unreconstructable documents, active for 30 days, kept for 4 years, then deleted. The difference is in the set of options: this option contains S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval, which returns to the object at a millisecond level, the same as Standard-IA, but the storage cost is only about one third of Standard-IA. For data that are rarely visited after 30 days, this is the cheapest category with immediate access. The trade-off is that the minimum storage lasts 90 days and is more expensive to retrieve - none of which conflicts with the scene.
Option B: One Zone-IA retains a copy in a usable area, and the file in the scene cannot be rebuilt. This risk is not worth some 20 per cent cost savings relative to Standard-IA.
Option C: A correct but not cheapest option: In the case of less frequent access, the storage cost of Glacier Instant Retrieval is only about one third of the same real-time search cost of Standard-IA.
Option D: This rule does not delete files after four years - it moves files to Glacier even if the strategy allows them to be deleted. You will pay for storage indefinitely and the data will remain in the more expensive Standard-IA for the first four years.

question_text:
A company runs its critical storage application in the AWS Cloud. The application uses Amazon S3 in two AWS Regions. The company wants the application to send remote user data to the nearest S3 bucket with no public network congestion. The company also wants the application to fail over with the least amount of management of Amazon S3.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
There are three requirements: to write to the most recent S3 buckets, to avoid congestion of the public Internet, and to make fault transfer in S3 with minimal management costs. Multi-area S3 access points provide a single global entry point: when requested to enter the AWS network, they enter from the nearest edge and then transfer to the nearest S3 bucket via the AWS core network; if an area is not available, the flow is automatically switched to another area. In order to keep the same object in two drums, cross-area copying is superseded. Active-active setting with a single global entry point is what is termed the `minimal management cost' here.
Option A: Direct access to the regional endpoint will pass through the public Internet, which is contrary to the requirement to avoid in the scene, and the failure transfer in the event of a regional failure must be encoded by the application itself.
Option B: Multi-area access points have a single global entry point - `Create an endpoint for each region' cannot be achieved through it. Active-passive settings do not allow the user to be routed to the nearest S3 bucket.
Option C: Cross-account copy is about different accounts, not different regions. The selection of the nearest entry point and the handling of the malfunctions will still have to be carried out by the application.

options.text: Implement an active-active design between the two Regions. Configure the application to use the regional S3 endpoints closest to the user.
Use an active-passive configuration with S3 Multi-Region Access Points. Create a global endpoint for each of the Regions.
Send user data to the regional S3 endpoints closest to the user. Configure an S3 cross-account replication rule to keep the S3 buckets synchronized.
Set up Amazon S3 to use Multi-Region Access Points in an active-active configuration with a single global endpoint. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication.

question_text:
A company is migrating a data center from its on-premises location to AWS. The company has several legacy applications that are hosted on individual virtual servers. Changes to the application designs cannot be made.
Each individual virtual server currently runs as its own EC2 instance. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the applications are reliable and fault tolerant after migration to AWS. The applications will run on Amazon EC2 instances.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Applications could not be changed, but needed to be able to withstand the failure of an available area. Captures one AMI from each instance, starts two copies from the AMI area in different serviceable areas and deploys load balancers at the front end to distribute traffic and exclude unhealthy backend targets. The application itself remains completely unchanged.
Option A: An example group restores the machine after a malfunction, but the application is not available during start-up: this does not constitute a fault tolerance.
Option B: A copy per hour is backup, not tolerance: recovery takes time and manual.
Option D: Splitting the application into components is precisely a structural change that the scene explicitly prohibits.

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group that has a minimum of one and a maximum of one. Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of each application instance. Use the AMI to create EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group Configure an Application Load Balancer in front of the Auto Scaling group.

Use AWS Backup to create an hourly backup of the EC2 instance that hosts each application. Store the backup in Amazon S3 in a separate Availability Zone. Configure a disaster recovery process to restore the EC2 instance for each application from its most recent backup.

Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of each application instance. Launch two new EC2 instances from the AMI. Place each EC2 instance in a separate Availability Zone. Configure a Network Load Balancer that has the EC2 instances as targets.

Use AWS Mitigation Hub Refactor Spaces to migrate each application off the EC2 instance. Break down functionality from each application into individual components. Host each application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with an AWS Fargate launch type.

question_text:
A company wants to isolate its workloads by creating an AWS account for each workload. The company needs a solution that centrally manages networking components for the workloads. The solution also must create accounts with automatic security controls (guardrails).

explanation_en:
Original answer: B; source correction answer: A.
The automatic protection rules for creating the account are from AWS Control Tower, which cannot be provided by the Organisations alone
Control Tower Account Actory can apply governance baseline/guardrails when new accounts are created; centralized network accounts share VPC sub-nets with task load accounts to reduce duplication. Original B creates account numbers only for Organisations and does not automatically provide required Control Tower security controls for the title; change to A.
There are two attributes that need to be met at the same time: accounts with automatic protective rules and a centralized network. The first attribute comes from Control Tower in conjunction with Account Factory, the second attribute comes from a network account that holds VPC and its subnet is shared with the task load account through AWS RAM.
Option B: AWS Organisations will not by themselves create an account with automatic protection rules: Preventive and detection controls are configured by Control Tower.
Option C: Control Tower is correct, but VPCs in each task load account perform traffic checks by checking VPC route, do not centrally manage network components and require large configurations.
Option D: This option combines two errors: an Organization without protection rules, and the use of a separate VPC instead of a shared subnet.

options.text: Use AWS Control Tower to deploy accounts. Create a networking account that has a VPC with private subnets and public subnets. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the subnets with the workload accounts.

Use AWS Organizations to deploy accounts. Create a networking account that has a VPC with private subnets and public subnets. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the subnets with the workload accounts.

question_text:
A company hosts a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website serves static content. Website traffic is increasing. The company wants to minimize the website hosting costs.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The site provides static content and therefore there is no need at all to calculate cluster and load balancers. The content will enter the S3 S3 bucket and be made available via CloudFront: you will only have to pay for storage and transmission costs, border caches will reduce the cost of transport out of the station, and traffic growth will not require an additional server.
Option B: ElastiCache is an area memory cache; it does not store the contents of the drums from the user service or form such a structure.
Option C: Amplify has made the website available through its own content distribution network; adding load balancers to it is futile and more expensive.
Option D: Use the EC2 instance as a cache in front of Amplify to reintroduce the server that the solution is designed to eliminate.

question_text:
A company is implementing a shared storage solution for a media application that the company hosts on AWS. The company needs the ability to use SMB clients to access stored data.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?
explanation_en:
Clients need SMB protocols, everything is running on AWS and management needs are extremely low. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server original supports the SMB protocol, supports Windows ACL and Active Directory, AWS maintains, backups and tolerance errors. The connection is simply a mount share. Similar processes are described in question 249.

Option B: Tape Gateway simulates a tape library for backup systems.

question_text:
A company is designing its production application's disaster recovery (DR) strategy. The application is backed by a MySQL database on an Amazon Aurora cluster in the us-east-1 Region. The company has chosen the us-west-1 Region as its DR Region.
The company's target recovery point objective (RPO) is 5 minutes and the target recovery time objective (RTO) is 20 minutes. The company wants to minimize configuration changes.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
explanation_en:
The request is for a 5-minute recovery point target, a 20-minute recovery time target and minimal configuration changes. The Aurora global database is replicated in storage, usually delayed at the subsecond level, and minor areas are elevated to the main area in individual operations through management failure transfer, while maintaining an extended structure. Applications continue to use the same cluster endpoints.
Option A: A cross-regional Aurora reading copy is copied through the logical layer with greater delay, and failure transfer is a manual process involving multiple steps.
Option C: An independent cluster is duplicated manually by configuration and is built manually, and failure to transfer to the cluster is also manual: RTO up to 20 minutes is suspicious.
Option D: DMS requires a copy of the example and ongoing maintenance, and it is not designed for the Aurora standard disaster recovery mechanism.

options.text: Create an Aurora read replica in us-west-1 similar in size to the production application's Aurora MySQL cluster writer instance.

question_text:
A company runs a critical data analysis job each week before the first day of the work week. The job requires at least 1 hour to complete the analysis. The job is stateful and cannot tolerate interruptions. The company needs a solution to run the job on AWS.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The operation lasted at least one hour, was state-of-the-art and could not tolerate interruptions. This excludes the 15-minute limit for the Lambda function and possible interruptions. AWS Fargate operates containers on ECS, which can be operated on an ongoing basis as required, without the need to manage servers, while EventBridge Scheduler arranges them in the weekly plan.
Option B: The Lambda function is limited to 15 minutes and the operation takes at least one hour.
Option C: AWS can recycle Spot at any time and the operation cannot tolerate interruptions.
Option D: DataSync is used to transfer data between storage systems, rather than to run random operations.

question_text:
A company runs workloads in the AWS Cloud. The company wants to centrally collect security data to assess security across the entire company and to improve workload protection.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
explanation_en:
Amazon Security Lake is designed for this scenario: it collects security data from AWS services, local sources and partner solutions, standardizes them into open OSF formats and stores them in the S3 S3 buckets in your account. There is basically no development work involved — just to activate the service and point to the data source.
Option A: Lake Formation combined with Blue Data reptile is a generic data lake construction tool: Format standardization and integration of security data sources must be built manually.
Option B: A custom function exports data to CSV means that code, mode, and continuous maintenance are required - maximum development effort.
Option D: DMS Migration Database data, not designed to collect security incidents.

question_text:
A company is migrating five on-premises applications to VPCs in the AWS Cloud. Each application is currently deployed in isolated virtual networks on premises and should be deployed similarly in the AWS Cloud. The applications need to reach a shared services VPC. All the applications must be able to communicate with each other.
If the migration is successful, the company will repeat the migration process for more than 100 applications.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?
explanation_en:
There are now five applications, which will eventually exceed 100, all of which will require access to a shared VPC and connectivity, as well as management operations as few as possible. The transfer gateway serves as the central node: a new VPC can be attached by a single connection and is immediately connected to all other VPCs via the gateway chart. The increase in the number of objects is linear rather than secondary.
Option A: The use of software VPN tunnels on their own equipment means the need for licences, maintenance, bandwidth limitations and multiple failure points.
Option B: The peer connection between VPCs is not transmissible: For 100 VPCs to be visible, you need thousands of connections and edit each route chart.
Option C: Directly connects the company's own site to AWS instead of connecting VPC to each other: it does not apply to this task.

question_text:
A company wants to use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to run its on-premises application in a hybrid environment. The application currently runs on containers on premises.
The company needs a single container solution that can scale in an on-premises, hybrid, or cloud environment. The company must run new application containers in the AWS Cloud and must use a load balancer for HTTP traffic.
Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
A container platform is needed to support both the cloud and the local environment. ECS can cover both situations: cloud-end packagings use the Fargate start-up type, and containers in the local environment are registered through Amazon ECS Anywhere in conjunction with external start-up type (A). An application load balancer is located in front of the cloud service and is used to handle HTTP traffic (B).
Option C: The network load balancer works on the 4th floor, while the scene explicitly refers to HTTP traffic, which requires a layer function.
Option D: Fargate is the AWS computing resource: you cannot deploy containers to Fargate in the company's own data centre.
Option E: ECS Anywhere Starts the type of work externally, not Fargate: The combination described in the title does not exist.

question_text:
A company is migrating its workloads to AWS. The company has sensitive and critical data in on-premises relational databases that run on SQL Server instances.
The company wants to use the AWS Cloud to increase security and reduce operational overhead for the databases.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
There are two requirements: to improve security and to reduce the maintenance costs of the database. The example of a multi-usable area of hosting Amazon RDS for SQL Server will hand over patches, backups and failovers to you (the multi-usable area will maintain a simultaneous backup copy in another available area), and KMS key encryption will be enabled during static storage, overwhelming disks, snapshots and backups. Running SQL Server on EC2 on your own, although it can also achieve static storage encryption, all operations still need to be done by yourself. A related issue is Question 529.
Option A: Running SQL Server on EC2 still means you need to handle patches, backups and your own fault tolerance. The cost of transportation will not be reduced.
Option C: S3 plus Macie is the object storage plus data classification. There is no place to run relationship service queries.
Option D: DynamoDB is a non-relative database with different data models: Moving SQL Server there means rewrite the application. Cloudwatch Logs just collect logs and don't protect data.

options.text: Migrate the databases to Amazon EC2 instances. Use an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for encryption.

question_text:
A company wants to migrate an application to AWS. The company wants to increase the application's current availability. The company wants to use AWS WAF in the application's architecture.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
There are two requirements, each of which is met by its own separate components. Through an automatic extension group that crosses two available areas and is deployed after the application of the load balancer, availability can be enhanced: a single available area or case failure does not cause the application to be interrupted. AWS WAF is specifically attached to the load balancer - this is the type of resource it supports; Web ACL cannot be attached to an automatic extension or placement group. This makes this option the only one that correctly meets two conditions.
Option B: A cluster placement group gathers examples closely within a single available area to achieve a low delay - this actually reduces usability, and WAF cannot be attached to the placement group.
Option C: Two fixed examples provide faulty faults across available areas, but do not have either extension or automatic replacement: availability increases less than automatic extension groups.
Option D: An error occurs at the last step: Web ACL cannot be linked to the auto-extension group - it can only be attached to the load equalizer.

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group that contains multiple Amazon EC2 instances that host the application across two Availability Zones. Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and set the Auto Scaling group as the target. Connect a WAF to the ALB.

question_text:
A company manages a data lake in an Amazon S3 bucket that numerous applications access. The S3 bucket contains a unique prefix for each application. The company wants to restrict each application to its specific prefix and to have granular control of the objects under each prefix.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
Original answer: B; source correction answer: A.
ACL is non-extensible through batch operation settings and is contrary to AWS recommendations; providing fine particle control at prefix level is the function of the S3 access point co-ordinated policy
Creates a S3 access point with each other by applying to limit prefixes and object privileges while sharing a data lake bucket; changes the ACL volume by object and complex permission models. Source B to A.
There are many applications, each of which has its own prefixes and requires fine particle size control. This is exactly what S3 access points were designed for (A): each application has its own entry point and its own strategy, and the barrel strategy does not expand into a form that is difficult to read.
Option B: Set ACL to each object unextended through batch processing, needs to run again for new objects, and ACL itself is now defaulted and AWS is not recommended.
Option C: Copying each application to a separate S3 bucket doubles the amount and cost of storage and still does not provide fine particle control in the prefix.
Option D: Same unnecessary data copy: Access points do not need to split objects into multiple S3 buckets - they work on individual drums.

options.text: Create dedicated S3 access points and access point policies for each application.

question_text:

The processing for each image takes 2 minutes and requires 512 MB of memory.
A solutions architect needs to change the application to process the images when the images are uploaded.
Which change will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
Processing takes two minutes and requires 512 MB memory - suitable for the Lambda function. The S3 notification places the message in a SQS queue, which reads the message and processes the image as soon as it is uploaded. You only pay for the actual two minutes of each document, and the sample fleet will disappear completely.
Option B: A reserved example is billed 24 hours a day, even if work is only occasional.
Option C: An example of an ECS cluster is continuously running and billing, and SNS without queues cannot provide a reliable buffer.
Option D: An Elastic Beanstalk application again means an example of continuous operation and its full cost and maintenance.

question_text:
A company wants to improve the availability and performance of its hybrid application. The application consists of a stateful TCP-based workload hosted on Amazon EC2 instances in different AWS Regions and a stateless UDP-based workload hosted on premises.
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to improve availability and performance? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
The problem is that there are two loads, none of which are HTTP. The network load balancer in each region serves both the EC2 instance of TCP and the local UDP task load - the latter is achieved through target groups registered by IP addresses and can be accessed through VPN or DirectConect(D). The global accelerator is located on it: it provides static random transmission addresses, enters at the nearest edge, transmits via the AWS core network path, and achieves rapid failure switch (A) in the event of a failure of an area. TCP connectivity is maintained because the accelerator always selects the same target.
Option B: CloudFront only supports HTTP and caches; it neither serves a current TCP task load nor a UDP task load.
Option C: Apply a load balancer to understand only HTTP and HTTPS, so it does not match any of the tasks described.
Option E: An error occurred in the second half: the local UDP workload cannot be served by applying the load balancer (ALB) - it does not support the agreement.

options.text: Create an accelerator using AWS Global Accelerator. Add the load balancers as endpoints.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin that uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to route requests to the load balancers.

question_text:
A company runs a self-managed Microsoft SQL Server on Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS). Daily snapshots are taken of the EBS volumes.
Recently, all the company’s EBS snapshots were accidentally deleted while running a snapshot cleaning script that deletes all expired EBS snapshots. A solutions architect needs to update the architecture to prevent data loss without retaining EBS snapshots indefinitely.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
explanation_en:
The snapshot was deleted by a script with legal permission, and therefore the rejection of tactics and programmes to replicate to another area is a bad fix: the script will also remove copies and the rejection strategy will disrupt the routine clean-up process. This is precisely why a wastebin for EBS snapshots exists: the retention rules would intercept deletion operations and retain the snapshot for a certain period of time (in this case, seven days), after which the dispatch notes would automatically disappear. Recovery requires only one console operation, without any development work.
Option A: A refusal to remove the operation would undermine the normal clean-up process for expired snapshots required by the company and would not prevent deletions by other subjects.
Option B: If the same script is running in another area, copying to another area will not help and will increase storage costs twice.
Option D: EBS snapshots cannot simply `copy to S3' as documents: they are the object of service management. Export requires additional development work.

options.text: Change the IAM policy of the user to deny EBS snapshot deletion.
Copy the EBS snapshots to another AWS Region after completing the snapshots daily.
Create a 7-day EBS snapshot retention rule in Recycle Bin and apply the rule for all snapshots.
Copy EBS snapshots to Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).

question_text:
A company wants to use an AWS CloudFormation stack for its application in a test environment. The company stores the CloudFormation template in an Amazon S3 bucket that blocks public access. The company wants to grant CloudFormation access to the template in the S3 bucket based on specific user requests to create the test environment. The solution must follow security best practices.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
S3 buckets are closed to public access and only one visit to the template is required at the request of a specific user. The pre-signed URL provides a temporary link with a limited validity, with the permission of the signer: ClaudFormation reads the template through this link without any changes to the drum settings.

Option B: The deployment of API Gateway in front of the S3 bucket is an additional layer that needs to be constructed and reinforced, and the built-in pre-signed URL has solved the problem.
Option D: The temporary opening of public access violates security requirements: the template is visible to all during this period.

question_text:
A company has applications that run in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company outsources operational support of the applications. The company needs to provide access for the external support engineers without compromising security.
The external support engineers need access to the AWS Management Console. The external support engineers also need operating system access to the company’s fleet ofAmazon EC2 instances that run Amazon Linux in private subnets.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST securely?
explanation_en:
External engineers need to have access to both the control desk and the operating system level and to be as safe as possible for example in the private subsystem. Access to the console is achieved through IAM Infrastructure Center: temporary vouchers are used to log in through the enterprise identity provider and IAM users are not required to be distributed between accounts. Operating system access is achieved through Ssession Manager: deployment of proxy programs in instances where role is assigned, no open ports, no SSH keys, no springboards - and every session is logged and restricted by the IAM strategy.
Option B: The use of local IAM users in each account means that outsiders will obtain long-term vouchers and require manual maintenance. Session Manager is the right choice here, but the console access is not granted in the same way.
Option C: Open SSH with an IP address is the weakest option: the key cannot be set aside centrally and the IP address list needs manual maintenance.
Option D: Jumper opportunities add an additional server to an open port, which also requires the distribution of keys and local IAM users to outside engineers.

options.text: Confirm that AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is installed on all instances. Assign an instance profile with the necessary policy to connect to Systems Manager. Use AWS IAM Identity Center to provide the external support engineers console access. Use Systems Manager Session Manager to assign the required permissions.

Confirm that AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) is installed on all instances. Assign an instance profile with the necessary policy to connect to Systems Manager. Use Systems Manager Session Manager to provide local IAM user credentials in each AWS account to the external support engineers for console access.

question_text:
A company uses Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL to run its applications in the us-east-1 Region. The company also uses machine learning (ML) models to forecast annual revenue based on near real-time reports. The reports are generated by using the same RDS for PostgreSQL database. The database performance slows during business hours. The company needs to improve database performance.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The report and the workload share the same example, and therefore performance decreases during peak periods of operations. Read copies in the same area can unload the report load from the main database, which is the cheapest of all options: there is no cross-regional data transfer cost, and you simply pay for the copy example itself.
Option A: Cross-regional copy resolves the same problem, but increases the cost of trans-regional data transfer and has no practical benefit because the report is generated at the same location.
Option B: A backup example in Multi-AZ settings is not readable: the report cannot be directed to it.
Option C: Logical replication through DMS requires a copy of an example and a target database, combined with ongoing maintenance work - more expensive and complex than standard reading copies.

options.text: Create a cross-Region read replica. Configure the reports to be generated from the read replica.
Activate Multi-AZ DB instance deployment for RDS for PostgreSQL. Configure the reports to be generated from the standby database.
Use AWS Data Migration Service (AWS DMS) to logically replicate data to a new database. Configure the reports to be generated from the new database.
Create a read replica in us-east-1. Configure the reports to be generated from the read replica.

question_text:
A company hosts its multi-tier, public web application in the AWS Cloud. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances, and its database runs on Amazon RDS. The company is anticipating a large increase in sales during an upcoming holiday weekend. A solutions architect needs to build a solution to analyze the performance of the web application with a granularity of no more than 2 minutes.
What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?
explanation_en:
The amount of time required shall not be less than two minutes. Basic EC2 monitoring issues indicators every five minutes, while detailed monitoring issues every minute. It is only necessary to open detailed monitoring of examples and use standard Cloudwatch indicators.
Option A: Using a red migration log and dashboard means analysing text records rather than performance indicators, and cannot increase the particle size.
Option C: Use a function to access the log does not convert them to indicators or change the frequency of publication of the log.
Option D: A conduit consisting of S3, Redshift and QuickSight adds a heavy layer to the log, and the required indicator frequency is only one setting.

options.text: Send Amazon CloudWatch logs to Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon QuickS ght to perform further analysis.
Enable detailed monitoring on all EC2 instances. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to perform further analysis.
Create an AWS Lambda function to fetch EC2 logs from Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use Amazon CloudWatch metrics to perform further analysis.
Send EC2 logs to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Redshift to fetch logs from the S3 bucket to process raw data for further analysis with Amazon QuickSight.

question_text:
A company runs an application that stores and shares photos. Users upload the photos to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Every day, users upload approximately 150 photos. The company wants to design a solution that creates a thumbnail of each new photo and stores the thumbnail in a second S3 bucket.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The frequency of processing 150 photos per day is rare and only brief. When a photograph is uploaded, the S3 storage barrel notification immediately triggers a Lambda function: you only have to pay for the 150 calls, there is no continuous infrastructure, and thumbnails immediately appear.
Option A: The cost of a running EMR cluster, which works for only a few seconds a day, is extremely unreasonable.
Option B: An example that is always online rotates every minute, is also billed on a full-time basis and increases maintenance costs.
Option D: S3 Storage Lens is an analytical tool to store the usage - it cannot call a function when the event triggers.

options.text: Configure an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke a script every minute on a long-running Amazon EMR cluster. Configure the script to generate thumbnails for the photos that do not have thumbnails. Configure the script to upload the thumbnails to the second S3 bucket.

Configure an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke a script every minute on a memory-optimized Amazon EC2 instance that is always on. Configure the script to generate thumbnails for the photos that do not have thumbnails. Configure the script to upload the thumbnails to the second S3 bucket.

Configure an S3 event notification to invoke an AWS Lambda function each time a user uploads a new photo to the application. Configure the Lambda function to generate a thumbnail and to upload the thumbnail to the second S3 bucket.

Configure S3 Storage Lens to invoke an AWS Lambda function each time a user uploads a new photo to the application. Configure the Lambda function to generate a thumbnail and to upload the thumbnail to a second S3 bucket.

question_text:
A company has stored millions of objects across multiple prefixes in an Amazon S3 bucket by using the Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class. The company needs to delete all data older than 3 years except for a subset of data that must be retained. The company has identified the data that must be retained and wants to implement a serverless solution.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
There are millions of objects that are in deep archiving storage and solutions need to be server-free. The S3 dashboard report lists objects and their dates, a Lambda function filters objects that need to be deleted while complying with the retention list, while the S3 batch operation applies the operation on a large scale - without any server involvement - on millions of objects.
Option A: Scripts on the EC2 instance are both a server and require manual maintenance - not a server-free solution.
Option B: AWS Watch operates in a computing environment that you need to define and pay for; the bulk operation mechanism for an object is more appropriate.
Option C: Glue data crawler is used to build an analytical directory, not to generate a list of objects that need to be deleted, and it does not execute deletions.

options.text: Use S3 Inventory to list all objects. Use the AWS CLI to create a script that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance that deletes objects from the inventory list.
Use AWS Batch to delete objects older than 3 years except for the data that must be retained.
Provision an AWS Glue crawler to query objects older than 3 years. Save the manifest file of old objects. Create a script to delete objects in the manifest.
Enable S3 Inventory. Create an AWS Lambda function to filter and delete objects. Invoke the Lambda function with S3 Batch Operations to delete objects by using the inventory reports.

question_text:
A company is building an application on AWS. The application uses multiple AWS Lambda functions to retrieve sensitive data from a single Amazon S3 bucket for processing. The company must ensure that only authorized Lambda functions can access the data. The solution must comply with the principle of least privilege.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The principle of minimal authority in AWS services is achieved through independent roles: each Lambda function has its own executive role, and its strategy allows only for operations that are actually required for the prefixing of the relevant S3 buckets. In this way, the leaking of a function or a loophole does not lead to access privileges for other functions and allows for a function-by-function adjustment of privileges. The drums can also be further limited by strategy, listing only those roles.
Option A: A shared role with full barrel access is completely opposite to the minimum access principle: each function receives all privileges.
Option B: Link access to the IP address of the endpoint is fragile and does not recognize a specific function: any resource on the same network will receive the same permission.
Option D: The ARN of the function is not the subject of the storage barrel policy: authorization is assessed on the basis of the role assumed when the function calls API.

options.text: Grant full S3 bucket access to all Lambda functions through a shared IAM role.
Configure the Lambda functions to run within a VPC. Configure a bucket policy to grant access based on the Lambda functions' VPC endpoint IP addresses.
Create individual IAM roles for each Lambda function. Grant the IAM roles access to the S3 bucket. Assign each IAM role as the Lambda execution role for its corresponding Lambda function.
Configure a bucket policy granting access to the Lambda functions based on their function ARNs.

question_text:
A company has developed a non-production application that is composed of multiple microservices for each of the company's business units. A single development team maintains all the microservices.
The current architecture uses a static web frontend and a Java-based backend that contains the application logic.
The architecture also uses a MySQL database that the company hosts on an Amazon EC2 instance.
The company needs to ensure that the application is secure and available globally.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
Each layer is replaced by a hosting service. The static front end becomes the S3 S3 bucket behind CloudFront, providing global coverage and HTTPS. Microservices become the Lambda function, which is located behind API Gateway, with authorized, restricted and extended functions embedded in API Gateway. The database becomes Amazon RDS for MySQL, not a self-managed example. There's hardly a single place that needs manual operation.
Option A: A database that is deployed on preset EC2 cases will still need to be maintained by the company itself: patches, backups, error tolerances — all of which will require manual operation.
Option C: The Lambda function cannot be registered as the goal of Network Load Balancer: this goal type only supports Application Load Balancer.
Option D: There is no global distribution without CloudFront, and the database is once again on the EC2 instance, assuming the full operational burden.

options.text: Use Amazon CloudFront and AWS Amplify to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that the microservices access by using Amazon API Gateway. Migrate the MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance.

Use Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3 to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that the microservices access by using Amazon API Gateway. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL.

Use Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3 to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that are in a target group behind a Network Load Balancer. Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon RDS for MySQL.

Use Amazon S3 to host the static web frontend. Refactor the microservices to use AWS Lambda functions that are in a target group behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the MySQL database to an Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance.

question_text:
A video game company is deploying a new gaming application to its global users. The company requires a solution that will provide near real-time reviews and rankings of the players.
A solutions architect must design a solution to provide fast access to the data. The solution must also ensure the data persists on disks in the event that the company restarts the application.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
Close real-time access to rankings is required, while data will still need to be stored on disks after the application has been restarted. ElastiCache for Redis meets these two needs: it provides persistence (RDB and AOF) based on memory and delayed below milliseconds, supports copying and orderly assembly - in fact, is specifically designed for rankings. As a hosting service, its operating costs are extremely low.
Option A: S3 and CloudFront are built for static files and caches and do not apply to near real-time updates of counters.
Option B: Using self-managed EC2 instances and manually synchronizing data in multiple regions is the largest operating load option and the least reliable.
Option D: Memcached neither sustains data to disk nor duplicates data: the ranking after application restarts will be lost, and this requires an explicit prohibition.

options.text: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin. Store the player data in the S3 bucket.
Create Amazon EC2 instances in multiple AWS Regions. Store the player data on the EC2 instances. Configure Amazon Route 53 with geolocation records to direct users to the closest EC2 instance.
Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis duster. Store the player data in the ElastiCache cluster.
Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached duster. Store the player data in the ElastiCache cluster.

question_text:
A company is designing an application on AWS that processes sensitive data. The application stores and processes financial data for multiple customers.
To meet compliance requirements, the data for each customer must be encrypted separately at rest by using a secure, centralized key management solution. The company wants to use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to implement encryption.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
explanation_en:
The requirement that "each client's data must be encrypted" means that each client has an independent key -- so that even if one key is leaked or removed, it does not affect the other clients, and deleting a client's data from the encryption perspective is equivalent to deleting the client's key. "Safe and centralized key management" points to KMS, and "minimal operating expenses" means no self-defined components need to be deployed. Comply: each client has a KMS key with a key strategy to limit interviews and to use CloudTrail to record the use of the key.
Option A: Store an encryption key in a S3 barrel is a reverse mode: the key and data are stored close to the neighbor, protected only by interview permission, not by a hard module. There is no centralized management and there is no journal recording of behaviour with the key.
Option B: Self-defined hard module in the cloud is the highest operational cost: clusters must be deployed, maintained and redundant. ClaudHSM was designed for this, but needs to be focused on minimum operating costs.
Option C: A single key per client is a violation of core needs: data from different clients are ultimately protected by the same confidentiality and cannot be removed from a client's access rights only.

options.text: Generate a unique encryption key for each customer. Store the keys in an Amazon S3 bucket. Enable server- side encryption.

Deploy a hardware security appliance in the AWS environment that securely stores customer-provided encryption keys. Integrate the security appliance with AWS KMS to encrypt the sensitive data in the application.
Create a single AWS KMS key to encrypt all sensitive data across the application.
Create separate AWS KMS keys for each customer's data that have granular access control and logging enabled.

question_text:
A company needs to design a resilient web application to process customer orders. The web application must automatically handle increases in web traffic and application usage without affecting the customer experience or losing customer orders.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Each requirement is met once: the network traffic is received and distributed using a load balancer, the processing capacity is expanded when the load increases, the SQS queue saves unprocessed orders to ensure that orders are not lost during the surge, and the RDS database, configured in the multi-usable area, can continue to operate in case of failure in the available area.
Option A: The NAT gateway does not connect to the flow of revenue stations and "store unprocessed orders in a function" neither provides a buffer nor a guarantee of persistence.
Option B: The placement of a network load balancer in front of the application load balancer is redundant, while Redshift is an analytical data repository that is not designed to receive orders.
Option C: Gateway load balancers pass traffic through network devices and cannot store orders.

options.text: Use a NAT gateway to manage web traffic. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups to receive, process, and store processed customer orders. Use an AWS Lambda function to capture and store unprocessed orders.

Use a Network Load Balancer (NLB) to manage web traffic. Use an Application Load Balancer to receive customer orders from the NLUse Amazon Redshift with a Multi-AZ deployment to store unprocessed and processed customer orders.

Use a Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) to manage web traffic. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to receive and process customer orders. Use the GWLB to capture and store unprocessed orders. Use Amazon DynamoDB to store processed customer orders.

Use an Application Load Balancer to manage web traffic. Use Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups to receive and process customer orders. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to store unprocessed orders. Use Amazon RDS with a Multi-AZ deployment to store processed customer orders.

question_text:
A company is using AWS DataSync to migrate millions of files from an on-premises system to AWS. The files are 10 KB in size on average.
The company wants to use Amazon S3 for file storage. For the first year after the migration, the files will be accessed once or twice and must be immediately available. After 1 year, the files must be archived for at least 7 years.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The key detail is the size of the document: in millions of documents, the average is 10 KB. The minimum chargeable object for IA and Glacier Industrial Retrieval is 128 KB, while the archive class also has metadata for each object, so that small files in the archive ultimately consume costs well above their actual size. Therefore, the first step is to package documents into larger objects before moving. Thereafter, according to the pattern of visits: occasional, but immediate, visits within a year are appropriate for the use of Glacier Instant Retrieval, and seven years of pure archiving requirements are suitable for the use of Glacier Deep Archive.
Option B: Packing steps are correct, but the cost of the selected storage category is higher than necessary: in the case of one or two visits per year, the price of Standard-IA is higher than the price of Glacier Instant Retrieval, and seven years of archiving is stored in Glacier Instant Retrieval instead of Deep Archive, approximately four times the excess payment.
Option C: Documents are not grouped, so millions of KB objects are subject to the minimum KB subtotal fee of 128 KB. In addition, the seven-year cost of Glacier Flexible Retriev was higher than Deep Archive, and there was no need for urgent visits.
Option D: Once again, there is no grouping — also faced with overpayment of the smallest object size — and the cost of using Standard-IA in the first year is higher than that of Glacier Instant Retrieval, in the case of one or two visits per year.

options.text: Use an archive tool to group the files into large objects. Use DataSync to migrate the objects. Store the objects in S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval for the first year. Use a lifecycle configuration to transition the files to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.

Use an archive tool to group the files into large objects. Use DataSync to copy the objects to S3 Standard- Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use a lifecycle configuration to transition the files to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.

Configure the destination storage class for the files as S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval. Use a lifecycle policy to transition the files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.

Configure a DataSync task to transfer the files to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Use a lifecycle configuration to transition the files to S3 Deep Archive after 1 year with a retention period of 7 years.

question_text:
A company recently performed a lift and shift migration of its on-premises Oracle database workload to run on an Amazon EC2 memory optimized Linux instance. The EC2 Linux instance uses a 1 TB Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume with 64,000 IOPS.
The database storage performance after the migration is slower than the performance of the on-premises database.
Which solution will improve storage performance?
explanation_en:
The maximum IOPS limit for an io1 volume is 64,000 and the volume is fully distributed, so the number of operations on the volume cannot be further increased. The solution is to add an extra io1 volume and use LVM to group them together: the operation is spread over multiple volumes, and the total volume of throughput increases more or less as the volume of the volumes increases.
Option B:io1 Volume cannot set more than 64,000 IOPS: this is the hard limit for each volume.
Option C: Increase size to 2 TB does not increase the IOPS limit: O1 is independently distributed and has reached maximum value.
Option D: Storage optimized examples provide fast local disks, but EBS volumes remain unchanged, their limitations remain unchanged and database data cannot be stored on temporary storage.

options.text: Add more Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volumes. Use OS commands to create a Logical Volume Management (LVM) stripe.
Increase the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume to more than 64,000 IOPS.
Increase the size of the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume to 2 TB.
Change the EC2 Linux instance to a storage optimized instance type. Do not change the Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) EBS volume.

question_text:
A company is migrating from a monolithic architecture for a web application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 to a serverless microservices architecture. The company wants to use AWS services that support an event-driven, loosely coupled architecture. The company wants to use the publish/subscribe (pub/sub) pattern.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
A publication/subscription model is required, which means a SNS theme is required. The most economical front-end solution is HTTP API in API Gateway: it is about 70% less expensive to process the same request than RET API, and the additional RET functionality is not required here.
Option A: A SQS queue is a model for a consumer-by-consumer message rather than a publication/subscription model.
Option B: The design is correct, but REST API costs significantly more than HTTP API when it is functionally the same as this task.
Option C: A WebSocket API with an enhanced broadcast stream is the most expensive configuration and is over-designed for simply notifying the subscriber.

options.text: Configure an Amazon API Gateway REST API to invoke an AWS Lambda function that publishes events to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure one or more subscribers to read events from the SQS queue.

Configure an Amazon API Gateway REST API to invoke an AWS Lambda function that publishes events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure one or more subscribers to receive events from the SNS topic.
Configure an Amazon API Gateway WebSocket API to write to a data stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with enhanced fan-out. Configure one or more subscribers to receive events from the data stream.

Configure an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API to invoke an AWS Lambda function that publishes events to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure one or more subscribers to receive events from the topic.

question_text:
A company recently migrated a monolithic application to an Amazon EC2 instance and Amazon RDS. The application has tightly coupled modules. The existing design of the application gives the application the ability to run on only a single EC2 instance.
The company has noticed high CPU utilization on the EC2 instance during peak usage times. The high CPU utilization corresponds to degraded performance on Amazon RDS for read requests. The company wants to reduce the high CPU utilization and improve read request performance.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The application is a mono-structure, operating only on a single case, and therefore horizontal expansion cannot be achieved: the only option is to increase the specification of the case and fix the auto-extend group on a machine to achieve automatic recovery. Delays in accessing the database are addressed by adding read-only copies and redirecting reading traffic.
Option B: Writing cannot point to a copy: read-only copies are read-only.
Option C: The largest group size is two that conflict with the application ' s own limitations, and an increase in the database example specification does not separate reading and writing operations.
Option D: An increase in the specifications of the database example would increase the overall resource ceiling, but reading operations would still compete with the same resources as writing operations.

options.text: Resize the EC2 instance to an EC2 instance type that has more CPU capacity. Configure an Auto Scaling group with a minimum and maximum size of 1. Configure an RDS read replica for read requests.

Resize the EC2 instance to an EC2 instance type that has more CPU capacity. Configure an Auto Scaling group with a minimum and maximum size of 1. Add an RDS read replica and redirect all read/write traffic to the replica.
Configure an Auto Scaling group with a minimum size of 1 and maximum size of 2. Resize the RDS DB instance to an instance type that has more CPU capacity.

Resize the EC2 instance to an EC2 instance type that has more CPU capacity. Configure an Auto Scaling group with a minimum and maximum size of 1. Resize the RDS DB instance to an instance type that has more CPU capacity.

question_text:
A company needs to grant a team of developers access to the company's AWS resources. The company must maintain a high level of security for the resources.
The company requires an access control solution that will prevent unauthorized access to the sensitive data.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The correct access model in AWS is based on the role of fine-particle permission: developers log in through federal identity or Identity Center, assuming a role, and obtaining a temporary certificate that meets their mission needs. No long-term key will be created, access rights will be revoked by changing the role assignment and can be traced back to a specific individual in CloudTrail. That is exactly what the right option describes.
Option A: Sharing vouchers makes it impossible to determine who performed what, and a person who leaves office requires the password to be reset for all. This is a clear violation of security practice.
Option C: Access keys are long-standing keys that must be stored and rotated. For personnel, the standard path is a temporary character certificate.
Option D: Cognito is designed for application end users, not for staff access to AWS resources.

options.text: Share the IAM user credentials for each development team member with the rest of the team to simplify access management and to streamline development workflows.
Define IAM roles that have fine-grained permissions based on the principle of least privilege. Assign an IAM role to each developer.
Create IAM access keys to grant programmatic access to AWS resources. Allow only developers to interact with AWS resources through API calls by using the access keys.
Create an AWS Cognito user pool. Grant developers access to AWS resources by using the user pool.

question_text:
A company hosts a monolithic web application on an Amazon EC2 instance. Application users have recently reported poor performance at specific times. Analysis of Amazon CloudWatch metrics shows that CPU utilization is 100% during the periods of poor performance.
The company wants to resolve this performance issue and improve application availability.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)
explanation_en:
In one example, CPU usage was fixed at 100 percentage points, which required horizontal expansion and increased availability. Captures an AMI from an active server and quotes it to a new starter template (B), then creates an automatic extension group (E) with an application load equalizer, which adds examples (E) to the load. The application itself was not rewritten.
Option A: An example of vertical expansion does not provide usability: a single machine is still a single point failure.
Option C: Automatic expansion groups with load balancers are horizontal rather than vertical expansions - the description corresponds to a non-existent pattern.
Option D: Compute Optimizer recommends the type of example, which facilitates vertical expansion; it does not solve the problem of horizontal growth.

options.text: Use AWS Compute Optimizer to obtain a recommendation for an instance type to scale vertically.
Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) from the web server. Reference the AMI in a new launch template.
Create an Auto Scaling group and an Application Load Balancer to scale vertically.
Use AWS Compute Optimizer to obtain a recommendation for an instance type to scale horizontally.
Create an Auto Scaling group and an Application Load Balancer to scale horizontally.

question_text:
A company runs all its business applications in the AWS Cloud. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts.
A solutions architect needs to review all permissions that are granted to IAM users to determine which IAM users have more permissions than required.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?
explanation_en:
IAM Access Analyzer helps to detect excessive privileges: in addition to identifying resources with external access, it analyses the historical history of CloudTrail ' s activities, and is based on operational production strategies that are actually used, and the unused access that it discovers exposes unused privileges, roles and keys. This is a hosting service operated at the organizational level through the commissioning of an administrator, and therefore there is no need for manual access to the accounts.
Option A: Network Access Analyzer analysis of resources, not IAM privileges.
Option B: Setting up a alarm for resource creation does not answer the question who has more than the required permissions and requires a manual review of each event.
Option D: Amazon Inspector detects a loophole in the load. It does not analyse IAM strategies.

options.text: Use Network Access Analyzer to review all access permissions in the company's AWS accounts.
Create an AWS CloudWatch alarm that activates when an IAM user creates or modifies resources in an AWS account.
Use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Access Analyzer to review all the company’s resources and accounts.
Use Amazon Inspector to find vulnerabilities in existing IAM policies.

question_text:
A company needs to implement a new data retention policy for regulatory compliance. As part of this policy, sensitive documents that are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket must be protected from deletion or modification for a fixed period of time.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
Regulatory requirements that "no deletion or modification is allowed for a fixed period and cannot be bypassed by anyone" mean a pattern that cannot be broken. The S3 object is locked in compliance mode and it is prohibited to delete or overwhelm the object version before the end of the retention period, and neither the administrator nor the root user can shorten or remove the retention period - only waiting for its expiry. The mode of governance is different: it prevents accidental operations, but any user with S3: BypassGovernanceRetension privileges can routinely bypass that limitation. Compared to Question 446 the latter adds a requirement for protection also for those who already exist.
Option A: The governance model can be removed by users with bypass privileges. This is not sufficient to meet regulatory requirements.
Option C: Version control makes deletion reversible, but does not prohibit deletion, while a life-cycle rule that removes objects after the set time does not actually have any protective effect - it simply executes deletion.
Option D: Turning to Glacier changes the cost and speed of access. Object can be deleted or overwhelmed after.

options.text: Activate S3 Object Lock on the required objects and enable governance mode.
Activate S3 Object Lock on the required objects and enable compliance mode.
Enable versioning on the S3 bucket. Set a lifecycle policy to delete the objects after a specified period.
Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval for the retention duration.

question_text:
A company runs its customer-facing web application on containers. The workload uses Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate. The web application is resource intensive.
The web application needs to be available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week for customers. The company expects the application to experience short bursts of high traffic. The workload must be highly available.
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?
explanation_en:
The application operates 24 hours a day, but the load consists of a stable baseline plus short peaks. The ECS Capacity Provider allows you to mix: a stable baseline part is running on the standard Fargate to ensure availability, while the peak part is covered by the Fargate pre-set example, with a discount of up to 70%. Only interrupts the preset instance task to affect the additional peak part of the load.
Option A: Resize the task correctly, although useful, but does not save the cost of the peak part and requires manual load testing.
Option C: There is a risk that the stabilization baseline will be retained on the reserved capacity: its recovery will affect the availability of the baseline and requires continuous running.
Option D: Compute Optimizer helps to optimize the task, but does not provide a hybrid capacity model or save the cost of the peak component.

options.text: Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate. Conduct load testing by using a third-party tool. Rightsize the Fargate tasks in Amazon CloudWatch.
Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate for steady state and Fargate Spot for burst traffic.
Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate Spot for steady state and Fargate for burst traffic.
Configure an ECS capacity provider with Fargate. Use AWS Compute Optimizer to rightsize the Fargate task.

question_text:
A company is building an application in the AWS Cloud. The application is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company uses Amazon Route 53 for the DNS.
The company needs a managed solution with proactive engagement to detect against DDoS attacks.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
The key phrase is "management solutions with active participation". Active participation from AWS Shield Reponse Team is available only when you have a Shield Advanced subscription: it monitors protected resources and contacts you on its own initiative when an attack is detected. Load balancers and Route 53 hosting areas will be added to subscriptions to cover applications and DNS. Shield Standard will run automatically, but will not provide active support.
Option A: AWS Config does not have a management rule to detect DDoS attack: Config to evaluate resource allocation.
Option B: WAF can guard against a layered attack, but cannot resist a traffic-type attack or provide active participation from the AWS team.
Option C: GuardDuty analyzes logs and generates discovery results, but does not provide automatic DDoS protection or active support.

options.text: Enable AWS Config. Configure an AWS Config managed rule that detects DDoS attacks.
Enable AWS WAF on the ALCreate an AWS WAF web ACL with rules to detect and prevent DDoS attacks. Associate the web ACL with the ALB.
Store the ALB access logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to detect and take automated preventative actions for DDoS attacks.
Subscribe to AWS Shield Advanced. Configure hosted zones in Route 53. Add ALB resources as protected resources.

question_text:
A company hosts a video streaming web application in a VPC. The company uses a Network Load Balancer (NLB) to handle TCP traffic for real-time data processing. There have been unauthorized attempts to access the application.
The company wants to improve application security with minimal architectural change to prevent unauthorized attempts to access the application.
Which solution will meet these requirements?
explanation_en:
TCP traffic is handled by the Network Load Balancer and WAF cannot be attached to it - therefore filtering must be done on the network level. Since 2023, NLBs have supported security groups, but they can only be distributed when a load equalizer is created: it is not possible to add a security group to the existing NLB. The answer is therefore - recreate the load balancer and configure a security group that only allows a trusted address. This is the least possible structural change.
Option A: AWS WAF does not support network load balancers: it only applies to HTTP resources such as CloudFront, ALB and API Gateway.
Option C: Adding a second load equalizer next to the first load equalizer does not prevent anyone from accessing the old load equalizer and doubles costs rather than solves the problem.
Option D: Shield Advanced can resist a serviceable assault, but it cannot restrict access through an address or prevent unauthorized connection attempts.

options.text: Implement a series of AWS WAF rules directly on the NLB to filter out unauthorized traffic.
Recreate the NLB with a security group to allow only trusted IP addresses.
Deploy a second NLB in parallel with the existing NLB configured with a strict IP address allow list.
Use AWS Shield Advanced to provide enhanced DDoS protection and prevent unauthorized access attempts.

question_text:
A healthcare company is developing an AWS Lambda function that publishes notifications to an encrypted Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. The notifications contain protected health information (PHI).
The SNS topic uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys for encryption. The company must ensure that the application has the necessary permissions to publish messages securely to the SNS topic.
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose three.)
explanation_en:
Three permissions are required for a function to publish the message to an encrypted theme, and all three are listed in the answer. First, the SNS theme ' s own resource policy allows for the role of the function to be published (A). Second, the KMS key strategy allows the same role to perform key operations - for distribution, requires kms: GeneralDataKey and kms:Decrypt(C). Third, the performance role of the function has the corresponding authority (F) in its own IAM policy. The general rule underlying this topic is that access to KMS keys requires inspection in two respects — key and main strategy — while access to the subject is examined on the basis of its own strategy.
Option B: Switch to AWS-managed keys that conflict with scenes (the company uses a customer-managed key) and fail to resolve the issue of privileges: without proper authorization, the release will still fail.
Option D: The subject of the resource policy is a role (or an account) rather than an ARN for the Lambda function. The name of the function ARN as the subject is invalid.
Option E: The placement of API Gateway in front of the SNS theme is an unnecessary level that neither gives function release rights nor gives KMS key privileges.

options.text: Create a resource policy for the SNS topic that allows the Lambda function to publish messages to the topic.
Use server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for the SNS topic instead of customer managed keys.
Create a resource policy for the encryption key that the SNS topic uses that has the necessary AWS KMS permissions.
Specify the Lambda function's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) in the SNS topic's resource policy.
Associate an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API with the SNS topic to control access to the topic by using API Gateway resource policies.
Configure a Lambda execution role that has the necessary IAM permissions to use a customer managed key in AWS KMS.

question_text:
A company has an employee web portal. Employees log in to the portal to view payroll details. The company is developing a new system to give employees the ability to upload scanned documents for reimbursement. The company runs a program to extract text-based data from the documents and attach the extracted information to each employee’s reimbursement IDs for processing.
The employee web portal requires 100% uptime. The document extract program runs infrequently throughout the day on an on-demand basis. The company wants to build a scalable and cost-effective new system that will require minimal changes to the existing web portal. The company does not want to make any code changes.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?
explanation_en:
Original answer: D; source correction answer: A.
The request imposes two constraints at the same time: "a minimum change to the existing portal" and "a company does not want any code change". Option D suggests moving the portal to a static hosting on S3 and re-energizing existing functions through API Gateway and Lambda, which are re-engineered by the application and are explicitly requested to ban. Option A maintains the portal as it is and is placed in an automatic extension group (which meets the required 100 per cent availability) and adds a Lambda function to the new, rarely running text extraction task, which is triggered when the document is uploaded and billed only on the actual running time.
Retain the original EC2 Web port, without rewriting the entire site as S3 + API Gateway + Lambda; occasional documents extracting a separate upload event triggers Lambda, with minimal modifications and as needed extensions. Source D changed to A; 100 per cent of dry uptime is in target wording, and any actual architecture still needs to be designed for failure recovery.
Here's the source practice material key has been corrected to A. The scene clearly limits the change: the portal is touched to a minimum and the code is never changed.
